Nanocellulose strengthens bamboo from within
abstract: An article in Advanced Materials reports bamboo veneers reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals that are strong, flexible and can be made at scale.

title: Harvesting thermal energy from sunlight with wood
abstract: An article in Advanced Functional Materials reports a wood–metal–organic framework thermoelectric that converts both heat and evaporation-driven water flow into electricity, inspired by the transport functions of natural trees.

title: Data centre materials need an end-of-life strategy as deployment accelerates
abstract: Data centres are fast-growing stocks of copper, steel and critical materials, yet what happens to these materials at end of life is understudied. The scale, timing and geography of retiring hardware make it an unusually recoverable resource, if corporate and governmental policy incentivizes action now.

title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
abstract: The economics of residential electrification in high-cost electricity regions remain uncertain. Using metered data from over 20,000 California homes, we assess the economic, environmental, and equity impacts of end-use electrification under rollout strategies based on household income and gas infrastructure age. Even under favorable electricity rates, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values (NPVs). Cost-effectiveness improves with deeper electrification scenarios, particularly when more costs are shifted to fixed charges and for homes with existing air conditioning—54–67% of these households break even when electrifying space heating, compared to fewer than 5% of those without. Income-based rebates more than double the share of low- and moderate-income households with positive NPVs. Prioritizing areas with aging gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions on par with high-income-led adoption and avoids costly pipeline replacement, but requires the highest subsidy to achieve cost-effectiveness across all households. These findings highlight trade-offs in designing equitable electrification strategies.

Radical detour in photocatalyst–enzyme pairs
abstract: Combining photoredox catalysts with enzymes can create reactivity unavailable to either catalyst class alone. Now, systematic screening of 180 such pairings uncovers a C(sp3)–C(sp3) radical cross-coupling that can be directed to either the β- or γ-position, enabling the synthesis of valuable non-canonical amino acids.

title: Transport without a tether
The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
abstract: The active transport and retention principle states that nanoparticles enter tumours via endothelial cells and exit via lymphatic drainage. How nanoparticles are retained in the tumour microenvironment remains unclear. Here we report a computational strategy to determine the mechanism of nanoparticle retention in solid tumours. We find that tumour cellular and acellular components delay and obstruct the movement of nanoparticles by influencing nanoparticle drag, Brownian and electric forces. We mathematically define nanoparticle retention based on these interactions, linking retention quantitatively to tumour pathophysiology, nanoparticle design and delivery efficiency. We create a software interface to simulate and predict nanoparticle retention across different tumour systems and nanoparticle designs, enabling us to select optimal tumour and nanoparticle delivery conditions for better therapeutic outcomes.

title: Nanoparticle transport and retention in tumours
abstract: Mathematical modelling and systematic studies in mouse tumour models uncover pathophysiological features and nanoparticle design criteria that promote tumour retention, providing cues and clues for improving the efficacy of cancer nanotherapy.

Concurrent atmospheric phenomena amplify precipitation extremes under anthropogenic climate change
abstract: Extreme precipitation events are increasing in many regions. Here the authors discuss how the increasing concurrence of atmospheric phenomena could contribute to these trends under anthropogenic warming.

title: Through the lens of fog
abstract: Hyomin Lee explores why a surface that repels large water droplets can still become covered with fog, and how scaling arguments suggest an unexpected solution.

title: CMOS surprises
abstract: Unexpected effects are still being discovered in complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits, and the results could have implications for the advance of quantum computing.

title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
abstract: Machine learning guides the design of an additively manufactured titanium alloy containing superfine features at the 10 nm scale through controlled martensitic transformation, which achieves an ultimate tensile strength of more than 1.7 GPa and 7.5% uniform elongation.

title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur-sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur-carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm-2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15-25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg-1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li-In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage.

title: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions
abstract: The contribution of glacial lakes to glacier mass loss is unclear. This work maps global glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020 to quantify changes in number, volume and area, showing that they explain 11 ± 7% of lake-terminating glacier loss, with climate forcing and glacier geometry the dominant factors.

title: Plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots for crop disease management
abstract: Plant fungal pathogens in crops can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security. To tackle wheat Fusarium head blight, a devastating disease infecting wheat crops, an effective antifungal strategy using plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots has been developed.

title: The person behind the scientist
abstract: Matteo Seita and Mengying Liu discuss their reflections as organizers of The Past Metallurgists Society lecture series, where scientists meet to share stories of distinguished metallurgists from the past.

title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes
abstract: Cobalt-free cathodes are vital for green energy but suffer from structural instability. Here the authors report a unique O6-type framework that stabilizes oxygen redox for exceptional cycling durability.

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract:
Abstract
                  Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.

title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
abstract: Antireflection coatings are widely used in optical systems to increase transmission and suppress unwanted reflections by matching the optical impedance across a uniform interface. Applying the same idea to metasurfaces is fundamentally more challenging because their wavefront control relies on arrays of geometrically distinct meta-atoms, presenting as a spatially varying optical impedance. Here we show that vertical integration can overcome this limitation by allowing bilayer meta-atoms to act simultaneously as phase shifters and impedance-matching stacks. By treating meta-atoms as multilayer thin films, we derive a design rule that links the effective refractive indices of two independently patterned layers and identifies antireflective bilayer libraries with full 0-2π transmission phase coverage. We demonstrate the approach with a free-standing TiO2/TiO2 metalens operating at 1,310 nm, which suppresses reflection below that of bare glass while maintaining diffraction-limited focusing. These results establish bilayer metasurfaces as a platform for jointly engineering optical impedance and wavefront response at the meta-atom level.

title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
abstract: Linking electrode microstructure to electrochemical performance is essential for optimizing Li-ion batteries. However, this requires mechanistic four-dimensional observations at the ultimate spatiotemporal scales, which remain elusive. Here we demonstrate the use of interrupted-operando synchrotron X-ray nano-holotomography combined with digital volume correlation to track chemomechanical dynamics at both particle (local) and electrode (averaged) scales. Quantitative scale-bridging image analysis is applied to composite graphite-silicon electrodes during their electrochemical formation cycle. Our findings reveal that local ionic diffusion properties, graphite particle morphology and position in the electrode, distance to silicon clusters, surface contact with the liquid electrolyte solution, and mechanical deformations all directly affect local electrochemical activity and irreversibility, although these parameters are not equally important. In particular, we identify fast ionic diffusion channels that play a key role and counterbalance intrinsic depth-dependent reaction heterogeneities arising from ionic and electronic diffusion limitations. The various structural factors that determine the electrochemical performance of composite graphite-silicon electrodes in Li-ion batteries beyond ensemble properties are classified using a scale of influence, providing a practical framework for the optimization of materials and electrode manufacturing.

title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
abstract: Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.

title: Tracking local chemomechanics in graphite–silicon composite electrodes
abstract: Operando 4D imaging reveals how local ionic pathways govern activity in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles.

title: Assessing public preferences for reforming water subsidy eligibility rules in Delhi
abstract: Sinha and co-authors survey 728 residents of Delhi about water subsidy design options to understand which eligibility rules people consider most acceptable and fair. Although the study finds support for subsidies when water use remains below a threshold as well as an income-based subsidy, preferences differ sharply across population groups, making reform politically and practically challenging.

title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
abstract:
Abstract
                  Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management.

title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li

                    −2
                    at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm
                    −2

                    at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries.

title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays.

title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis
abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

title: Designing solar panels for realistic end-of-life scenarios
abstract: The rapid growth of photovoltaics is generating vast waste streams, a portion of which flows to regions where recycling is unregulated. Solar panel design criteria do not account for these end-of-life realities, creating global asymmetry in environmental burdens. This Comment proposes research directions beyond material substitution to address these design gaps.

title: G:C:G:C-Flanked i-Motifs Are Thermodynamically Favored and Their Sequences Highly Enriched in the Human Genome
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract i-Motifs are biologically relevant noncanonical DNA structures whose stability is strongly influenced by capping interactions. Among these, minor groove tetrads (MGTs) are among the most powerful stabilizing elements identified to date, yet the molecular factors governing their effects and their potential biological significance remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic experimental and computational analysis of 16 MGT-stabilized i-motifs (MGTiMs), encompassing all combinations of terminal tetrad composition and orientation within a common sequence scaffold. NMR spectroscopy confirms that all sequences adopt closely related architectures, enabling direct comparison of the effects of tetrad identity and orientation on stability. Thermal denaturation experiments reveal that the stability hierarchy, previously observed in selected structures (G:C:G:C ≳ G:C:G:T ≫ G:T:G:T), is broadly maintained across the series, although substantial positional effects are observed. Molecular dynamics simulations and energy decomposition analyses suggest that differences in electrostatic interactions and local conformational flexibility contribute to these trends. Notably, genome-wide analysis of the human genome reveals a strong enrichment of sequences capable of forming the most stabilizing tetrads, with motifs containing two G:C:G:C tetrads reaching a 45-fold enrichment relative to random expectation. Interestingly, this most abundant genomic motif is also the only one that undergoes pronounced pH-driven conformational transitions, highlighting the unique structural plasticity of these architectures. Together, these findings reveal how tetrad composition and positional context govern MGTiM stability and identify NN-type motifs as a particularly enriched class of structurally distinctive genomic sequences.

title: Catalytic Enantiodivergent Neophyl Rearrangement
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The neophyl rearrangement is a long-established radical 1,2-aryl migration, yet catalytic enantioselective control of this process has remained elusive. Here we report a cooperative photoredox and chiral Brønsted acid catalytic system for the enantioselective neophyl rearrangement of tertiary alcohol-derived olefins. The reaction affords 1,5-dicarbonyl compounds bearing azaarene-substituted all-carbon quaternary stereocenters with up to 97% ee. Changing the radical precursor alters the preferred mode of catalyst recognition and reverses the absolute stereochemical outcome with the same catalyst configuration, providing access to opposite product enantiomers. The reaction also accommodates racemic olefin substrates, and experiments with the individual substrate enantiomers show that the chiral catalyst can counter their intrinsic stereochemical preferences. The results reveal how changes in catalyst–substrate recognition can alter stereochemical control during a transient radical rearrangement.

title: Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization of endo -Cyclic Monomers for Regioregularity Control in Vinyl Polymers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Radical polymerization of vinyl monomers is inherently governed by propagation pathways that favor head-to-tail connectivity, limiting access to alternative backbone regioregularities. To address this challenge, we report the radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) of endo-cyclic monomers, a class of monomers that has been largely unexplored in radical processes. Whereas many established rROP systems have been designed to introduce functional or cleavable units into polymer backbones, the present endo-cyclic monomers undergo selective rROP to generate carbon–carbon-backboned vinyl polymers enriched with nonhead-to-tail linkages. Copolymerization with conventional vinyl monomers was also achieved, providing access to copolymers with tunable backbone microstructures. In particular, using vinyl ketones and their corresponding endo-cyclic cyclodimers as structurally matched pairs, we accessed poly(vinyl ketone)s with systematically varied head-to-tail linkage contents. This control over backbone regioregularity translated into tunable macroscopic properties, including glass transition temperature and photodegradation kinetics, establishing regioregularity as a structural handle for controlling material properties. The strategy was also compatible with controlled radical polymerization, enabling the synthesis of well-defined block copolymers. Micelles assembled from these block copolymers further exhibited regioregularity-dependent sizes and photoresponsive behavior. These findings establish endo-cyclic rROP as a previously unrecognized strategy for controlling backbone regioregularity and properties in vinyl polymers.

title: Construction of benzochalcogenaboroles via single-atom editing of boracycles
abstract: Benzoxaborole is arguably the most important boron-based pharmacophore. Since Torssell's 1957 synthesis, hundreds of benzoxaborole derivatives have emerged, including US Food and Drug Administration-approved tavaborole and crisaborole. However, while peripheral modifications are well studied, synthetic challenges leave isoelectronic core modification less explored, despite its potential to enhance potency and reveal unexplored functions. Here we report a challenging ring expansion of benzoboretenes with elemental chalcogens, where benzoboretenes act as a 'diradical reservoir'. This synthetic protocol provides a versatile and modular platform for accessing three previously inaccessible classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeletons, in which the oxygen atom of the benzoxaborole core is formally replaced with Se, S or SO2. Preliminary biological evaluation reveals that this 'O-to-S' modification confers potent ferroptosis-inhibitory activity. Furthermore, its excellent functional group compatibility enables structure-activity optimization, leading to a 20-fold increase in cellular potency. This research not only expands the chemical space of boron-containing pharmacophores via single-atom ring expansion but also exemplifies how skeletal editing can unlock biological activities.

title: Mechano-redox catalysis enables anthraquinone-inspired H2O2 synthesis at polydopamine-water interfaces
abstract: A polydopamine (PDA)-based mechano-redox catalyst, inspired by the anthraquinone process, enables continuous H2O2 synthesis from water and oxygen under ambient conditions. Its dynamic catechol/quinone cycling and ultrasonic interfacial strain sustain redox turnover, thus offering an organic-solvent-free route to on-demand H2O2 production.

title: The potential of nanosized zeolites in catalysis
abstract: This review highlights nanosized zeolites in catalysis, emphasizing enhanced diffusion through shortened pathways and increased external surface area, which improve reactant accessibility, catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability.

title: Hydrogen-based green steel corridors: cost saving and emission reduction potentials of emerging trade routes
abstract: Deploying hydrogen-based direct-reduced iron (H 2 -DRI) technologies will be decisive to defossilize the global steel sector by replacing coal-based blast furnaces (BF) in conventional steelmaking. DRI can then either be directly fed into an electric-arc-furnace (EAF) and alternative electric smelting furnaces or transported as cold hot-briquetted iron (HBI) and a green commoditiy to a steel plant. The availability and expansion of low-cost renewable electricity and green hydrogen supply options is the essential and site-specific precondition to deploy H 2 -DRI plants that can be gradually switched from natural gas to hydrogen. However, near-zero emission steel made from H 2 -DRI needs to produced at competitive costs compared to fossil steel regulated under carbon emission pricing schemes. Based on revised green hydrogen cost forecasts in potentially low-cost countries like Australia or Oman, this study reveals the cost competitiveness of emerging green steel corridors built on international partnerships. With green HBI then exported to a representative EAF green steelmaking site, the analysis shows the potential cost savings of importing green HBI from renewable-rich countries when facing a future lack of affordable hydrogen supply options in leading steel countries like Germany or South Korea characterized by a high dependence on energy imports. Overall, low-emission crude steel based on 66 vol% H 2 -HBI imports achieves fossil cost parity in Germany in 2040 at increased carbon prices in the EU, while all 100% hydrogen-based steel scenarios inhere higher costs with a premium of 6%–13% over natural gas-based DRI-EAF crude steel at 828 € t −1 CS (with 0% scrap) at hydrogen costs ranging between 4.14 and 4.94 € kg −1 H 2 . In addition, a cradle-to-gate accounting of greenhouse gas emissions reveals that cost savings from HBI imports potentially come at the expense of up to 50% higher total emissions compared to an integrated H 2 -DRI-EAF plant running on iron ore pellet imports. All 100% H 2 -DRI-based scenarios yield an emission reduction between 42%–57% compared to a domestic benchmarked NG-DRI-EAF scenario at 1293 kg CO 2 (e) t −1 CS. The carbon footprint analysis further highlights the effect of upstream defossilization measures related to iron ore mining, pelletising and transport by rail and ship.

title: System-level optimization of seawater-based water supply and cooling for large-scale green hydrogen and ammonia production under variable renewable operation
abstract: As green hydrogen and ammonia projects expand in arid coastal regions, coupled demands for process water (PW) and cooling water (CW) increasingly constrain cooling system (CS) selection and water supply infrastructure sizing. To address this research gap, a transferable methodology for designing and techno-economically evaluating cooling and water supply systems for large-scale seawater-based production is presented. It combines time-resolved renewable power and ammonia production modelling, CS performance models, water treatment plant (WTP) sizing, PW and CW storage simulation, and cost assessment. It is applied to the 1.5 GW Phase 1 Murchison Green Hydrogen Project in Western Australia as a case study, using hourly ERA5 climate data for 2015–2024. The investigated CS options include once-through seawater cooling (OTSC), dry cooling (DC), wet cooling towers (WCT), and adiabatic hybrid coolers (AHC). Storage-based optimization substantially reduced the required peak treatment capacities, lowering WTP capacity by 12.4% (to 273 m 3 /h) for PW and CW capacity by 20.6% (to 1,127 m 3 /h) for WCT, and 63.0% (to 636 m 3 /h) for AHC. These reductions translated directly into lower PW-related capital expenditure, operational expenditure, and levelized cost of water (−8.7%, −4.2%, and − 7.3%, respectively). On an integrated cost basis, WCT achieved the lowest levelized cost of cooling (5.96 USD/MWh th ), below DC (38.0%), AHC (44.7%), and OTSC (73.6%). A simplified cost-allocation sensitivity showed that neglecting water treatment and marine infrastructure requirements can alter the CS ranking. The analysis further indicated that CS and water supply make a non-negligible contribution to the total levelized cost of hydrogen, accounting for 2.0–7.4%.

title: Printable Fe-Containing Apatitic Cement Scaffolds Coupling Sustained Platelet Lysate Release and Osteogenic Stimulation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Printable apatitic calcium phosphate cement (CPC) scaffolds integrating bioceramic particles, growth factors, and a polymer-based matrix were developed as an innovative strategy toward biomimetic bone substitutes. Iron-doped calcium phosphate (FeCaP) microparticles and human platelet lysates (PLs) were incorporated into a natural polymer-based matrix to create CPC-based inks that can be processed by Direct Ink Writing. CPC-based scaffolds containing FeCaP (Fe-CPC) and Fe-CPC/PL with controlled architecture, high shape fidelity, defined macroporosity, and compressive strength in the trabecular bone range (10–15 MPa) were successfully printed. After 21 days of immersion at 37 °C, the scaffolds preserved structural integrity, exhibited moderate degradation (5.77–6.23% mass loss), and sustained the release of PL-derived proteins of up to 82%, while the magnetic response of the FeCaP phase was preserved. In vitro, Fe-CPC/PL scaffolds supported human adipose-derived stem cell (hASC) attachment, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation. Higher early bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) secretion was followed by higher osteopontin (OPN) and osteocalcin (OCN) expression at later stages (∼9- and ∼3-fold, respectively, vs CPC), consistent with an osteogenic-supportive microenvironment. These findings demonstrate that Fe-CPC/PL is a 3D-printable apatitic scaffold that combines structural support with sustained biological signaling, with strong potential as a next-generation hybrid composite bone substitute.

title: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.

title: Chiral cobalt-catalysed electrochemical enantioselective C–P coupling via phosphinoyl radicals
abstract: The stereocontrolled generation and utilization of phosphinoyl radicals for asymmetric synthesis remain a formidable challenge, stemming from their transient nature and stereochemical unpredictability. Here we show an electrocatalytic strategy that addresses this longstanding challenge via the merger of asymmetric Lewis acid catalysis with anodic oxidation to enable highly enantioselective C–P bond formation. Through a Lewis acid-coupled electron-transfer mechanism, the chiral cobalt catalyst directs radical generation while creating a confined chiral environment that governs stereoselective bond formation. This integrated platform enables intermolecular coupling under mild conditions, providing efficient access to a diverse array of P(V)-stereogenic compounds with excellent enantioselectivity (up to 99% enantiomeric excess) and enabling synthetic diversification. Mechanistic studies, including electrochemical analysis, radical-clock experiments and density functional theory calculations, corroborate the proposed pathway and elucidate the origin of stereocontrol. This work bridges electrochemistry, asymmetric catalysis and radical chemistry, expanding the synthetic toolkit for constructing phosphorus stereocentres.

title: Self-Assembly–Galvanic Replacement Route to Conformal Ag Nanoflower Interfaces for Dendrite-Suppressed Zn Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable aqueous Zn anodes are severely limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics and morphological instability. Herein, we report a simple and vacuum-free self-assembly/galvanic replacement strategy that converts a silver nanoplate dispersion into a conformal Ag nanoflower scaffold on Zn foil (Zn@AgNF). This porous and highly wetting metallic interface provides continuous electron-transport pathways and a favorable interfacial environment for Zn nucleation, thereby promoting more uniform Zn deposition and improved interfacial kinetics. Ex situ morphological observations suggest a progressive deposition evolution toward compact Zn deposits with reduced surface oxidation. Symmetric cells exhibit reduced nucleation and growth overpotentials, narrow voltage hysteresis across a wide current-density range, and stable cycling at 10 mA cm–2. In rechargeable Zn–air full cells, Zn@AgNF decreases round-trip polarization and stabilizes interfacial impedance, while improving the full-cell Coulombic efficiency and cycling endurance under the tested conditions (5 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2). These advantages are maintained in gel electrolytes, in which the cells tolerate repeated bending up to 180°. This work demonstrates a simple solution-based interfacial engineering strategy for improving Zn deposition stability in aqueous Zn-based energy-storage systems.

title: Hypoxia-Driven, Self-Accelerating Immolative Photosensitizer Enabling Effective and Safe Photodynamic Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an emerging cancer treatment modality, but its clinical translation is hindered by the persistent post-PDT phototoxicity of existing photosensitizers. To address this challenge, we herein report a hypoxia-driven, self-accelerating immolative photosensitizer in which PDT itself drives posttherapy detoxification. This is demonstrated with AIE photosensitizers with an N-oxidation-mediated photoinduced electron transfer (PET) feature, which creates a charge-separation state with pronounced electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling feature, enabling efficient intersystem crossing. This N-oxidation thus converts the highly emissive fluorophore TBP into the robust type I photosensitizer TBPO. Critically, the N-O bond could be selectively cleaved by cytochrome P450 reductases under hypoxia, immolating TBPO back to TBP. Unlike previously reported ROS-driven immolative photosensitizers, this hypoxia-mediated immolation does not consume therapeutic ROS and is accelerated by PDT-aggravated hypoxia. Consequently, TBPO exhibits a self-propelled detoxification mechanism, ensuring an initial high PDT efficacy while minimizing residual phototoxicity after therapy. Moreover, this transition process is self-reported by the fluorescence light-up. This molecular design achieves both potent hypoxia-resistant PDT and fail-safe posttreatment safety, addressing two long-standing barriers to clinical PDT. This paradigm shift offers a general design principle for therapy-fueled self-detoxifying photosensitizers toward outpatient PDT without lifestyle restrictions.

title: NMR Reveals Coupled Ligand and Protein Conformational Equilibria That Modulate the Affinity of MDM2-Inhibitory Peptoids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Peptoids, atypical peptides with N-substitutions, are a promising drug modality for targeting protein–protein interactions. The binding affinity of an MDM2-inhibitory peptoid decreases by more than 100-fold upon removal of the backbone-restricting methyl groups attached to the α-carbons, although this modification alters the population of the all-trans amide-bond isomer by only 1.6-fold. This discrepancy raises the possibility that backbone flexibility affects not only ligand preorganization but also the conformational ensemble of the target protein. Here, we used NMR to examine the binding mode of the MDM2-peptoid complexes. ZZ-exchange experiments demonstrated that peptoid isomers containing cis amide bonds bind less favorably to MDM2 than the all-trans amide bond isomer. In addition, observation of the I19 δ1-methyl resonance of MDM2 in complex with the peptoids revealed that MDM2 exists in equilibrium between an open state, corresponding to the crystal structure of the MDM2-peptoid complex, and a semiclosed state, which retains partial interactions between the N-terminal region of MDM2 and the ligand-binding cleft. Increased population of the semiclosed state correlated with reduced binding affinities of the peptoids. We propose that cis-trans isomerization of the peptoid amide bonds and the conformational equilibrium of MDM2 within the peptoid complex synergistically contribute to the more than 100-fold decrease in binding affinity. These results identify coupled ligand and protein conformational equilibria as determinants of binding affinity and suggest conformational-plasticity control as a potential design principle for oligomeric ligands targeting protein–protein interactions.

title: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.

title: Resolving Chlorine Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron Diffraction Crystallography
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach could be extended to other complex solids incorporating quadrupolar nuclei and is not limited to solid-form screening, polymorph identification, and differentiation of salts and cocrystals.

title: Entropy Engineering Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The high-temperature oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity is closely correlated to the spin state of transition metals in perovskite anodes. However, the roles of entropy engineering in modulating the spin state and influencing high-temperature OER kinetics remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that entropy engineering of La0.7Sr0.3FeO3−δ to (SmNdPrLaBaSrCa)FeO3−δ (SNPLBSCF) induces a transition of B-site Fe species from high-spin to low-spin states. This transition enhances the d–p hybridization of Fe–O bonds, lowers the energy barriers for electron transfer and oxygen ion migration, and finally accelerates the high-temperature OER kinetics. Consequently, the SNPLBSCF anode in a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) achieves a current density of 3.64 A·cm–2 at 800 °C and 1.6 V, outperforming most reported anodes. This work not only provides fundamental insights into the spin state-activity relationships of perovskite oxides but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of highly efficient SOEC anodes through entropy engineering.

title: Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional Screening Reveals Noncanonical Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase (CRL)-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that likely induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.

title: Enantioconvergent N -Alkylation of Indoles with Alcohols Promoted by an Axially Chiral Iridacycle
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving chemo- and enantioselective N-substitution of indoles presents significant challenges for catalytic method development. Herein, we report an enantioconvergent N-substitution of indoles with racemic secondary alcohols enabled by a newly developed axially chiral biaryl-supported iridacycle and chiral phosphoric acid. This borrowing-hydrogen process proceeds through an intriguing sequence involving transfer hydrogenation of indole, enantioselective reductive amination of an indoline intermediate, and subsequent rearomatization. Controlled reaction temperatures also enable selective access to the N-substituted indolines prior to rearomatization. The catalytic process accommodates diverse indoles and unactivated secondary alcohols without additional stoichiometric reagents, providing a direct and atom-economical approach to enantioenriched N-substituted indoles, including analogs of established drug candidates.

title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH > 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

title: Elusive *CH–*CHO Coupling Pathway for High-Performance CO2 Electroreduction to n-Propanol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic reduction of CO2 to high-value n-propanol represents a promising yet challenging route toward sustainable carbon utilization. However, its practical implementation is severely hindered by low selectivity and activity, primarily originating from the high energy barrier involved in the rate-limiting *C2–*C1 coupling step. Herein, we have successfully constructed an elusive *CH–*CHO coupling pathway on a stable Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst, enabling low-barrier *C2 intermediate formation and highly selective n-propanol production. Leveraging the strong electron-accepting capacity of Cu2+ sites, key *CHO intermediates are strongly adsorbed and driven toward deep reduction to *CH species, effectively overcoming the critical five-electron transfer bottleneck for *CH generation. Meanwhile, adjacent Cu0 sites provide moderate and balanced adsorption of *CHO intermediates, allowing their asymmetric coupling with the Cu2+-stabilized *CH via a markedly low energy barrier, synergistically steering the reaction along the favorable *CH–*CHO pathway. In situ fiber-optic guided ATR-FTIR spectroscopy provides evidence for the coexistence of *CHO and *CHx-related intermediates, while DFT calculations further support the proposed *CH–*CHO coupling pathway. Accordingly, the Janus Cu2+/Cu0 catalyst achieves a high n-propanol Faradaic efficiency of 18.1% at a partial current density of 72.4 mA cm–2, alongside remarkable stability. This work establishes the *CH–*CHO pathway as a powerful strategy for kinetically favorable C–C coupling, opening a new mechanistic avenue for efficient conversion of CO2 to multicarbon via electrosynthesis.

title: An Allosteric CLR N-Terminal Swing-Out Mechanism for RAMP-Mediated Adrenomedullin Receptor Selectivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMP1–3) form heterodimers with the calcitonin (CTR) and calcitonin-like (CLR) G protein-coupled receptors and determine their selectivity for six CGRP family peptide agonists. These ligand–receptor systems are drug targets for migraine headache, diabetes and obesity, and circulatory system disorders. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulations and pharmacological assays of receptor chimeras and point mutants to identify a crucial allosteric component of the mechanism by which RAMP2 and RAMP3 modulate CLR to confer selectivity for two adrenomedullin (AM) peptides. We found that the extracellular domain (ECD) of RAMP2 and RAMP3, but not RAMP1, stabilized a partially unwound “swing-out” conformation of the CLR ECD N-terminal α-helix to accommodate the unique binding mode of the midregion of the AM peptides. The inability of the CTR N-terminus to adopt the swing-out conformation contributed to the distinct peptide selectivity profile of the three CTR-RAMP amylin receptors. By exploiting the CLR swing-out conformation, we engineered AM antagonist peptide variants with enhanced affinity and selectivity for CLR-RAMP2 and -RAMP3. Our results reveal the long-sought mechanism of RAMP-altered CLR ligand selectivity and have significant implications for drug development targeting the CLR- and CTR-RAMP complexes.

title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe 2–x Te x Polytypic Heterostructures
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure–superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2–xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range─from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T′ structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8) shows suppressed Tc (∼2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin–orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.

title: Experimental and Computational Identification of Wide-Gap Quaternary Oxychalcogenides BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oxychalcogenides have attracted attention as candidates for wide-gap p-type semiconductors in view of the energetically high and spatially spread characteristics of their valence electronic states. An appropriate choice of constituent cations would also enable n-type doping. However, reports on p-type doping have been mostly limited to Cu-based systems, which exhibit a strong p-type tendency due to hole generation and electron compensation by native Cu-vacancy acceptors. Oxychalcogenides with a practical level of n-type conductivity are yet to be developed. In this study, we focus on oxychalcogenides in the Ae–Zn–O–Ch (Ae = Ca, Sr, Ba; Ch = S, Se) quaternary system to explore new wide-gap semiconductors. Two as-yet-unreported compounds with wide band gaps, namely BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2, have been synthesized, along with four previously reported oxychalcogenides. First-principles calculations indicate that both BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2 feature direct-type band structures with low electron and hole effective masses, comparable to related compounds. Carrier compensation by native defects, however, is likely to make BaZn2OS2 insulating, whereas it can be well suppressed in SrZn2OSe2 by controlling the growth conditions. Systematic calculations of extrinsic dopants predict that bipolar doping of SrZn2OSe2 is feasible. Our results reveal the potential of non-Cu-based oxychalcogenides as a platform for the development of wide-gap, bipolar-dopable semiconductors, thereby stimulating exploration of related compounds.

title: Tritium breeding lifetime assessment of a ceramic-based blanket in a fusion tokamak device
abstract: Achieving tritium self-sufficiency is a critical requirement for the viability of future fusion power plants. Here, a comprehensive assessment of the operational lifetimes of ceramic breeder materials under neutron irradiation within a tokamak environment is presented, focusing on the evolution of the tritium breeding ratio (TBR) over reactor-relevant timescales. This is defined here as the operational timeframe at which the TBR is maintained above a critical threshold of 1.10. Using the depletion capabilities within the OpenMC neutronics code, both conventional ceramic breeders (Li TiO , Li SiO , and advanced ceramic breeder—ACB) and emerging hybrid breeder-multiplier ceramics (Li PbO , Li Be O ) are assessed for operational lifetime strategies. Initial optimisation identifies breeder-to-multiplier volumetric ratios that maximise TBR at time zero, followed by time-dependent simulations to quantify TBR degradation due to lithium depletion during service. It is shown that while higher initial multiplier fractions enhance TBR, they also accelerate lithium depletion, reducing blanket lifetime. Conversely, hybrid ceramics with intrinsic neutron multiplication show reduced sensitivity to additional multipliers. A novel layer-wise optimisation approach, varying breeder and multiplier distributions radially and poloidally, is shown to extend blanket lifetimes and maintain TBR above the critical threshold for longer periods demonstrating lifetime limitations may be elsewhere within the breeder blanket. Verification against FISPACT-II confirms the accuracy of the OpenMC depletion methodology utilised. The results highlight the importance of spatially optimised material distributions and lithium inventory management in maximising breeder blanket longevity. This work provides a robust framework for the design of next-generation solid breeder blankets, offering practical strategies to minimise replacement frequency and support sustainable fusion energy.

title: Programmable synaptic and stochastic regimes in a monolayer hBN atomristor
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrically programmable control over distinct memristive operation regimes remains largely unexplored in atomically thin materials. Here we demonstrate a monolayer hBN atomristor in which electrical stimuli reversibly switch the device between synaptic and stochastic regimes within the same atomic-scale platform. Electrical, thermal, and low-frequency noise measurements across the HRS–LRS transition reveal regime-dependent signatures of localized Ag configuration in the monolayer hBN device. In the stochastic regime, stochastic fluctuations and switching probability are electrically programmable, whereas the synaptic regime exhibits stable potentiation and depression characteristics. System-level studies further show that the regime tunability can be exploited for both neuromorphic and probabilistic computing. These results establish electrically programmable dynamic regime control as an operational framework for atomically thin memristive systems, providing pathways towards reconfigurable energy-efficient computing hardware.

title: Unidirectional rolling of single-crystal graphene into nanoscrolls
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transforming planar two-dimensional (2D) materials into rolled-up nanoscrolls has attracted broad interest, owing to the introduction of new degrees of freedom for materials design and property modulation. As one of the most representative 2D materials, graphene is a promising candidate for nanoscroll fabrication. However, the practical exploitation of graphene nanoscrolls has been hindered by the lack of reliable methods for precise control over structure and orientation, limiting their integration into large-scale electronics and optoelectronics. Here we show the aligned fabrication of graphene nanoscrolls via deterministic rolling of wafer-scale single-crystal graphene films during post-growth cooling, driven by anisotropic interfacial thermal stress from unidirectional Cu steps on vicinal Cu(111). The receiving nanoscrolls exhibit tunable thicknesses from 2 to 40 nm, and an approximately one-order-of-magnitude enhancement in photocurrent over planar monolayer graphene, together with improved conductance and carrier mobility. This process also enables the formation of adjacent wrinkle-free graphene single crystals, providing a promising strategy for wrinkle control in 2D materials.

title: Diminished subsurface oxygen maximum linked to rapid decline of the North Pacific Central Mode Water
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mode waters strongly shape ocean heat storage and oxygen uptake, yet their persistence under continued warming remains unclear. Here we show a rapid decline in the North Pacific Central Mode Water (CMW) since the early 2020s, leading to a marked reduction in the subsurface oxygen maximum at Station ALOHA, the monitoring site for the Hawaii Ocean Time-series program, 50 km north of Oahu. In general, weakened westerlies over recent decades have intensified surface warming and stratification, suppressing CMW renewal, whereas strong El Niño typically strengthens the westerlies and promotes vigorous CMW formation. In contrast, we find that the strong 2023–2024 El Niño failed to reinvigorate the CMW because the El Niño–related atmospheric teleconnection pattern shifted unusually far east of the formation region. Similar atmospheric anomalies are projected under future warming scenarios, implying inhibited surface-thermocline exchanges due to failed mode water ventilation, with consequences for climate, biogeochemical cycles, and marine ecosystems.

title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Global glacier recession is driving a rapid increase in the number and volume of ice-marginal lakes, leading to more frequent Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs). The long-term impact of GLOFs on glacier dynamics remains poorly understood, including in Greenland, which holds the largest glacial lake volume in the world. Here, using multi-decadal observations from Isortuarsuup Sermia, Southwest Greenland, we reveal that cyclical GLOFs regulate ice sheet motion. We identify a ‘sawtooth’ pattern of ice-dynamics, whereby multi-year acceleration is terminated abruptly by high-magnitude lake-drainage that resets the glacier to a ‘quiescent’ state for several years. The 2022 event exemplifies this process: the near-terminus ice velocity accelerated briefly from a pre-event baseline of ~200 m a−1 to ~1000 m a−1 before dropping to ~50 m a−1 over subsequent years. Each GLOF releases an immense meltwater volume (mean discharge in 2022 ~17000 m³ s−1), carving a ~1.5-km-wide, efficient subglacial channel. This channel enables extensive lowering of the subglacial water pressure, increasing ice–bed friction and suppressing ice motion. As climate warming increases GLOF frequency, this powerful negative feedback will modulate ice sheet motion acting as a brake on ice-dynamics at the margins of the Greenland Ice Sheet.

title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anthropogenic pressures on biodiversity necessitate efficient and scalable methods to predict global species distributions. Current species distribution models (SDMs) face challenges with large-scale datasets, complex species associations, and data quality. Here, we introduce EcoVAE, an autoencoder-based generative model that integrates bioclimatic variables with georeferenced occurrences. The model is trained separately for plants, butterflies, and mammals to predict global distributions at both genus and species levels. Through unsupervised learning, EcoVAE captures underlying distribution patterns from large-scale species occurrence data. It achieves high precision and speed, outperforming traditional SDMs in spatial block cross-validation. EcoVAE also reveals signatures of species associations that align with known prey-predator relationships. Taken together, these capacities enable the robust evaluation of global sampling efforts and interpolates distributions in data-limited regions, offering new applications for biodiversity exploration and monitoring.

title: Global intercomparison of ocean-based geochemical carbon dioxide removal efficiencies
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ocean-based geochemical CO2 removal approaches, including ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) and direct ocean removal (DOR), have received attention for their potential to remove billion-ton-scale amounts of CO2 from the atmosphere. Their viability at scale depends on efficiency. Here, we develop a unified framework for evaluating the efficiencies of ocean geochemical perturbations: OAE adds alkalinity, DOR removes dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), and combined alkalinity and DIC addition (ADA) adds both simultaneously. Using a global ocean biogeochemical model, we map global and seasonal DOR efficiency and compare it with OAE efficiency. Further, we show that OAE and DOR simulations can be combined to quantify the effect of simultaneous perturbations in alkalinity and DIC. This enables direct quantification of the oceanic fate of ADA perturbations from approaches such as enhanced rock weathering, riverine alkalinity enhancement and accelerated weathering of limestone. In these approaches, the added alkalinity partially equilibrates with CO2 before entering the ocean, effectively adding both alkalinity and DIC.

title: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sub-tomogram averaging of cryo-electron tomography maps often fails to reach the resolution required for atomic model building based on side-chain information, preventing accurate protein identification from the density alone. We develop DomainSeeker, which identifies protein domains by integrating AlphaFold2 models with experimental data. It partitions these models into domains by clique analysis of predicted aligned errors, fits them into segmented densities, and evaluates each fit globally and locally, deriving prior probabilities. Bayesian inference integrates the priors with cross-linking mass spectrometry, computing posterior probabilities. Applying prior probability analysis to mouse sperm microtubule doublet densities reveals higher recognition accuracy and resolution robustness than existing approaches. Incorporating cross-linking mass spectrometry for yeast nuclear pore complex densities further improves recognition performance and confidence. An interactive ChimeraX plugin facilitates user access. In this work, DomainSeeker addresses a bottleneck in in situ structural biology and supports visual proteomics in native cellular environments.

title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to skin homeostasis, but the antigenic targets remain unclear. Whilst CD1a is known to present lipid antigens to effector T cells, the possibility of CD1a presentation to Treg cells us not fully understood. Here, we show CD1a reactivity in subsets of human circulating and cutaneous CD4+ Treg cells, displaying αβ T cell receptors (TCRs), memory phenotypes and suppressive functions, including the ability to secrete interleukin-10 (IL-10) in response to the permissive lipid antigen lysophosphatidylcholine, known to be enriched in skin inflammation. Moreover, CD1a-reactive IL-10-producing CD4+ Treg cells from patients with psoriasis up-regulate type 1 and type 17 pro-inflammatory signatures under in vitro stimulation, while a corresponding Treg cell population is enriched and dysfunctional in psoriatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomic analyses suggest that CD1a-reactive Treg cell signatures are localized in close proximity to CD1a⁺ antigen-presenting cells within psoriatic lesions and are potentially connected through ligand-receptor interactions relevant to cell-cell contact, recruitment, and functional regulation. Furthermore, clonally expanded IL-10-producing Treg cells retain their suppressive phenotype in a CD1a-dependent and TCR-dependent manner. Together, these findings show that subsets of Treg cells are directed to self-lipid antigens and CD1a, but show an altered phenotype equipped with pro-inflammatory potential in the setting of psoriasis.

title: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Toll-like receptors (TLRs) support T cell priming in lymphatic tissues, but whether TLR stimulation within tumors also affects T cell function locally remains undefined. Here, we show that TLR2 signaling is necessary to promote CD8+ T cell-mediated tumor control by dual intravenous and intratumoral delivery of attenuated Listeria monocytogenes (IV + IT Lm). TLR2 signaling supports T cell priming in the spleen during IV infection, but unexpectedly, TLR2 is also critical for the activity of anti-Lm CD8+ T cells in tumors upon IT Lm injection. TLR2 signaling is unique among all TLRs in its capacity to drive a cDC2-dependent reduction in regulatory T cells (Treg) and destabilize Foxp3 expression. TLR2-mediated Treg destabilization correlates with increased tumor antigen cross-presentation and stronger antitumor CD8+ T cell responses. Ultimately, TLR2-dependent Treg depletion is required for tumor control by IV + IT Lm. These findings reveal a novel role for TLR2 activation by bacteria in tumors to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance tumor-specific T cell responses.

title: Encoding information into an embroidery of topological defects in liquid crystals
abstract: A photopatterned alignment layer with a periodic lattice of vortices acts as a substrate for pinned defect lines in a liquid crystal. These topological defect lines can be rearranged by optical manipulation into a vast number of states that can store information.

title: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a human bacterial pathogen with an array of molecular mechanisms to evade the action of antibiotics. Within the organism, efflux pumps provide a first-line defense mechanism, enabling broad multidrug resistance across antibiotic classes and the ability for the organism to evolve target-level resistance mechanisms. NorA is a key efflux transporter in S. aureus responsible for conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, puromycin, and other cytotoxic compounds. Here, we describe an approach to develop peptide efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) of NorA by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement and S. aureus growth inhibition. Our cryo-EM structure reveals that a lead peptide NPI-5 inserts deeply into NorA’s substrate binding pocket by using two tryptophan-arginine motifs to bind an anionic patch within NorA, thereby stabilizing the outward-facing conformation of the transporter and halting antibiotic efflux. Further optimization of NPI-5 involving unnatural residues and macrocyclization yielded cNPI-7, a peptide which potentiates fluoroquinolones in vitro and in a murine bacteremia infection model. The successful development of potent and selective peptide-based EPIs provides an approach for inhibiting other efflux systems from pathogenic organisms.

title: Promoted phase transition in perovskite heterojunctions via in-situ regulated 2D intermediates enables stable solar cells
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The formation of 2D/3D perovskite heterojunctions often relies on spacer-induced ion-exchange, which is difficult to achieve graded distribution of 2D species for efficient charge transport. Here, we report a phase-regulation strategy for formamidinium-based perovskites guided by pre-adding a full-composition 2D perovskite (hereinafter denoted as Pre-2D) into the FA-based 3D perovskite precursor.
