This approach enables coordinated control of precursor organization and interfacial phase evolution, resulting in bottom-up growth of phase-stable α‑FAPbI3 with vertically aligned 2D/3D heterostructures. The gradient architecture at the buried interface improves crystallographic orientation, suppresses defect-assisted recombination, and mitigates ion migration. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.61% at room temperature with a high efficiency of 28.01% at 245 K, and 23.58% for mini-modules. Notably, devices retain over 95% of initial efficiency after 1100 hours of continuous MPP tracking and 1700 hours of damp-heat testing. These findings provide a scalable route to regulate phase competition and buried-interface energetics in FA-based perovskites, advancing the development of efficient and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Current understanding of these processes largely derives from in vitro flat plates, hydroponics and gnotobiotic platforms. However, fungal-plant interactions largely occur in soil – a disordered and granular 3D environment with heterogeneous elasto-viscoplastic properties – whose inherent opacity precludes direct visualisation of the infection. How the physical structure of such natural habitats influences interkingdom interactions remains unknown. Here, we introduce an optically transparent 3D jammed granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments. This platform supports long-term co-culture of plants and fungi, while being compatible with classical physiological assays. We accomplish a direct cellular-level visualisation of the plant-fungal interface. Specifically, host-derived signals prior to the physical contact trigger hyphal reorientation towards the root tips. Using spatiotemporally resolved transcriptomics we discover distinct pathogen-host ex- and in-planta signalling modules, which are associated with granular heterogeneous environments. Together, our findings establish an experimental platform for dissecting fungal development and pathogenesis with unprecedented microscopic and molecular resolution.

title: CD33-CD45 interaction in Alzheimer’s disease susceptibility
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: CD33 is associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) susceptibility. The AD-associated rs3865444C risk variant reduces splicing of the sialic acid-binding domain, increasing the sialic acid-binding isoform seven-fold. Here we identify CD45, a GWAS-associated AD risk gene, as an immune cell-specific sialic acid-dependent cis CD33 binding partner, whose phosphatase activity CD33 inhibits. CD33 loss improved microglial amyloid beta clearance and protected against amyloid beta-induced dendritic spine loss in microglial-neuronal co-cultures, whereas CD45 loss impaired clearance, aligning with detrimental effects of CD33-mediated CD45 inhibition. CD33-CD45 interaction frequency was increased in monocytes from rs3865444CC individuals versus rs3865444AA, as well as in AD versus controls, independent of genotype. An interaction between CD33 and PTPRC (CD45) expression in human brain tissue was associated with a pathological AD diagnosis and global burden of AD pathology, consistent with the cellular findings above. Together, our results link CD33-mediated suppression of CD45 with AD genetic susceptibility and systemic myeloid dysfunction.

title: Distinct mechanisms of CNV formation at the human 15q13.3 locus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Human chromosome 15q13.3 is a hotspot for recurrent pathogenic copy number variants (CNVs) associated with schizophrenia, developmental delay and epilepsy. We generated long-read genome assemblies for 10 patient-parent trios and compared them to 581 population control haplotypes from diverse ancestry where this complex region is fully resolved. We find that both the long (“BP4-BP5”) and short (“CHRNA7”) forms of 15q13.3 CNVs arise predominantly by non-allelic homologous recombination (NAHR) whose susceptibility has been promoted by large inversion polymorphisms. While three BP4-BP5 breakpoints cluster in a 2 kbp PRDM9-enriched recombination hotspot, most CNVs are structurally distinct and affect the disease-relevant genes ARHGAP11B and CHRFAM7A differentially. Population analyses reveal at least 18 distinct structural haplotypes in 15q13.3 and show that the risk for BP4-BP5 CNVs is stratified more than 10-fold depending on ancestry, with 68.4% of Europeans but only 5.1% of East Asians predisposed, establishing inversion polymorphisms as major determinants of population-specific recurrent CNV susceptibility. Comparison to six ape species indicates that the duplication architecture promoting instability expanded recently and is largely human-specific.

title: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The GID/CTLH ubiquitin ligase is a multisubunit E3 conserved across eukaryotes. GID/CTLH has been implicated in a variety of processes, including metabolic regulation, cell proliferation, embryonic development and cell differentiation. However, our understanding of substrate recognition by GID/CTLH remains incomplete. Here, we characterize the regulation, specificity and functions of the putative substrate receptor Gid11 in budding yeast. We find that upon its expression during the switch of carbon source from glucose to ethanol, Gid11 associates with the core GID complex, likely assembling into a ring-like complex. Through systematic mutagenesis, we identify a negatively charged pocket on Gid11 that binds substrates carrying N-terminal degrons starting with threonine and define the Thr/N-degron motif. Such Thr/N-degrons are exposed upon co-translational removal of the initiator methionine, while escaping N-terminal acetylation. Finally, we show that during the glucose-to-ethanol transition, GIDGid11 targets for degradation factors linked to ribosomal biogenesis, amino acid, nucleotide and central carbon metabolism, opposing the established role of GID during the reverse transition from ethanol to glucose. Taken together, our results establish Gid11 as a bona fide GID substrate receptor and highlight GID as a regulator of metabolic transitions.

title: Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aneuploidy, resulting from whole-chromosome or segmental gains and losses, is generally detrimental to organismal fitness and is strongly associated with tumorigenesis. While sex chromosome aneuploidies are relatively well tolerated due to dedicated allelic dosage compensation mechanisms, the existence of comparable regulatory processes for autosomes remains debated. Here, we investigate transcriptional responses to autosomal aneuploidy and identify widespread dosage compensation across affected chromosomes. Using high-sensitivity allele-resolved single-cell RNA sequencing of monoclonal cell expansions spanning diverse ploidies and degrees of aneuploidy, we uncover consistent transcriptional compensation of both chromosomal gains and losses. This response operates in a region-specific manner across both complete and segmental aneuploidies, revealing an unexpected flexibility in dosage regulation. We show that chromosome losses are compensated through increased transcriptional burst frequency from the remaining allele. Complementary proteomics analyses demonstrate additional buffering at the protein level, resulting in a substantial, though still incomplete, restoration of stoichiometric balance across autosomal aneuploid chromosomes for both copy number gains and losses. Analyses of cancer transcriptomes confirm that compensatory mechanisms are active in human tumours. Together, our findings establish dosage compensation as a genome-wide and dynamic response to gene dose imbalance. This mechanism extends beyond sex chromosomes, supports transcriptional homeostasis, and represents a fundamental and evolutionarily conserved mode of gene regulation active across species and in aneuploid cancer cells.

title: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A pause in DNA synthesis that occurs when the replisome encounters an obstacle could lead to genome instability. Although important, systematic identification of replication pause sites is challenging due to their low frequency and delocalised nature. Here we present a single-molecule identification of sites of replisome perturbation across a eukaryotic genome using long-read nanopore sequencing. For each single-molecule replication pause we determine the direction of replication, leading/lagging-strand identity, location and approximate duration, and whether the replisome resumed synthesis. Although pauses are largely diffuse over the genome, they are significantly enriched over transcribed features and correlate with transcription and R-loop levels. Transcription-replication conflicts are more numerous when head-on than co-directional. Finally, we identify genomic loci with a strong bias towards leading over lagging strand pauses, consistent with uncoupling of the helicase from polymerase epsilon. As one such locus overlaps with an epigenetically-regulated gene, we suggest that helicase-polymerase uncoupling resulting from replication pausing could trigger epigenetic switching.

title: Rethinking Klebsiella pneumoniae vaccines: from protective immunity to rational vaccine design
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae infections cause hundreds of thousands of deaths annually, yet a licensed vaccine remains elusive. Current strategies targeting capsular polysaccharides and lipopolysaccharides show promise but face limitations due to the complexity of Klebsiella pathogenesis and incomplete understanding of protective immunity. This Review highlights the critical barriers hindering broad protection against K. pneumoniae. We argue that next-generation vaccines require a paradigm shift, integrating antigen discovery, systems immunology and translational models to define conserved protective targets and immune correlates. This holistic strategy is essential to predict vaccine efficacy and finally combat this escalating global health threat.

title: Impact of ICRH-driven beta-induced Alfvén eigenmode on fast-ion redistribution and ion heating in EAST plasmas
abstract: In magnetically confined plasmas, energetic-particle (EP)-driven instabilities can induce redistribution and losses of energetic ions, thereby affecting plasma heating and confinement. In this work, fast-ion-driven beta-induced Alfvén eigenmode (BAE) excited by ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) was investigated in low-density EAST plasmas using experimentally reconstructed equilibria and profiles. Experimentally, strong ICRH led to a significant increase in ion temperature and plasma stored energy, accompanied by the excitation of an Alfvén eigenmode at 64 under 1.6 MW heating power, while no such mode was observed at reduced power. Continuum analysis identified this mode as a core-localized BAE. To interpret these observations, integrated simulations combining TORIC, ASCOT, and GTC were performed. A modified fast-ion distribution function was implemented to capture the strong velocity-space anisotropy of ICRH-generated fast ions. Linear gyrokinetic simulations reproduced the observed BAE frequency and identified a threshold in fast-ion pressure for mode excitation. Orbit-following simulations with realistic wall geometry demonstrated that the BAE induces significant phase-space redistribution and enhances the loss of high-energy fast ions (energy ). Separately, the ASCOT power-deposition analysis shows that the strong BAE reduces the collisional power transferred from fast ions to thermal ions, thereby suppressing the fast-ion contribution to ion heating and limiting the increase in ion temperature. As the measured BAE activity decreases in Phase B, recovery of this ion-heating channel explains the subsequent rise in ion temperature. These results clarify the interplay between ICRH-generated fast ions, BAE activity, and ion heating, and provide insights into optimizing fast-ion confinement and heating efficiency in future burning plasma devices.

title: Linear and nonlinear benchmark of gyrokinetic simulation of energetic particle driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes in ITPA TAE benchmark case
abstract: A new gyrokinetic code, TEK, was benchmarked in simulating energetic particle (EP) driven toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) in the simple tokamak configuration chosen by the ITPA-EP group for code benchmarking purposes. Linear benchmark has been well established by other codes, whereas nonlinear benchmark for this case is lacking. This paper presents, besides the linear benchmark, nonlinear results for both single- and multiple- simulations ( is the toroidal mode number). The nonlinear results are in good agreement with an analytical theory on zonal field beat-driven by Alfvén eigenmodes, partially verifying the correctness of the nonlinear simulations. The saturation level and the resulting EP transport are examined. This provides data for future inter-code nonlinear benchmarking. In TEK, all species (electrons, thermal ions, EPs) are treated on the same footing using the gyrokinetic model (with electrons in the zero Larmor radius limit). The electromagnetic cancellation problem is mitigated by using the mixed-variable pullback method. Numerical details related to electromagnetic gyrokinetic simulation are discussed.

title: Differentiable Solvation Shell Model for Rational Electrolyte Design
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tailoring the Li+ solvation shell is a central design principle for many emerging Li metal battery electrolytes but remains largely qualitative. Here, we introduce a mean-field Ising model that predicts the Li+ solvation shell from the donor number (DN), acceptor number, molar ratio, and molecular size. The model is end-to-end differentiable, enabling direct parameterization from molecular dynamics (MD) solvation structures. For localized high-concentration electrolytes, it reproduces MD shell compositions with 10.7% RMSE at much reduced cost and captures solvation trends in other electrolyte classes without re-fitting. Model interaction terms show that DN dominates Li+ solvation energetics, explaining the empirical DN-based design rules. For LiTFSI in tetraglyme absent from training, the model identifies fluorobenzene as a diluent and a concentration window with anion-rich solvation shells and low free solvent. The predicted solvation structure is confirmed by MD, and published experiments on related electrolytes support the design principles.

title: Revealing the Atomic-Scale Degradation of Platinum-Based Intermetallic Nanocatalysts Upon Relevant Fuel Cell Conditions
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Platinum-based intermetallic nanomaterials are promising catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, insights regarding their degradation under realistic PEMFC conditions still represent a knowledge gap. Herein, a systematic series of L12-Pt3M (M = V, Cr, or Zn) intermetallics with a similar structure, chemical composition, and morphology were synthesized, and their activity-stability trends were evaluated under conditions relevant to PEMFCs. Time- and potential-resolved catalyst dissolution were acquired and quantified through online ICP-MS using 1 M HClO4 at 65 °C, revealing that the first catalyst/electrolyte contact induces significant catalyst degradation before operation. During electrochemical operation, the anodic dissolution at 65 °C is substantially higher than at 25 °C, and a strong competition between cathodic dissolution and ion redeposition takes place. Identical-location electron microscopy analyses captured atomic degradation processes directly linked to catalyst electrochemical dissolution enhanced by temperature, providing new understanding for developing robust catalysts for PEMFCs.

title: Fast-Charging Sodium Solid-State Batteries Enabled by closo -Hydridoborate Anode Interlayers for Sulfide Electrolytes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sodium solid-state batteries may offer high-power operation through highly conductive sulfide solid electrolytes but remain limited by unstable electrode|electrolyte interfaces. Bilayer separators can decouple interfacial requirements if electrochemical compatibility, contact quality, and charge transfer are ensured. Here, the closo-hydridoborate Na4(B10H10)(B12H12) is identified as an effective interlayer material for sulfide electrolytes. Time-dependent impedance measurements reveal that Na3PS4 bilayer cells still suffer from severe instability, while Na3SbS4 and Na2.9P0.9W0.1S4 bilayers are stabilized by the hydridoborate interlayer. For the latter cells, the interface resistance is easily dominated by poor mechanical contact but can be eliminated under moderate stack pressure. Incorporating Na4(B10H10)(B12H12) enables stable cycling of Na2.9P0.9W0.1S4-based cells with a TiS2-based cathode and Na15Sn4/Na3Sn anode, delivering >90% capacity retention over 250 cycles and capacitor-like charging from 0–50% SOC in 30 s (82 mA cm–2) at 80 °C. The results identify closo-hydridoborate interlayers as key enablers for high-power sodium sulfide solid-state batteries.

title: Host control of rhizobial proliferation in soybean nodules
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The root nodules of leguminous plants contain rhizobia that proliferate and differentiate into bacteroids inside symbiosomes for nitrogen fixation. Hosts must tightly regulate rhizobial proliferation to optimize symbiotic benefits and avoid pathogenicity, yet the mechanisms governing this balancing act remain unknown for most legumes. Here, using in vitro assays and pectin-deficient mutants, we show that intracellular demethylesterified pectin (DMEP) directly constrains rhizobial growth in soybean nodules. Furthermore, we show that host factors HOF1 and HOF2 act as regulators of DMEP stability, binding DMEP to prevent its degradation via polygalacturonase. Genetically altered plants with modestly reduced rhizobial abundance exhibited significantly higher nitrogenase activity per gram of nodules, revealing the importance of host-mediated restriction of bacterial numbers in determining symbiotic efficiency. Our findings uncover an unanticipated role for cell wall components in controlling endosymbiont population size and provide insights into host–symbiont interactions, with potential implications for legume improvement and crop yields.

title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation in endometriosis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting 10% of women, characterized by the growth of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus. Through a genome-wide DNA methylation meta-analysis of nine independent cohorts (n = 1138 samples), we show an epigenetic dichotomy: the eutopic endometrium of endometriosis cases shows no significant divergence from healthy controls, whereas ectopic lesions exhibit massive, consistent hyper/hypomethylation. We identify 1824 differentially methylated regions targeting the HOX clusters, ESR1, and GATA2, key regulators of cell differentiation and hormonal response. This suggests that endometriotic cells possess an epigenetic identity distinct from normal endometrial cells. While most alterations reflect biological mechanisms shared across anatomical sites, distinct signatures exist between lesion types. By harmonizing independent datasets, our study provides a high-resolution molecular map of lesions and strengthens the evidence that DNA methylation drives endometriosis biology.

title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Photonic computing offers high bandwidth, parallelism and energy efficiency for artificial intelligence (AI), yet its scalability remains limited by bulky optical components and immature optoelectronic integration. Here we present HyperON, a thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) hyperdimensional optical network built around a passive spectral-spatial interweaver and broadband wavelength-parallel modulators. The interweaver combines wavelength multiplexing with spatial replication in a log2P-stage network, delivering the full wavelength set to every spatial output without beam-combination loss. By interweaving P spectral channels with K spatial units, HyperON forms a unified P × K parallel computing framework, supporting O(N2) operations with only O(N) modulators, improving hardware efficiency and scalability. A 16 × 16 interweaver shows low-loss, broadband and highly uniform operation across 1523.40-1568.85 nm, with 1.30 dB average loss, 0.196 dB output-port variation and 0.414 dB cross-wavelength variation. The integrated wavelength-parallel modulators retain system-level bandwidths of 53-67 GHz after large-scale routing, while standalone devices exhibit bandwidths beyond 67 GHz. Together, these features enable the fabricated HyperON chip to deliver a projected peak throughput of 32.8 TMAC/s, with estimated energy and area efficiencies of 7.04 TMAC/s/W and 0.163 TMAC/s/mm2, respectively. Experimental demonstrations in image convolution, handwritten digit recognition, and 64-mode parallel computing confirm its high speed operation, versatility, and scalability for large-scale AI workloads.

title: Ligand-field reconstruction enables 4.7 V LiCoO 2 with suppressed chemomechanical degradation for high-energy batteries
abstract: Ligand-field reconstruction via bulk fluorine incorporation stabilizes the oxygen sublattice of LiCoO 2 , enabling outstanding cycling stability under a 4.7 V high cutoff voltage with suppressed surface reconstruction and chemomechanical degradation.

title: Ultrasound-Based Physiological Sensing: Challenges, Strategies, and Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultrasound is well suited to repeated deep-tissue imaging, but it rarely measures local biochemical conditions directly. Stimuli-responsive chemistry enables materials to respond to physiological cues through physicochemical changes, yet these changes are not necessarily detectable by ultrasound. Multiscale structural organization can bridge this gap by translating and amplifying molecular or nanoscale responses into larger-scale material changes that produce detectable acoustic signals. The field is progressing from proof-of-concept demonstrations of material responses towards integrated sensing platforms. Advances across these platforms include bioresorption, multiparametric sensing, and repeated measurements over defined periods in animal models. This review examines how responsive chemistry and multiscale structural design jointly enable ultrasound-readable physiological sensing. It also considers the requirements for reliable operation in vivo. Looking ahead, integration with wearable and conformal ultrasound interfaces, soft robotic systems, and AI-assisted decoding could enable longitudinal, personalized, and multiparametric sensing across internal organs and tissue interfaces.

title: Catalytic Manganese Ferrite Nanoparticles Improve Therapeutic Response in Glioblastoma Spheroids through Hypoxia Mitigation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by treatment resistance, high recurrence rate, and dismal survival, features influenced by tumor hypoxia, a clinically well-established driver of radio- and chemoresistance. Manganese ferrite nanoparticles possess catalase-like activity capable of generating oxygen from tumor-endogenous hydrogen peroxide, offering a strategy to alleviate tumor hypoxia and re-sensitize GBM cells to chemotherapy. In this study, two manganese ferrite compositions (Mn2FeO4 and MnFe2O4) were synthesized using flame spray pyrolysis, characterized, and evaluated for their ability to reduce hypoxia. Nanoparticle internalization and distribution were confirmed in both patient-derived ZH757 and commercial U87MG GBM spheroid models. Both ferrite formulations decreased the hypoxic cell fraction in GBM spheroids after 17 days, without inducing cytotoxicity in normal fibroblasts. Therapeutic in vitro efficacy was assessed on the previously established GliaMimic treatment evaluation platform, which longitudinally monitors tumor progression during a 17-day in vitro treatment regimen of single-fraction radiation (4 Gy) plus multicycle temozolamide (10, 50, 100 μM TMZ) followed by a treatment-free interval. Nanoparticle-treated tumor spheroids exhibited in combination with radio- and chemotherapy enhanced early cytotoxicity and reduced viability and metabolic activity at the end of treatment, compared to the radiation plus TMZ control alone, with treatment benefits generally becoming more pronounced at higher TMZ doses. Notably, after treatment cessation, nanoparticle-treated groups displayed lower post-treatment progression, likely indicating sustained post-treatment efficacy. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding of catalytic nanoparticle-mediated tumor oxygenation, providing a crucial in vitro foundation for its application as an adjuvant strategy to improve therapeutic efficacy in GBM.

title: Efficient Depolymerization of Polyester Plastic Enabled by Ultrathin Co-Doped ZnO Nanosheets with Abundant Oxygen Vacancies
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The chemical recycling of polyester plastics is a promising sustainable route to resource recycling and environmental protection, yet its success hinges on the development of efficient heterogeneous catalysts. Herein, a high-gravity-assisted strategy using rotating packed bed (RPB) is proposed to continuously and rapidly synthesize ultrathin Co-doped nanosheets (Co/ZnO-RPB) for depolymerizing polyester plastics. Compared to the counterpart of batch-type stirred tank (Co/ZnO-ST), the optimized nanosheets exhibit a 60% reduction in thickness, accompanied by a 2.3-fold enhancement in doping efficiency and a 1.3-fold increase in oxygen vacancy concentration. The as-prepared Co/ZnO-RPB possessed outstanding performance for PLA methanolysis at 105 °C, achieving a methyl lactate (MeLA) formation rate of 521.7 g gcat–1 h–1, which is 1.8 times higher than that of Co/ZnO-ST, exceeding most reported catalysts. Comprehensive characterization and in situ infrared spectroscopy reveal the synergistic mechanism of PLA methanolysis. Oxygen vacancies enhance the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon while driving the cleavage of methanol to generate nucleophilic species, which further drives ester bond cleavage. More importantly, the Co/ZnO-RPB exhibits remarkable versatility by effectively depolymerizing other polyester plastics and various real-life polyester wastes. This work offers a valuable guidance to the challenge of waste polyester plastics accumulation.

title: Injectable Hydrogels for Programmable Protein Release
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Injectable and degradable hydrogels provide a promising route for controlling the spatiotemporal release of protein therapeutics, yet achieving programmable release kinetics across proteins of different sizes remains challenging. Here, dextran–oxanorbornadiene (OND)/PEG–thiol hydrogels are described that integrate a degradable hydrogel network with tunable Michael addition reactivity to enable hydrolysis-gated and chemically programmable protein release. The OND linkers serve dual functions as crosslinkers forming the hydrogel network and as covalent tethers for protein cargos, allowing kinetic control over tethering efficiency and release rate through the choice of OND variant, precursor mixing sequence, and degree of protein functionalization. Using model proteins of different sizes and structural flexibilities—green fluorescent protein (GFP, 27 kDa), immunoglobulin G (IgG, 150 kDa), and the trimeric ectodomain of the HIV-1 glycoprotein (350 kDa)—the system demonstrates a transition from diffusion-dominated to hydrolysis-gated, non-first-order release behavior. Two mechanistically distinct tethering regimes were identified: reaction-rate-dominated tethering for IgG and competition-limited tethering for GFP, providing complementary routes for controlling cargo retention and release. Additional formulation-level modulation through network density and crosslinker topology provided orthogonal control over release rate and protein loading capacity. Representative cargos subjected to covalent tethering and release preserved protein structure and function after release. Collectively, this study establishes a modular framework for designing injectable OND hydrogels that achieve predictable and customizable release kinetics, offering a versatile platform for long-acting delivery of biologic therapeutics.

title: Microneedle-Enabled Metabolic-Redox Amplification Cascade for Suppressing Postoperative Tumor Recurrence
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Residual tumor cells can survive surgical resection by maintaining nutrient supply and antioxidant defenses, thereby driving postsurgical recurrence. Here, we develop a dissolvable microneedle platform, MN-MnO2/MPN, that integrates glucose depletion with redox catalysis to establish a localized metabolic-redox amplification cascade. MnO2 exhibits glucose oxidase-like activity, promoting glucose consumption and H2O2 generation, while the copper-tannic acid metal-polyphenol network facilitates stimulus-responsive Cu2+ release, glutathione depletion, and Fenton-like oxidative catalysis. These coordinated processes amplify intracellular oxidative stress, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, and tumor cell death. In a 4T1 incomplete-resection model, MN-MnO2/MPN markedly suppresses residual tumor regrowth, reducing tumor weight by approximately 80% and achieving 60% survival at day 38. Mechanistically, treatment decreased intratumoral glucose levels by approximately 60% and increased malondialdehyde levels by 2.5-fold, supporting coordinated metabolic deprivation and oxidative damage in vivo. Transcriptomic analysis further identified 3904 differentially expressed genes, with enrichment of metabolic, oxidative stress, and cell-death-associated pathways. This study shows the potential of locally deployable catalytic therapies that exploit the metabolic and redox vulnerabilities of postoperative residual tumors.

title: Engineering Nitroimidazole-Based Molecular Elements for Hypoxia-Responsive Oligonucleotide Materials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hypoxia-responsive oligonucleotides (ONs) offer a route to conditionally regulate nucleic acid activity in diseased tissues, but the chemical factors that govern their masking and activation remain insufficiently defined. Here, we synthesized four nitroimidazole-modified phosphoramidite monomers derived from adenine (Ah), guanine (Gh), thymine (Th), and cytosine (Ch) and incorporated the Th, Ah, and Gh building blocks into ONs by automated solid-phase synthesis. Using a common parent sequence, we compared Th-, Ah-, and Gh-modified ONs in terms of synthetic compatibility, duplex stability, and reductive release, and further evaluated selected Th-modified ONs in cellular and in vivo studies. Thermal denaturation studies showed that internal Th and Gh modifications caused substantial destabilization of DNA/RNA duplexes, whereas Ah modifications were better tolerated. Under nitroreductase/NADPH reduction conditions, the Gh modification showed the most efficient regeneration of the native ON, while Ah mainly formed reduced but uncleaved products and Th gave partial release. Although Gh provided favorable masking and release behavior, Th offered a more practical balance of synthetic accessibility and duplex inhibition. Th-modified ONs retained Clusterin-silencing activity in MIA PaCa-2 cells and showed hypoxia-associated recovery of activity, and enhanced and prolonged tumor-associated fluorescence in tumor-bearing mice compared with an unmodified control. These results highlight the importance of the tested nucleobase–attachment-site combinations in the design of nitroimidazole-modified ONs.

title: Thickness-Driven Evolution of Third-Order Nonlinear Response in Ternary TMDC MoNbSe2
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thickness variation in 2D materials is essential for nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Since key nonlinear parameters such as nonlinear absorption, effective nonlinear coefficients, and carrier generation-recovery dynamics change from monolayer to few-layer thicknesses, systematic thickness-dependent measurements are needed to extract reliable NLO parameters and identify optimal regimes for applications including mode-locking, optical switching, and optical limiting. Here, third-order NLO responses of heterometallic ternary transition metal dichalcogenide (TMDC) MoNbSe2 nanoflakes are observed with varying thicknesses under two excitation wavelengths. Under 1 µm laser excitation, the saturable absorption (SA) behavior diminishes (β decreasing from –42 to –9.7 × 103 cm/GW) with decreasing thickness from approximately 63 to 3 nm, while under 1558 nm excitation, β varies from –10 to –7.6 × 103 cm/GW at low pump intensity and from 11 to 15.2 × 103 cm/GW at high intensities as the thickness is reduced to 3 nm. Notably, at 3 nm thickness under 1 µm excitation, only SA is observed, as the reduced thickness provides a limited carrier population, thereby only a small fraction of photons excites these carriers, while the rest are transmitted. In contrast, at 1.5 µm excitation reverse saturable absorption (RSA) dominates since the incoming lower photon energy promotes absorption through excited-state and defect-state pathways. These results validate wavelength-dependent NLO fundamentals and highlight the versatility of MoNbSe2 for miniaturized photonic technologies. Moreover, the observed SA response is leveraged for ultrafast photonic generation, enabling stable mode-locked pulse formation with a measured pulse duration of 766 fs at 1.5 µm with a repetition rate of 8.011 MHz. Collectively, this study aims to elucidate thickness-dependent NLO mechanisms, and the demonstrated broadband, wavelength-dependent NLO response and mode-locking performance establish MoNbSe2 as a strong candidate for next-generation ultrafast photonic components.

title: Harnessing Weak Intermolecular Interactions for Efficient PFOA Capture in a Fluorine-Rich Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Membrane
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

title: Electronic Structure and Charge Separation Modulation of Carbon Nitride by -B(OH)- Groups for Enhanced Photocatalytic Phenol Degradation via Peroxymonosulfate Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (CN) has emerged as a promising photocatalyst for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based advanced oxidation processes, but its performance is constrained by rapid charge recombination and poor PMS activation capability. Herein, we report a boron-doped CN featuring distinctive -B(OH)- groups (OH-BCN20), synthesized via one-step calcination of urea with trace boric acid. The -B(OH)- groups play a pivotal role in PMS activation by strategically modulating the electronic and band structure of CN. Under dark conditions, the electron-deficient B atoms in the -B(OH)- groups serve as primary active sites, facilitating PMS adsorption and subsequent oxidation to generate 1O2. Upon visible light irradiation, photogenerated holes tend to accumulate at B sites, and the resultant efficient charge separation promotes PMS activation. Consequently, the OH-BCN20/PMS/Vis system removes 99.5% of phenol (PE) under visible light, outperforming the CN/PMS/Vis system (38.8%). In the dark, the OH-BCN20/PMS system degrades 43.5% of PE in 60 min, whereas pristine CN shows no activity. This system also demonstrates robust performance in complex water matrices, achieves effective detoxification, and maintains stable continuous-flow operation for 12 h. This study uncovers the critical role of -B(OH)- groups in achieving efficient electronic and band structure modulation of CN, offering a novel paradigm for designing high-performance metal-free catalysts for wastewater treatment.

title: Catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation for precise synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Organic semiconductors such as polythiophenes (PThs) offer substantial potential for flexible optoelectronics. Incorporating silicon into the PTh backbone represents a promising strategy to enhance flexibility and tune electronic properties; however, conventional metal-catalyzed synthetic approaches lack precise control over polymer chain growth, yielding materials with poorly defined energy levels and relatively board dispersity. Here, we report a catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation (TDP) strategy for the direct incorporation of silicon into PThs, producing a class of narrowly dispersed silicon-incorporated polymers. This thermally driven, radical-mediated mechanism circumvents the uncontrolled initiation and competitive pathways of conventional catalytic routes, enabling precise control over chain growth and yielding well-defined PThs with narrow dispersity (Đ = 1.2 – 1.4). The dehydrogenatively coupled diphenylsilane- terthiophene polymer (PS-1) shows favorable energy-level alignment and a hole mobility of 9.2 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1. When employed as a hole-transport interlayer in inverted tin-lead (Sn-Pb) perovskite solar cells, PS-1 enables a champion power conversion efficiency of 23.3% with enhanced operational stability, surpassing the 20.8% efficiency of standard PEDOT:PSS-based devices. This work establishes a scalable synthetic route to advanced conjugated polymers, providing a versatile materials platform for optoelectronic applications.

title: Biodegradable Periodic Mesoporous Organosilica Nanoparticles for Enhanced Rifampicin Activity Against Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Its Biofilm
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multidrug-resistant (MDR) and biofilm-associated bacterial infections are increasingly prevalent in healthcare settings, and they create a serious global health problem by increasing the morbidity and mortality rates. Nanomaterial-based alternative therapeutic approaches have therefore been widely explored as potential strategies for improving the treatment of MDR infections. Here, we report a drug delivery system based on biocompatible and biodegradable surface-engineered periodic mesoporous organosilica nanoparticles (nanoPMOs), designed to enhance the antibacterial and antibiofilm efficiency of the antibiotic rifampicin against the high-priority MDR Gram-negative pathogenic bacterium, Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Mannose functionalization appeared to improve the association of the nanoPMOs with bacterial cells and biofilms, while the acid-cleavable imine linkages enabled faster nanoparticle degradation and rifampicin release under acidic conditions. Compared with free rifampicin, the rifampicin-loaded nanoPMOs effectively killed planktonic bacteria and reduced the biomass of preformed biofilms under the tested in vitro conditions. The rifampicin-loaded nanoPMO formulations also showed low nonspecific cytotoxicity and hemolytic activity at the concentrations examined.

title: Surface Texturing Boosts Silicon-Based Tribovoltaic Nanogenerators via Synergistic Edge Electric Field and Tribochemistry
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon-based tribovoltaic nanogenerators (TVNGs) can directly convert sliding-induced interfacial processes into electrical output, but their performance is often limited by inefficient carrier generation and transport. Here, square-pillar arrays were fabricated on monocrystalline silicon to investigate how surface texture affects output magnitude and polarity. Texturing increased the peak current by approximately 25-fold, and both n-type and p-type textured devices exhibited positive current polarity. The p-type device also showed a gradual transition from negative to positive current during initial sliding. Output depended strongly on the longitudinal spacing between pillars and the number of simultaneously engaged transverse rows, whereas no clear monotonic dependence on pillar width was observed under the tested conditions. Among the counterface materials, GCr15 steel produced the highest and most stable output; H62 brass and 1060 aluminum produced lower or unstable currents accompanied by different transfer and oxidation features. Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) revealed a spatially nonuniform surface-potential distribution near pillar edges and a sliding-associated potential change in the trench-bottom region. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) detected SiO2 and substoichiometric silicon oxides on the silicon surface, as well as Fe2O3 in steel-derived wear debris. The strong suppression of output during nitrogen purging further indicates that the response is sensitive to the ambient atmosphere. Taken together, these observations are consistent with a mechanism in which texture-dependent contact and repeated edge encounters modify the interfacial state, while oxide-related transport and oxygen-sensitive tribochemistry contribute to carrier generation and collection. The proposed competition between the built-in electric field (BEF) and an evolving interfacial electric field (IEF) provides a framework for interpreting the polarity transition.

title: NIR-Triggered Photothermal-Gated Microneedle Patch for Stage-Responsive Microenvironment Remodeling in Infected Burn Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Achieving precise and effective treatment of infected burn wounds across different healing stages remains a major challenge in current wound management strategies. To address this issue, we developed a near-infrared (NIR)-responsive photothermal-gated hemin-coated polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/polyacrylamide (PA)/magnesium silicide (Mg2Si) microneedle patch (abbreviated as PPMH), designed to enable spatiotemporally controlled therapeutic gaseous-ionic release for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling throughout wound healing. The microneedle matrix, constructed from biocompatible polymers, integrates exudate-absorbing components at the base and hydrogen-generating magnesium silicide nanosheets (MN) at the needle tips. A hydrophobic hemin shell serves as a photothermal-responsive gate for on-demand activation. Upon insertion into the wound tissue, the microneedles effectively penetrate biological barriers and establish localized therapeutic interfaces. Upon NIR irradiation, the hemin shell undergoes rapid photothermal conversion, triggering gate opening and controlled hydrogen release within the dermal tissue. During the inflammatory phase, the released hydrogen alleviates oxidative stress and suppresses inflammation, while the photothermal effect of the outer hemin coating exerts potent antibacterial action to clear local bacterial infection. In the subsequent regeneration phase, the sustained release of Mg2+ and Si-containing species promotes angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. Collectively, this system effectively modulates the wound microenvironment in a stage-dependent manner, accelerating tissue regeneration and functional recovery. Therefore, PPMH designed in this study represents a versatile and translational platform for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling and multi-targeted treatment of complex burn wounds.

title: Two-Stage Machine Learning-Assisted Multiplex Catecholamine Quantification in Artificial Urine on a Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Paper
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catecholamines, including dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine, are important biomarkers of neurological and neuroendocrine disorders. However, their simultaneous quantification in body fluids remains challenging because of their similar molecular structures, which produce highly overlapping Raman spectroscopic signatures. Here, we develop an integrated platform combining an iron-nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA-Fe)-functionalized surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) paper with a two-stage machine learning pipeline for catecholamine quantification in artificial urine. The SERS paper enables rapid drop-and-measure detection, achieving limits of detection of 7.18, 9.01, and 6.80 μM for dopamine, epinephrine, and norepinephrine in artificial urine, respectively. For samples with unknown compositions, the pipeline first classifies the catecholamines present (92.19% group-level accuracy) and then quantifies single-component samples via intensity-ratio calibration and mixtures via trained partial least squares regression models (global root-mean-square error: 2.27 μM). This work establishes a functionalized SERS paper platform coupled with machine learning as a proof of concept for the identification and quantitative analysis of structurally similar metabolites in complex mixtures.

title: Revealing Cu–Mn Electronic Structure in Activated CuMn/Al2O3 Catalyst By Decoupling of Overlapping X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Spectra
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mn-promoted Cu-based catalysts demonstrate high efficiency and stability in various chemical processes, including methanol synthesis. XPS investigations of catalytic reactions and active catalytic centers in Cu–Mn-based catalysts face certain problems: it is challenging to determine the Mn oxidation state because of the strong overlap of Cu and Mn photoelectron and Auger spectra. In this study, a strict background subtraction based on a comprehensive set of standard samples as a reference was applied to separate the net Mn photoelectron spectra from the overlapping Cu signals, which reveals the Mn oxidation state with accurate quantitative analysis. Together with XAS, XRD, and HRTEM evidence, the results jointly support a strong Cu–Mn interaction and changes in their electronic states in the CuMn/Al2O3 catalyst during activation and passivation, providing new insights into the nature of the catalytic centers.

title: Dynamic Network Engineering of Soy Protein-Based Ionic Hydrogels via Freeze-Locking and Metal Coordination for Intelligent Human–Machine Interaction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous achievement of high ionic conductivity and mechanical robustness remains a fundamental challenge for conductive hydrogels, as excessive ionic species often disrupt polymer networks and compromise structural integrity. Herein, a dynamic network engineering strategy integrating PVA freeze-locking, reversible Fe3+ coordination, and ionic conduction is developed to construct a robust ionically conductive hydrogel (IL-PPM0.1-Fe) for intelligent wearable electronics. The freeze-locked PVA crystalline domains establish a rigid physical framework, while reversible Fe3+–MSPI coordination interactions contribute to network reinforcement and energy dissipation. Meanwhile, the incorporation of VBIMBr introduces imidazolium-containing ionic species into the hydrogel system. The resulting hydrogel achieves a tensile strength of approximately 1.5 MPa, a fracture strain of 673%, and an ionic conductivity of 16.2 S/m, while maintaining mechanical integrity over 500 tensile loading–unloading cycles at 100% strain. The sensor exhibits a strain sensing range of 1–500% (GF = 2.14), a pressure sensitivity of 0.21 kPa–1 at 0–1 kPa, and rapid response and recovery times of 230 and 192 ms, respectively. Furthermore, the hydrogel enables human motion monitoring, handwriting recognition, and proof-of-concept Morse-code-based human–machine interaction. This work demonstrates a promising strategy for combining mechanical robustness, ionic conduction, and multifunctional sensing in wearable electronics.

title: Light-Programmable Broad-Spectrum CPC-like Surfactants as Environmentally Benign Alternatives to Cationic Antimicrobial Agents
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs), particularly cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC), are widely employed as antimicrobial agents in personal care, hygiene, and pharmaceutical applications. However, the extensive and sustained use of CPC and related QACs has accelerated the emergence of microbial resistance, a consequence attributable in part to their exceptional chemical stability. In this work, we report a new class of photoactive CPC-like platforms (2a–l) featuring diverse structural motifs, including a sulfide linkage, that confer superior antimicrobial performance relative to legacy QACs. The most effective CPC-like surfactants (2b and 2k) exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including Streptococcus mutans, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of approximately 1–8 μg/mL. Furthermore, these surfactants generate type II reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon photochemical activation, supplementing the type I ROS produced by the pyridinium moiety. The critical micellar concentration (CMC) of these surfactants was, on average, one order of magnitude lower than that of CPC, an enhancement attributed to the presence of the sulfide motifs. Importantly, these sulfide moieties can be released as aroma or bioactive fragments upon induced photochemical degradation, providing a built-in mechanism for environmental remediation. This work offers a sustainable and multifunctional alternative to legacy QACs, effectively addressing their principal shortcomings of environmental persistence and ecological toxicity.

title: 2D Perovskite Seed-Mediated Crystallization Regulation for Stable and High-Performance Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract During low-temperature solution processing, the rapid crystallization of three-dimensional (3D) perovskites often lead to disordered nucleation and severe defects at surfaces and grain boundaries. Introducing 2D perovskite seeds into the precursor is an effective strategy for modulating the crystallization of 3D perovskites. However, the effects of 2D seeds on the chemical stability of perovskite precursors, as well as the mechanisms by which they regulate perovskite nucleation and crystal growth, remain unclear. Herein, 2D perovskite crystals (DFPD)2PbI4 are synthesized through a slow-cooling crystallization method and employed as seeds to regulate 3D perovskite crystallization. The results reveal that the regulatory effects of the 2D seeds extend across multiple stages of perovskite formation and establish a more favorable crystallization pathway. The 2D seeds facilitate nucleation by lowering the associated Gibbs free energy barrier while moderating subsequent crystal growth, thereby promoting the formation of larger grains and smoother perovskite films. The residual 2D phase interacts with the Pb–I framework through N–H⋯I hydrogen bonding and coordination with uncoordinated Pb2+, further passivating defects and establishing a favorable band alignment with the 3D perovskite. Consequently, the incorporation of 2D seeds enables carbon-based perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) to achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 17.39%, outperforming the control device. In addition, the presence of 2D seeds effectively suppresses colloidal aggregation and retards the formation of I3– species during precursor aging, contributing to improved precursor stability. The target C-PSCs without encapsulation maintain 90% of their original PCE after 40 days in ambient conditions, reflecting an enhanced operational long-term stability. This work reveals how the low-dimensional (LD) perovskite seed affects the 3D perovskite crystallization and offers a promising strategy for improved PCE and stable C-PSCs.

title: Solvent-Specific Surface Reconstruction Enables Robust CsPbBr3 Perovskite Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Inorganic perovskites boast exceptional thermal and environmental stability, rendering them attractive for transparent photovoltaics and tandem cells. However, conventional post-treatment approaches fail to generate low-dimensional surface layers capable of defect passivation on all-inorganic perovskite films. The fundamental mechanisms behind this limitation remain unclear, and reliable fabrication protocol to fabricate 2D/3D perovskite heterostructures remain largely underexplored. Herein, we develop a solvent-selective surface reconstruction strategy to construct 2D/3D CsPbBr3 perovskite heterostructures. This strategy incorporates trace coordinating solvents into passivation formulations in order to establish coordination interactions with undercoordinated surface lead sites, tune the surface chemical environment of CsPbBr3, and facilitate the spontaneous generation of the n = 1 Ruddlesden–Popper phase. With this strategy implemented, thermally evaporated CsPbBr3 perovskite films exhibit suppressed interfacial charge carrier recombination and optimized interfacial quality. The corresponding solar cells reach a power conversion efficiency of 9.927% and a remarkable open-circuit voltage of 1.654 V, ranking among the highest reported performance for evaporated CsPbBr3. More encouragingly, the resultant devices demonstrate outstanding stability under shelf storage and thermal aging conditions. This work opens a new pathway to fabricate 2D/3D heterostructures for all-inorganic perovskites.

title: Bacterial Extract with Immunomodulatory Properties Ameliorates DSS-Induced Colitis Partly by Inhibiting Ferroptosis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ulcerative colitis (UC) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder that affects the digestive tract. OM-85, a bacterial extract known for its immunomodulatory properties, has been investigated in this study for its potential therapeutic effects on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis. The study comprehensively evaluated inflammatory markers, mucosal integrity, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in colonic tissues. Additionally, the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins was analyzed using Western blotting, while immune cell populations were assessed through multiplexed immunohistochemistry. Oral administration of OM-85 significantly alleviated colitis symptoms in DSS-treated mice by reducing inflammation and tissue damage and by enhancing mucosal barrier integrity. Moreover, OM-85 treatment reduced ROS levels, suppressed the ferroptosis pathway, and restored the Th17/Treg balance in DSS-induced colitis. OM-85 treatment could partly ameliorate DSS-induced gut dysbiosis and regulate various metabolic pathways, including Th17 cell differentiation. By inhibiting the ferroptosis pathway in vitro, OM-85 could alleviate inflammation in LPS-stimulated NCM-460 cells. The results revealed that OM-85 administration could relieve colitis-associated symptoms through downregulating the ferroptosis pathway, which may provide a potential therapeutic option for UC.

title: Triple-Robust p -Aramid Copolymer Fibers via Comonomer Engineering: Concurrent Mechanical, Thermal, and Chemical Durability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Para-aramid (p-aramid) fibers have long been the benchmark for ballistic and structural protection owing to their outstanding tensile strength and energy-absorption capability. However, conventional aramid fibers have been predominantly optimized for mechanical loading, limiting their reliability under high-temperature and chemically aggressive environments typical of modern multi-threat defense applications. Addressing this limitation requires a molecular design strategy that balances mechanical performance with thermal and chemical durability. Herein, we report triple-robust p-aramid copolymer (p-AC) fibers engineered through comonomer engineering. 2,7′-Diaminofluorene (2,7′-DAF) was incorporated as a functional comonomer into a 3,4′-oxydianiline-based p-aramid backbone, where its rigid and planar molecular geometry promoted molecular orientation, crystallinity, and chain packing within the copolymer framework. The p-AC fibers maintain high tensile strengths of 2.8–3.3 GPa while achieving a tensile modulus of up to 98.3 GPa. Beyond mechanical performance, the fibers exhibit enhanced thermal and chemical durability, with tensile strength retention reaching up to 86% after thermal aging at 300 °C for 6 h and 70% after exposure to 60 wt % nitric acid for 6 h, surpassing those of commercial benchmark aramid fibers. This study establishes comonomer engineering as a scalable molecular design pathway for next-generation p-aramid fibers capable of reliable operation under coupled mechanical, thermal, and chemical stresses in multi-threat defense environments.

title: Rational Donor–Acceptor Design of Dye-Doped Conjugated Polymer Nanoparticles for Ratiometric Oxygen Sensing: Toward Hydrogel Platforms for Corneal Hypoxia Monitoring
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Corneal hypoxia, often induced by contact lens wear, is a precursor to severe ophthalmological pathologies. Early detection requires sensitive, noninvasive oxygen monitoring tools. We present a ratiometric optical oxygen sensor based on conjugated polymer nanoparticles (NP) of poly(fluorene-alt-benzothiadiazole) (F8BT) doped with platinum tetrabenzoporphyrin (BPPt). Spectral overlap between F8BT emission and BPPt absorption promotes efficient energy transfer to the porphyrin. Intersystem crossing then populates its triplet state (3BPPt*), whose phosphorescence is quenched by O2, whereas F8BT fluorescence is O2-insensitive and serves as the internal reference. The first design criterion concerns the choice of dopant: BPPt was selected because 3BPPt* lies energetically below 3F8BT* thereby limiting reverse triplet energy transfer and preserving BPPt phosphorescence. Monte Carlo simulations, constrained by two independent sets of experimental data, indicate that BPPt can deactivate the polymer by a second route that does not populate 3BPPt*. This led to a second design criterion: the doping level must be optimized for balanced dual emission, not for maximum energy transfer. The overall design yields a robust ratiometric sensor in aqueous suspension, with an estimated detection limit of 0.002 mM O2 and a reversible response over repeated O2/N2 cycling. Response times are practical (t90 < 20 s in hydrogel) and likely limited by mass transport. These sensor NP were incorporated into a poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (pHEMA) model hydrogel relevant to contact-lens materials. The hydrogel-sensor composite retained ratiometric oxygen-sensing capability and the model matrix remained transparent and swellable; preliminary non-ocular cell assays showed no detectable acute cytotoxicity under the conditions tested. These results establish proof of concept for preserving the sensor function after immobilization in a hydrated pHEMA matrix relevant to future corneal-oxygen-sensing studies.

title: A Metabolically Coupled Photochromic Protein AND-Gate for Living Materials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Engineered living materials (ELMs) capable of real-time logical operations would offer transformative opportunities for adaptive sensing and biosecurity. However, conventional synthetic biological logic gates rely heavily on transcriptional regulation, which results in sluggish responses, or depend on exogenous chemical reductants that compromise environmental safety and living autonomy. Here, we report an artificial metabolically coupled photochromic protein, engineered via combined site-specific unnatural amino acid incorporation and cysteine mutagenesis to reconfigure the chromophore microenvironment. At the protein level, this dual engineering is proposed to redirected excited-state energy dissipation from radiative decay toward nonradiative charge transfer, associated with enhancing photoreduction kinetics while enabling living bacteria to produce photochromic responses using intracellular reducing equivalents as “logical fuel”. At the living system level, combining this protein with an intracellular “metabolic clearance” mechanism established a precise “Logic 0” state. By integrating the engineered bacteria into 3D-bioprintable hydrogel matrices, we demonstrated a “metabolic–physical” dual-locking platform, in which encrypted visual data remains hidden under the tested conditions unless simultaneously triggered by specific illumination and metabolic substrate supply. This work links cellular metabolic state with optical responsiveness, offering a approach for designing living materials that combine rapid response with information security.

title: Proximal single atoms for stable electrocatalysts
abstract: Ru–O–Cr motifs atomically dispersed in proximity on a MnO2 substrate effectively suppress oxidation-induced Ru dissolution with enhanced catalyst durability towards the oxygen evolution reaction in acidic water electrolysers.

title: Three-Dimensional COF/rGO/AuNP Porous Membranes for Enrichment-Enhanced Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering Detection of Aldehydes in Exhaled Breath
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, highlighting the need for noninvasive approaches for early disease screening. Volatile aldehydes in exhaled breath have emerged as promising biomarkers because their concentrations may reflect disease-associated metabolic changes; however, their low abundance and inefficient interaction with SERS substrates remain challenging for reliable breath analysis. Herein, a three-dimensional porous membrane composed of covalent organic framework/reduced graphene oxide/gold nanoparticles (COF/rGO/AuNP) was developed as a SERS substrate for sensitive detection of volatile aldehydes in exhaled breath. The membrane was functionalized with 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) for selective aldehyde capture through Schiff-base formation. The combination of COF-mediated gas enrichment and electromagnetic enhancement from AuNPs enabled ultrasensitive aldehyde detection, with a detection limit of 0.28 ppb for benzaldehyde. The platform exhibited excellent selectivity, signal uniformity, reproducibility, and resistance to humidity interference. Its practical applicability was demonstrated by analyzing exhaled breath samples from healthy volunteers and patients with lung cancer, revealing distinct differences in aldehyde concentration profiles between the two groups. This work provides a simple and sensitive membrane-based SERS platform for trace gaseous aldehyde analysis and demonstrates its potential for noninvasive breath-based lung cancer screening.

title: Antimetastatic Sulfonate-Functionalized Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Enhance Irinotecan Stability and Delivery for Colorectal Cancer Treatment
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with irinotecan (IRI) serving as a backbone chemotherapeutic despite its dose-limiting toxicities, instability of the active lactone form, and lack of intrinsic antimetastatic activity. To overcome these barriers, we developed sulfonate-functionalized mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs), referred to as (SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA, as a multifunctional nanocarrier for IRI delivery. This nanoformulation markedly enhanced drug loading efficiency and preserved over 90% of IRI in its lactone form for up to six months, enabling sustained release and improved pharmacological stability. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient nanoparticle internalization, while IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA enhanced apoptosis and reduced the IC50 compared with free IRI. Beyond drug delivery, (SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA exhibited intrinsic antimetastatic activity associated with modulation of focal adhesion kinase/paxillin signaling and impaired tumor cell adhesion and migration. The nanoparticles also exhibited efficient tumor accumulation through the enhanced permeability and retention effect. Pharmacokinetic analysis further revealed that IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA prolonged systemic retention, maintaining approximately threefold higher IRI plasma concentrations than free IRI. IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA significantly inhibited both primary tumor growth and metastatic dissemination in orthotopic and heterotopic colorectal cancer models, while markedly reducing systemic toxicities and preserving bone marrow cellularity relative to free IRI and liposomal IRI (Onivyde). Transcriptomic profiling further revealed attenuation of extracellular matrix/mesenchymal remodeling and hypoxia/vascular-associated programs, providing molecular support for the observed antimetastatic phenotype. Consistently, reduced vascular endothelial growth factor expression and tumor-associated angiogenesis were observed in the chorioallantoic membrane model. Tumor immune-cell profiling was also performed to assess potential changes in major tumor-associated immune-cell populations. This dual-functional nanomedicine therefore provides an innovative therapeutic strategy that not only augments IRI efficacy but also confers metastasis suppression and favorable pharmacokinetics, addressing critical unmet needs in mCRC treatment. These findings highlight the translational potential of IRI@(SO3–)-MSN-PEG/TA as a safer and more effective therapeutic strategy for mCRC.

title: Fe3+ Post-Coordination-Locked Polyaryl Ether-Based Aerogels for Solar-Driven Interfacial Evaporation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Water-processable polymers are ideal materials for solar-driven interfacial evaporation (SDIE) due to their advantages in homogeneous processing and oriented molding. However, their inherently high hydrophilicity makes them highly susceptible to swelling or dissolution during operation. Here, we resolve the trade-off between processability and stability by employing a post-coordination locking strategy with Fe3+ in sulfonated poly(phthalazinone ether sulfone ketone) (SPPESK)-based aerogels. Polydopamine-coated molybdenum disulfide (PDA@MoS2) was introduced as a photothermal component, and vertically aligned water-conducting channels were constructed using directional freezing technology. Fe3+ was subsequently introduced to stabilize the prefabricated scaffold. The resulting aerogel maintained its structural integrity even after 192 h of immersion in water. The surface temperature of the aerogel reached 75 °C, with an evaporation rate of 2.4 kg m–2 h–1 and an energy utilization efficiency of 97.3% under one-sun irradiance. Its evaporation performance remained stable even after repeated cycling tests, and the evaporation flux could still reach 1.1 kg m–2 h–1 even under overcast conditions. This ‘build-then-lock’ strategy provides a viable solution for polyaryl ether-based, striking a balance between water treatment performance and operational stability.

title: Anion-Immobilizing Poly(ionic liquid) Copolymer Electrolytes for Flame-Retardant Lithium Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer electrolytes have emerged as promising alternatives for next-generation (quasi-) solid-state lithium metal batteries (LMBs), owing to their intrinsic safety, mechanical flexibility, and good processability. Nevertheless, their practical application is severely impeded by low room-temperature ionic conductivity and insufficient Li+ transport arising from sluggish polymer segmental dynamics. Herein, we design a thin (∼57 μm) poly(ionic liquid)-based copolymer electrolyte (CPIL) via copolymerization of 1-vinyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide and methyl methacrylate, which is integrated with a PVDF-HFP matrix and EMIMTFSI plasticizer. The incorporation of poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) endows the electrolyte with high flame retardancy, excellent thermal stability, and superior ionic conductivity (0.524 mS cm–1). Benefiting from the anion anchoring units of PIL, the Li+ transference number is significantly increased to 0.65, thereby enhancing Li+ transport efficiency and inducing even Li deposition on the anode surface. Consequently, the Li|CPIL-2|Li batteries display stable plating/stripping over 2000 h with low polarization of ∼75 mV at 0.1 mA cm–2. The Li|LiFePO4 batteries with CPIL-2 exhibit high-rate performance and long-term cycling stability, with a capacity retention of 65.3% at 0.5 C after 400 cycles. Beyond these, Li|CPIL-2|LiFePO4 pouch cells continue to light LEDs even after cutting and folding, highlighting the potential applications of CPIL for high-energy-density and safety LMBs.

title: Aqueous π‐Hole Interactions Enabled by Chiral Perfluoroarene Amphiphiles
abstract: ABSTRACT Arene‐perfluoroarene (AP) interactions, as a representative class of π‐hole‐driven noncovalent interactions, have demonstrated unique advantages in molecular recognition and supramolecular assembly. However, the precise regulation of hydrophobic aromatic molecules in aqueous environments through AP interactions remains challenging. Herein, we designed and constructed a series of chiral perfluoroarene amphiphiles based on an octafluoronaphthalene scaffold, in which the amphiphilicity, self‐assembly behavior, and confined microenvironment were regulated through end‐group engineering, enabling selective recognition and photophysical modulation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). These perfluoroarene amphiphiles readily formed stable lamellar vesicular assemblies in aqueous solution. The π‐hole region of the perfluoroarene moiety interacted with PAHs through AP interactions, facilitating the incorporation of guest molecules into the confined lamellar domains. Consequently, a variety of hydrophobic PAHs were successfully encapsulated in aqueous media, accompanied by effective modulation of their excited‐state behaviors. Moreover, the chiral confined microenvironment induced chiroptical responses from achiral PAHs, enabling efficient chirality transfer. This work provides a new design strategy for aqueous supramolecular recognition, aromatic guest aggregation regulation, and the construction of chiral photofunctional materials based on AP interactions.

title: Enantioselective Coupling of 1,3‐Dienes and Vinyl Acetate for the Synthesis of Succinic Acids and β‐ and γ‐Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalyzed by cationic cobalt(I) complexes, [( L *)Co] + [X] − , 1,3‐dienes and vinyl carboxylates, two readily accessible electron‐rich class of substrates, undergo highly regio‐ and enantioselective heterodimerization giving skipped 1,4‐dienes with two configurationally defined, electronically differentiated double bonds flanking the newly formed stereogenic center (er typically >96:4). Among the numerous chelating bis ‐phosphine and phosphino‐oxazoline ligands, commercially available P ‐centered chiral ligand, (2 S , 2’ S , 3 S , 3’ S )‐MeO‐BIBOP incorporating a dibenzooxaphophole scaffold was found to be uniquely suited to give high yields and excellent regio‐ and enantioselectivities. Notably, in these additions, vinyl acetate serves as an acetaldehyde enolate surrogate. Configurations of the double bonds and of the stereogenic center were established by the crystal structure of the adduct from vinyl ester of ( S )‐naproxen and ( E )‐1,3‐nonadiene. The reaction has wide scope in both the 1,3‐dienes and a surprisingly broad array of highly functionalized vinyl esters, including vinyl sorbate, vinyl α ‐chloroacetate, vinyl methacrylate, vinyl α‐phenyl acrylate, and vinyl esters of α ‐amino acids. Functional groups, such as bromide, aldehyde, and vinyl groups, are tolerated in the vinyl esters. The coupling products carry multiple latent functionalities enabling their facile conversions to several useful classes of compounds, among them, chiral succinic acids, β‐ and γ‐amino acids, and 4‐alkyl γ‐butyrolactams.

title: Single Chiroptical Pulse in Non‐Equilibrium Supramolecular Systems via Inter‐Macrocyclic Crosstalk
abstract: ABSTRACT Can an autonomous triphasic temporal pulse emerge in supramolecular architectures without relying on chemical transformations or external chemical fuel? Here, we demonstrate sequential chiroptical sign reversals in a time‐dependent, aperiodic circular dichroism waveform excursion governed purely by non‐covalent binding kinetics in a dual‐receptor network of pillar[5]arene and prism[5]arene. Challenging an established chiral equilibrium with an antipodal alanine derivative induces an out‐of‐equilibrium optical pulse that inverts the chiroptical sign before settling into a persistent state. This transient behavior originates from the synergy between mismatched macrocyclic binding/unbinding rates and ultra‐fast racemization of planar chirality during competitive ligand exchange, as verified by time‐resolved spectroscopy and kinetic modeling. Tailoring receptor substituents and component ratios enables straightforward regulation over both duration and amplitude of the transient response. By establishing indirect intermolecular signal relays through shared effectors, this work provides a transformative blueprint for engineering dissipative systems‐level dynamics in non‐reactive, life‐like materials.

title: Engineered Pore Bisection by a Cymbal‐Shaped Cycloaliphatic Pillar in a Zn‐Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework (MOF) for Selective CO 2 Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Physisorbents combining ultramicroporosity, high CO 2 affinity, and humidity tolerance remain a challenge in carbon‐capture materials. MOFs based on flexible Zn‐triazolate layers have emerged as a promising platform; however, balancing pore size, confinement, and regeneration remains nontrivial. Here we introduce a new pillared‐layer MOF, ZnTzBCP, constructed from Zn 2 + cations, 1,2,4‐triazolate (Tz) linkers, and the 3‐dimensional cycloaliphatic bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane‐1,3‐dicarboxylate (BCP) linker. Liquid‐assisted mechanochemical grinding affords a crystalline material in which the rigid BCP pillars with a cymbal‐shaped core bisect the pore space into symmetric twin ultramicropores with dimensions commensurate with the CO 2 kinetic diameter. Combined PXRD/PW‐DFT/Rietveld analysis integrated with gas sorption, calorimetry, and CO 2 ‐loaded structural refinement reveals reversible, guest‐responsive flexibility of the Zn‐Tz layers through anisotropic swelling of the MOF with CO 2 molecules generating multiple cooperative C─H···O interactions with both ligands and yielding high adsorption enthalpies of 41 kJ/mol. These properties are retained in a PVDF composite, which demonstrates stable, cyclic CO 2 capture under humid breakthrough conditions with minimal thermal regeneration (333 K) and outstanding selectivity for CO 2 over nitrogen of 226. These findings position the linkers with a cymbal‐shaped core as powerful pore‐controlling elements for the design of ultramicroporous MOFs capable of selective CO 2 capture under operative conditions.

title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantio‐ and Regioselective Addition of Silicon and Boron Nucleophiles to Methylene Cyclobutene for the Construction of Quaternary Stereocenters
abstract: ABSTRACT A nickel‐catalyzed enantio‐ and regioselective addition of silicon and boron nucleophiles to the 1,3‐diene unit of methylene cyclobutenes is reported. Si─B and B─B reagents serve as silicon and boron pronucleophiles, respectively. Notably, this protocol not only constitutes the unprecedented catalytic asymmetric synthesis of cyclobutanes containing a stereogenic, silicon‐substituted quaternary carbon atom but also provides an efficient access to their boron‐substituted analogs. The transformation proceeds with excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee) and regioisomeric ratios (up to r.r. > 20:1). The substrate scope is broad, and the resulting silicon‐ and boron‐substituted products can be engaged in diverse downstream functional‐group manipulations, underscoring the synthetic utility of this methodology.

title: Thorium and Uranium Cyaphido and Pnictaethynolato Complexes
abstract: ABSTRACT The synthesis of a homologous series of tris(hexamethyldisilazide) thorium(IV) and uranium(IV) complexes bearing phosphaethynolate (OCP), arsaethynolate (OCAs), and cyaphide (CP) ligands is reported.
