title: Single-cell genomics reveals genome streamlining and functional traits in dominant uncultured marine protists
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Marine protists are key players in marine ecosystems, yet a large fraction, particularly among the smallest taxa, belongs to uncultured lineages lacking genomic data, limiting our understanding of their ecology and evolution. Beyond determining their gene repertoires, genomic information is essential to reveal how genomes are organized. Features such as genome size, GC content, and structural gene architecture represent physical constraints that shape evolutionary fitness and adaptability in marine environments. Here, we present a genomic catalog of 147 marine picoplanktonic protist species, greatly expanding the genomic representation of uncultured and ecologically relevant lineages through a single-cell approach. This dataset enables refined phylogenomic placement of previously uncharacterized marine eukaryotes, including abundant marine protistan players as well as a few species belonging to novel or poorly known groups that are crucial for resolving deep questions in eukaryotic evolution. We uncover pronounced genome streamlining in ecologically successful lineages, coupled with extensive, mostly lineage-specific functional adaptations. At a broader scale, we identify functional traits enriched independently across several marine eukaryotic lineages, including genes involved in complex carbohydrate degradation in heterotrophic organisms and the presence of polyketide synthases. Together, these results provide a framework for investigating the genomic drivers and molecular mechanisms behind the ecological success of marine eukaryotic microbes.

title: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
High-nickel cathodes provide high capacity in lithium-ion batteries; however, their slow lithiation reactions require a prolonged high-temperature hold during synthesis which is directly responsible for high manufacturing cost. Here, we report that the precursor morphology and crystallinity can be engineered to regulate the nucleation and growth of the layered phase at temperatures as low as 575 °C. We use nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH)
                    2
                    with high specific surface areas to maximize the contact area between Li and Ni precursors and to shorten Li
                    +
                    diffusion lengths. Highly crystalline NiO seeds early and uniform layered phase nucleation at low temperatures. Preheating Ni(OH)
                    2
                    to NiO at 300 °C maintains the large surface area and yields a higher layered fraction with limited lamellae coarsening. Preheating at 500 °C produces more crystalline NiO seeds that promote the synchronous Ni oxidation and cation ordering upon layered phase formation to deliver higher discharge capacity and better rate capability than conventionally synthesized LiNiO
                    2
                    . In contrast, along the hydroxide-based route, in situ generated Li
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    disrupts wetting and hampers lithiation, ultimately trapping lithium within a disordered rocksalt intermediate. This work demonstrates that precursor morphology, crystallinity, and processing temperature control lithiation kinetics, providing broad guidance for energy-efficient synthesizing advanced oxide battery cathodes.

title: Sea-fishing cultures show rare blend of tight social ties and openness to strangers
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Research has linked cultural differences to historical subsistence styles, but most studies have focused on farming or herding. Sea fishing is a major subsistence style, yet we know much less about whether fishing shapes culture. We propose an explanation for why fishing has received less attention—its cultural patterns do not fit neatly into the individualism-collectivism dichotomy that has been so useful in studies of farming and herding. First, we tested 1,010 people from nearby regions in Japan as a more controlled comparison. Then we tested the generalizability of the findings across 150 contemporary nations and historical records from 1,265 ethnic groups worldwide. People from fishing regions think holistically and emphasize responsibilities in close relationships more than people in nonfishing cultures (culture level
                    d
                    = 0.91). These characteristics are more common in collectivistic cultures and may have been adaptive for cooperation in dangerous seas. However, they show less ingroup loyalty and less outgroup discrimination (
                    d =
                    1.37), which is more similar to individualistic cultures. Openness to outsiders may have been adaptive for fishing’s mobility and flexible labor networks. We address reverse causality by running instrumental variable analyses using data on environmental suitability for fishing. To pinpoint fishing, we compare regions that have coastlines, some by seas that support large fish populations and others that support few fish. Results show access to the ocean, trade, or transportation are not linked to these cultural differences. Finally, the cultural patterns do not extend to freshwater fishing, which has different demands from sea fishing.

title: Anterior cingulate cortex neurons parse speakers in a natural cocktail party
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The cocktail party problem—parsing relevant voices from competing speakers—has traditionally been studied as a sensory challenge for auditory cortex. Yet in natural communication, identifying speakers and coordinating interaction are inherently social processes. Here we recorded single neurons from anterior cingulate cortex (ACC, area 24) in freely moving marmosets engaged in spontaneous vocal exchanges within a noisy colony environment. ACC neurons selectively encoded vocalizations from a social partner versus other callers in the scene, effectively parsing speakers in the acoustic mixture. This selectivity was preserved even when vocalizations overlapped in time, indicating robustness to background interference. Apart from perception, ACC population activity represented vocal production, call type, and whether calls occurred within vocal turn-taking exchanges. Behaviorally, marmosets adjusted vocal timing based on the surrounding acoustic scene, and these interaction contexts were reliably reflected in ACC activity. Together, these findings suggest that neurons in ACC play a role in parsing conspecific speakers during communication in a natural “cocktail party,” linking auditory scene analysis with social monitoring and coordinated interactions.

title: Evidence for patterns of colonization risk in the nationwide hospitalized patient network in France
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Patient movement within and between hospitals creates a complex hospital network that facilitates the spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and contributes to healthcare-associated infections. Yet most national-scale studies infer spread from aggregated hospital-to-hospital patient sharing, leaving patient-to-patient contact pathways and the role of routine patient mobility in shaping colonization risk poorly characterized. Using France’s 2023–2024 national hospital-discharge data, we reconstructed a temporal patient-based network of 10.4 million patients across 1,408 acute-care hospitals, comprising 326.6 million overnight ward colocation interactions. We simulated colonization over 365 d on the observed day-by-day temporal network using a stochastic susceptible–colonized–susceptible model, with a mean colonization duration of 180 d. We used national carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) surveillance data to calibrate differences in transmission risk across clinical settings. Across 2,000 simulations initiated on randomly selected dates in 2023, we calculated patient-level colonization probabilities and summarized risk across patients’ residential areas, wards, and hospitals. We further assessed hospital-level consistency between simulated risk and recorded CPE occurrence. Simulated risk was highly heterogeneous across patients and care settings. When mapped by place of residence, hospital-associated colonization risk showed strong spatial clustering in both urban and rural areas. Multivariable regression analyses identified patient- and hospital-level characteristics associated with heterogeneity in simulated colonization risk. Sensitivity analyses varying initial seeding and colonization duration showed that relative risk patterns remained highly stable. This nationwide framework shows how patient mobility and ward colocation patterns can reveal patterns of hospital-associated colonization risk and could support pathogen-specific surveillance and intervention evaluation.

title: Microbially driven iron redox chemistry unlocks phosphorus reservoirs in oxygenated soils
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Biological phosphorus (P) mobilization is generally attributed to proton- and ligand-driven dissolution of mineral P, enzymatic hydrolysis of organic P, and, under anoxic conditions, reductive release of phosphate from Fe(III) minerals. Here, we show that extracellular metabolites released by diverse Gram-positive bacteria sustain Fe(III) reduction under oxic conditions, releasing mineral-associated phosphate. The resulting Fe(II) reacts with O
                    2
                    to generate reactive oxygen species that activate organic P. This redox pathway was observed across diverse aerobic bacteria and agricultural soils and increased plant-available P. These findings establish aerobic microbial Fe redox chemistry as a previously overlooked route for returning otherwise inaccessible P to bioavailable pools, with implications for reactivating legacy P in agricultural soils.

title: Targeted metabolic reprogramming of CD8 T cells restores immune regulation in lupus
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by pathogenic humoral autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking T cell dysfunction to aberrant B cell responses remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a CD8
                    +
                    T cell–intrinsic metabolic defect that promotes humoral immune dysregulation in lupus. CD8
                    +
                    T cells from patients with SLE exhibited elevated CD38 expression associated with reduced intracellular NAD
                    +
                    levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired cytotoxic capacity. Pharmacologic inhibition of CD38 with the small-molecule inhibitor MK-0159 restored NAD
                    +
                    metabolism and rescued cytotoxic function in human CD8
                    +
                    T cells ex vivo. To selectively target this pathway in vivo, we developed anti-CD8 antibody-conjugated nanoparticles encapsulating MK-0159. In lupus-prone MRL/
                    lpr
                    mice, CD8-targeted delivery enhanced granzyme B expression, improved degranulation, reduced plasmablast responses and autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and renal pathology. Importantly, targeted delivery restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell function without broad immune perturbation. These findings identify CD38-driven NAD
                    +
                    depletion as a reversible immunometabolic checkpoint limiting CD8
                    +
                    T cell cytotoxic competence and support a model in which targeted restoration of cytotoxic fitness contributes to the control of humoral autoimmunity in SLE.

title: Cognitive diversity and majority rule
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Societies rely on groups–boards, panels, committees, and representative bodies–to make important decisions for good reason: overwhelming evidence shows groups usually make more accurate choices than individuals. The predominant logic for group accuracy rests on reasoning formulated in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, which states that if voters receive independent and equally accurate generated signals, majority rule produces decisions that i) are more accurate than the average voter, ii) improve in individual accuracy and iii) group size, and iv) approach perfect accuracy as group size becomes large. An alternative logic based on interpreted signals explains the accuracy of majority rule as arising from the aggregation of diverse mental models. Group accuracy results from the same state of the world being classified differently by different people. In this framework, the set of possible group accuracies can be characterized conditional on average individual accuracy and average pairwise diversity. Majority rule groups are only guaranteed to outperform their members when diversity is high. Using data from a variety of empirical settings, along with simulations of a minimal nearest-neighbor model, we find much stronger support for the predictions of the interpreted signals framework than for the standard generated signals model. We further show empirical evidence for a diversity–accuracy paradox, in which more diverse groups are less accurate unless average individual accuracy is nearly constant across groups. Our findings have important implications for group composition and institutional and organizational design as well as for the potential gains from deliberation.

title: Phosphorylation-dependent ATPase activity regulates subunit shuffling dynamics in cyanobacterial circadian clock proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Protein complexes are essential for cellular functions, with their dynamics increasingly recognized as key regulatory elements. In the cyanobacterial circadian clock, the KaiC hexamer is highly dynamic, undergoing phosphorylation-dependent monomer shuffling that synchronizes individual oscillators. However, the molecular mechanism of monomer shuffling is not fully understood. Here we combine a chromatography-based method with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to quantify subunit exchange in the hexamerization domain of KaiC (KaiC-CI) and in full-length KaiC. We show that ATPase activity is essential for monomer shuffling. Through quantitative modeling of experimental data, we found that adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis at two independent monomer–monomer interfaces disassembles a KaiC-CI hexamer into two oligomers. Two complementary oligomers from two different hexamers can rapidly reform a mixed hexamer. Mechanistically, ATP hydrolysis induces unstable, shuffling-competent states in hexamers, while nucleotide exchange stabilizes them, suppressing shuffling. The balance between these two processes quantitatively explains the relationship between shuffling rate and ATPase activity across KaiC mutants observed in our experiments. Applying this model to full-length KaiC revealed that phosphorylation of the KaiC-CII domain modulates shuffling primarily by affecting the nucleotide exchange rate in the CI domain. This establishes a feedback loop where CII phosphorylation alters CI ATPase activity, which in turn controls subunit exchange to synchronize CII phosphorylation across the KaiC hexamer population. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework linking ATPase-driven subunit exchange to the robustness of circadian clocks, with implications for activation-coupled dynamics in other molecular machines.

title: Gaussian mixture model–based focused refinement for enhanced flexible structure determination in CryoEM and CryoET
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Dynamic conformational changes of proteins are crucial for their cellular functions. Here we present a unified refinement pipeline for flexible protein structures in both CryoEM and in situ CryoET. Using a Gaussian mixture model–based focused alignment procedure, we improve resolution of small domains in highly dynamic proteins and reveal intricate conformational changes. The method corrects the per-subunit motion of TRPV1 and captures the rotary dynamics of ATP synthase within mitochondria.

title: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Photolysis of nitrous acid (HONO) drives ozone and secondary aerosol formation, yet its sources remain poorly constrained. We identify HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a previously overlooked plant-derived component of terrestrial HONO emissions. Field observations and dual-isotope (
                    15
                    N–
                    18
                    O) tracing reveal that HONO arises mainly from nitrate reduction within decomposing plants. We integrated global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate to estimate HONO emissions from vegetation decay at 1.1 ± 0.1 Tg N y
                    −1
                    . This substantially narrows the long-standing uncertainty in HONO budget. This plant-mediated pathway extends the soil-atmosphere paradigm to soil-plant-atmosphere framework. Moreover, we identify emission hotspots and drivers, assess their climate-driven shifts, and propose region-specific mitigation strategies. These findings uncover a missing link between terrestrial nitrogen cycling and atmospheric reactivity, highlighting biogeochemical controls on air quality.

title: Glycosaminoglycans in the structures of Aβ42 amyloid fibrils purified from mouse brains
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has revealed the structures of the ordered cores of amyloid fibrils assembled in vitro and isolated from diseased tissue. Many of the ex vivo amyloid structures contain low-resolution density adjacent to the protein core, often attributed to nonproteinaceous ligands, yet their identity has remained unresolved. Here, we characterize such density in distinct polymorphs of Aβ fibrils purified from the brains of homozygous
                    
                      App
                      NL-F
                    
                    and
                    
                      App
                      NL-G-F
                    
                    knock-in mouse models of Alzheimer’s disease. In
                    
                      App
                      NL-G-F
                    
                    fibrils, which are built from the Arctic Aβ variant (E22G), we use immunogold labeling, immunofluorescence microscopy, and cryo-EM to identify the density as the glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) hyaluronic acid and chondroitin sulfate. These GAGs bind to an exposed positively charged patch on the Aβ
                    42
                    fibril surface, forming an intimate peptide-GAG copolymer through stacking interactions with the amyloid core. In
                    
                      App
                      NL-F
                    
                    fibrils the predominant polymorph (~ 85% of particles) is glycan-free, with the relevant side chains identified in the
                    
                      App
                      NL-G-F
                    
                    fibrils being buried within the
                    
                      App
                      NL-F
                    
                    fibril core. Formation of the glycan-binding site in a rare polymorph hence involves conformational rearrangement to create the required binding surface. Our findings reveal a structural basis for GAG incorporation into brain-derived amyloid fibrils and highlight amyloid-associated ligands as potential therapeutic targets in protein aggregation disorders.

title: Gap test–inspired crack-parallel tension tests of fracture of soft-knitted polymer composites simulated by microplane triads
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Soft composites are increasingly used in wearable and soft robotic systems, as advances in material architecture enable greater damage tolerance under large deformation. In these mesoscale architectures, the crack-parallel stresses modify the crack initiation and growth in the opening-mode fracture. Emulating the gap test, we introduce a fracture test to quantify how the superposed crack-parallel tension affects the maximum load (i.e., the load capacity) and the load-deflection curve. A Mode I (opening mode) center-notched tensioned strip is used because its advantages in generating crack-parallel tension outweigh its hypothetical disadvantages with possible instability of crack jumps at two competing crack fronts. We develop and experimentally validate a continuum model that captures the nonlinear behavior and progressive damage of knitted composites. To this end, we introduce an ensemble of oriented microplane triads tangential to the yarn at characteristic points of the yarn loop within a repetitive unit cell of the knit. The triads ensure the yarn-polymer transfer of all normal and shear stress components at each characteristic point. The experimentally calibrated computational model provides a tool to predict the effect of crack-parallel tension on the changes of load capacity and of the effective fracture energy of knitted polymer composites, enabling rational design of these composites in engineering applications such as wearables and soft robotics.

title: Airborne microbial diversity over Greenlandic and Antarctic plateaus reflects divergent atmospheric connectivity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The polar plateaus are among the most remote environments on Earth. Despite their extreme conditions, these cold deserts on the Greenland and Antarctic Ice Sheets harbor microbial life in snow, ice, and air. However, knowledge of polar airborne microbiomes remains scarce and methodological differences have hindered bipolar comparisons. Here, we present a systematic survey of airborne bacterial and eukaryotic communities across Greenlandic and Antarctic Plateaus, using standardized sampling and genetic techniques, coupled with atmospheric physics and advanced statistical analyses. We found that Antarctic airborne communities are characterized by low diversity and high homogeneity, whereas Greenlandic communities are richer, more variable, and more connected to coastal-marine zones. Our results indicate that atmospheric isolation, together with short-term atmospheric variables, is associated with differences in the microbial biogeography of each Plateau. Compared with Antarctica, the Greenlandic Plateau is more frequently influenced by air masses from outside the plateau over long timescales and exhibits more variable short-term air back-trajectories, reflecting enhanced microbial dispersal and diversity. These findings highlight the potential of polar plateaus as observational platforms for airborne microbial diversity, where sustained and temporally resolved sampling could help assess variations in community composition associated with atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic influence under global change.

title: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Meiotic recombination reshuffles genetic diversity through reciprocal DNA exchanges between chromosomes known as crossovers. In most eukaryotes, crossovers are highly constrained in both frequency and distribution, leaving large genomic regions with little or no recombination. A notable exception is the
                    Brassica
                    AAC allotriploid hybrid obtained from a cross between allotetraploid
                    Brassica napus
                    (AACC) and diploid
                    Brassica rapa
                    (AA), which exhibits elevated recombination and crossover formation near centromeres. Here, we generated a CCA allotriploid hybrid from a cross between
                    B. napus
                    and
                    Brassica oleracea
                    (CC), and subsequently produced AAC allotriploids by crossing the CCA hybrid with
                    B. rapa
                    . Both CCA and AAC allotriploids exhibit similar meiotic deregulation, demonstrating that this phenomenon is not restricted to AAC hybrids. Both systems displayed a marked increase in crossover frequency within normally low-recombining chromosome regions, reaching 9.4-fold in AAC and 13.4-fold in CCA allotriploids. Alternating CCA and AAC allotriploids efficiently reshuffled both
                    B. napus
                    subgenomes within only two generations. Using genetic mapping and cytogenetics, we further identified homoeologous exchanges. Remarkably, crossovers occurring on chromosomes involved in homoeologous associations exhibited a more pronounced redistribution toward nonrecombining regions than those on homologously paired chromosomes. Moreover, the frequency of homoeologous associations varied with the diploid progenitor genotype, indicating that genetic factors controlling homoeologous recombination already exist in
                    Brassica
                    diploids. Altogether, our results identify allotriploidy as a simple and powerful strategy to unlock recombination deserts, which harbor 21% of total resistance gene analogs, and provide insights into its potential role in allopolyploid evolution, adaptation, and speciation.

title: Frontispiece: Active‐Site Photothermal Energy Utilization in PET Depolymerization
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: Photothermal catalysis depends not only on heat generation, but also on the efficiency of energy delivery to active sites of the catalyst (Pd). In the Research Article e2844693, Yiming Bu, Jingliang Li, and co-workers reveal the critical role of the local thermal environment at active sites in PET depolymerization. These findings highlight effective active-site temperature, rather than bulk temperature, as a key factor for photothermal catalysis.

title: Ultrasound Rechargeable Bioelectronics With Acoustic Metamaterial‐Enhanced Triboelectric Energy Harvesting
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Wireless transcutaneous energy transfer to deep‐tissue bioelectronic implants remains challenging for long‐term autonomous bioelectronic operation because tissue attenuation limits the available acoustic excitation. Here, we present a proof‐of‐concept ultrasound rechargeable bioelectronic platform that integrates spatially confined acoustic energy delivery, energy harvesting, power management, and programmable electrical stimulation. A non‐resonant, transmissive acoustic metamaterial reshapes the incident ultrasound wavefront to form a localized field in the receiving region. The platform couples this acoustic structure with a compliant thin‐film triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for energy harvesting in a fluidic environment. An on‐board power conditioning circuit regulates the harvested energy to support recharging and controlled electrical pulse delivery. In ex vivo evaluations using a layered porcine‐tissue configuration, approximately 3.5 min of ultrasonic recharging supports nearly 16 h of programmed pulse generation into a 5 kΩ surrogate load, corresponding to an acoustic charging duty cycle of 0.36%. The stored energy also powered electrical pulses that evoked repeatable limb movement in ex vivo frog preparations. These results demonstrate a system‐level strategy for ultrasound‐rechargeable bioelectronics, providing a basis for future implantable neuromodulation systems.

title: Correction to “A Robust Au─C≡C Functionalized Surface: Toward Real‐Time Mapping and Accurate Quantification of Fe2+ in the Brains of Live AD Mouse Models”
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: C. Zhang, Z. Liu, L. Zhang, et al., “A Robust Au─C≡C Functionalized Surface: Toward Real-Time Mapping and Accurate Quantification of Fe2+ in the Brains of Live AD Mouse Models,” Angewandte Chemie International Edition 59 (2020): 20499-20507, https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202006318. During post-publication review, the following errors were identified: In Figure 5A, the images for the striatum under 30 µM CdCl2 were inadvertently misassembled. In Figure 5E, the amplicon sizes were incorrectly labeled. The correct sizes are 148 bp for NR1, 140 bp for CREB, and 76 bp for β-actin. In Figure 5E,G, the RT-PCR bands labeled as “p-CREB” should be corrected to “CREB,” because RT-PCR detects mRNA and cannot distinguish phosphorylated CREB. The text describing Figure 2I should read 28.3 ± 3.2%. The text describing Figure 3D should read 30 mM for the TPM concentration. The corrected version of Figure 5 is provided below: We apologize for these errors.

title: Direct Organozirconium‐Catalyzed Copolymerization of Propylene with Phosphino‐Olefins: Access to Isotactic Phosphine‐Functionalized Polypropylenes for Diverse Functions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient development of functionalized polypropylenes is of fundamental scientific and technological interest but has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the efficient synthesis of a phosphine‐functionalized isotactic polypropylene (PFiPP) series via direct propylene – phosphino‐alkene copolymerization, mediated by the activated ansa ‐bis(indenyl)zirconium catalyst, rac ‐Me 2 Si(indenyl) 2 ZrR + /B(C 6 F 5 ) 4 − . The copolymerizations are highly efficient and selective, with 25°C turnover frequencies up to 2940 kg/(mol·h·atm) with 2.0 mol% phosphine incorporation, and high product isotacticity (96% mmmm ). The high stereoregularity reflects experimentally‐ and DFT‐identified steric and electronic effects imposed by the C 2 ‐symmetric catalyst which mediates enantioselective olefin insertion into the Zr–C bond to promote stereoregular chain propagation. These phosphine‐functionalized isotactic polypropylenes serve as effective PdCl 2 ligands for high‐activity Suzuki‐Miyaura cross‐coupling catalysis with negligible metal leaching. Regarding interfacial properties, aluminum adhesion measurements reveal that phosphine incorporation significantly enhances PFiPP shear strength versus that of pristine isotactic iPP by six‐fold.

title: A Climate‐Adaptive Window Enabling All‐Day Anti‐/Deicing and Dynamic Thermal Management
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Transparent anti‐/deicing materials have traditionally focused on maximizing solar harvesting to achieve efficient ice mitigation under cold conditions. However, this approach can introduce overheating risks during warm periods, creating a challenge in balancing anti‐/deicing and thermal management. Here, we report a climate‐adaptive window consisting of a spectrally selective optical switch, a hybrid Joule‐heating and a highly transparent superhydrophobic coating. Guided by an energy‐balance framework for full spectrum design, the window simultaneously achieves high luminous transmittance (65.2%), strong near‐infrared absorption (76.1%), and large solar modulation capability (36.0%), enabling dynamic thermal regulation while preserving robust anti‐/deicing functionality. The synergistic interplay of photo‐electrothermal heating, thermal retention, and superhydrophobicity extends icing delay by 11‐fold and realizes rapid all‐day deicing at −20°C. Under hot conditions, the thermochromism reduces the average indoor temperature by 15.2°C, substantially reducing building cooling demand and boosting greenhouse seedling biomass relative to conventional configurations. By integrating solar modulation with transparent anti‐/deicing functionality, this work paves the way for the development of next‐generation climate‐adaptive windows.

title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Imperceptible skin electronic interfaces for bidirectional communication are essential for next‑generation healthcare and human–machine interfaces. The long‑standing absence of an ideal interfacing material has made it challenging to achieve high‑quality bidirectional electrophysiology without disturbing innate perception. Inspired by the human stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, we report a metallic stratum corneum (MSC): a synthetic mesohydrous gel reinforced with a silver nanowire network. MSC achieves > 10 6 S m −1 conductivity, dual‑mode (electronic/ionic) conduction, sub‐micron thickness, and months‑long ambient stability. Its porous ultrathin architecture enables multidimensional imperceptibility (tactile, mechanical, thermal, and vapor‑permeable). MSC records electrophysiology with signal‑to‑noise ratio surpassing commercial gel electrodes, delivers efficient neuromuscular stimulation, and forms high‑resolution electrode arrays for spatiotemporal muscle mapping. By reconciling electronic performance, skin compatibility, and imperceptibility, the mesohydrous gel establishes a promising material platform for next‐generation on‐skin bioelectronics.

title: Octahedral Co3+ Spin‐State Regulation in W‐Doped Co3O4 for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Kinetics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) are promising high‐energy storage systems, but their practical application remains limited by the low electronic conductivity of sulfur, sluggish Li–S redox kinetics, and the lithium polysulfide (LiPS) shuttle effect. These challenges require the rational design of cathode catalysts with well‐regulated electronic structures and active sites. Herein, Cu 2+ and Al 3+ substitution in Co 3 O 4 was first used to identify the catalytic roles of Co sites with different coordination environments, forming CuCo 2 O 4 and CoAl 2 O 4 as model systems. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that octahedral Co 3+ sites play a key role in enhancing LiPS adsorption and Li–S reaction kinetics. Guided by this insight, tungsten species with different oxidation states were used to direct distinct local perturbations of tetrahedral‐ and octahedral‐Co‐site environments in Co 3 O 4 , yielding W Td ‐Co 3 O 4 @NC and W Oh ‐Co 3 O 4 @NC, respectively, where NC denotes nitrogen‐doped carbon. Magnetic measurements and DFT calculations demonstrate that W 6+ doping induces a low‐spin to high‐spin transition of Co 3+ , generating additional unpaired 3d electrons that strengthen LiPS adsorption and accelerate LiPS conversion. As a result, W Oh ‐Co 3 O 4 @NC/S delivers high capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling stability, even under lean‐electrolyte conditions. This work demonstrates spin‐state engineering of octahedral Co 3+ sites as an effective strategy to optimize catalytic activity for LSBs.

title: Coordination‐Driven Spiral Self‐Assembly of Helical Mesoporous Polymer Nanospheres and Derived MoS2/Carbon Colloidal Nanospheres for Fast Lithium Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. Herein, we develop a coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly (CSS) strategy that converts achiral building blocks into helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres (HMPSs) with continuous spiral surface textures and internal helical mesopores. Interfacial Mo–S coordination drives micellar spiral organization without chiral additives, enabling systematic regulation of pore size, morphology, and composition. Subsequent carbonization transforms HMPSs into helical mesoporous MoS 2 /C nanospheres (HMMoS 2 /C) containing uniformly dispersed monolayer MoS 2 while retaining the helical mesostructure. Finite‐element simulations and density functional theory calculations reveal that the helical mesoporous architecture facilitates rapid Li + diffusion, local ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, thereby improving Li‐storage kinetics. Consequently, HMMoS 2 /C delivers a reversible capacity of 1776.3 mAh g − 1 at 0.3 A g − 1 after 150 cycles, a high‐rate capacity of 752.7 mAh g − 1 at 10 A g − 1 , and outstanding long‐term cycling stability. This work establishes coordination‐driven self‐assembly as a versatile route to helical mesoporous materials for energy storage.

title: Interfacial Electronic‐Structural Coupling Suppresses Jahn‐Teller Instability in NASICON Cathode Casting Long Cycling Life
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT NASICON‐type Na 4 VMn(PO 4 ) 3 cathodes possess attractive high‐voltage and structural robustness, yet its application is hindered by the intrinsic instability of Mn 3+ ‐induced Jahn‐Teller distortion. A mosaic‐like Na 4 VMn(PO 4 ) 3 /NaFePO 4 (NVMP/NFP) heterostructure is constructed to achieve interfacial electronic‐structural synergistic regulation. The nanoscale heterointerfaces induce charge redistribution and modify the local electronic environment, thereby strengthening Mn─O interactions indirectly and interrupting the spatial correlation of local distortions, which successfully suppresses the Jahn‐Teller instability. The suppression of local electronic instability by the NVMP/NFP heterostructure is confirmed by complementary experimental and theoretical analyses, which further reveal reversible V 3+ /V 4+ and Mn 2+ /Mn 3+ redox reactions. Furthermore, the heterointerface reconstructs the Na + transport network by generating more interconnected and multidimensional migration pathways with reduced diffusion barriers, mitigates the accumulation of lattice strain during Na + extraction/insertion and fosters electron transfer, casting fast reversible electrochemical reaction. Benefiting from this interfacial electronic‐structural coupling, the optimized NVMP/NFP cathode delivers excellent wide‐temperature cycling stability, retaining 89.91% capacity after 6000 cycles at 2 A g −1 , 91.80% after 2500 cycles at ‐15°C, and 80.23% after 6000 cycles at 45°C. This work provides an interfacial engineering strategy for decoupling electronic instability from structural degradation and offers a general pathway for stabilizing Jahn‐Teller active electrode materials.

title: Medium‐Entropy Metallene Enables Sequential Hot‐Carrier Nanocatalytic Triaptosis Induction for Suppressing Tumor Growth and Metastasis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Triaptosis, a newly recognized cell death modality driven by endosomal dysfunction and persistent vacuolization, holds promise for tumor therapy. However, its clinical translation has been hindered by the lack of spatiotemporally controllable strategies to disrupt endosomal homeostasis. Herein, we engineer ultrathin PdCuCo medium‐entropy metallene catalysts (PCC MEMCs) as a new class of sono‐activatable catalytic biomaterials that induce triaptosis for tumor therapy. Upon ultrasound irradiation, lattice oscillations in PCC MEMCs generate non‐equilibrium hot carriers that execute two synergistic catalytic functions. These high‐energy hot carriers directly drive interfacial electron transfer with H 2 O and O 2 to produce hydroxyl radicals and superoxide anions, with sufficiently energetic carriers further converting triplet oxygen to singlet oxygen. Simultaneously, these hot carriers accelerate the intrinsic enzyocatalytic reactions by lowering surface adsorption barriers and enhancing charge transfer. This sequential nanocatalysis triggers a massive oxidative burst and substantial depletion of antioxidants, leading to VPS34 oxidation, PI(3)P depletion, and disruption of early endosomal processing. Consequently, persistent vacuolization and membrane collapse induce triaptosis, effectively suppressing tumor growth and metastasis. Collectively, this work establishes a sono‑activatable hot‑carrier sequential nanocatalytic paradigm, offers a distinct nanotherapeutic strategy against tumors via triaptosis induction, and broadens the biomedical scope of medium‐entropy metallenes toward sonocatalytic therapy.

title: Chiral Bobbers in the Room‐Temperature Magnet Co8Zn10Mn2
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral bobbers are three‐dimensional magnetic solitons that emerge near surfaces of chiral magnets with bulk‐type Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. They can be regarded as skyrmion strings terminated by a Bloch point inside the material. So far, chiral bobbers have been observed only at cryogenic temperatures. Here, we report the direct observation of chiral bobbers in over a broad temperature range, including room temperature. Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations, we identify a previously unreported nucleation pathway in which skyrmion strings transform into chiral bobbers under an applied magnetic field. We also demonstrate that chiral bobbers on opposite surfaces can be coupled to form double‐bobber states. These findings establish chiral bobbers as room‐temperature magnetic textures and identify their role in the nucleation pathways of topological magnetic solitons.

title: Dynamic Commercial Silicones Toward Sustainable, Task‐Reconfigurable Suction Gripping
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicone suction cups are widely used in industrial automation for scalable, high‐throughput handling, yet conventional designs are restricted to limited geometries. Advancing toward gripping is essential to transition robotics from single‐task execution to versatile handling across dynamic environments but presents a fundamental materials challenge: balancing the properties of on‐demand geometric reconfigurability with operational strength and elasticity. Existing universal grippers typically utilize composite materials that couple shape adaptation and gripping operation within a single cycle, introducing critical performance trade‐offs in force, speed, and preload requirements while adding structural complexity that together hinder broad industrial adoption. To address this, we establish a versatile post‐fabrication strategy that transforms commercial silicone thermosets into dynamic silicone materials via catalyst‐mediated exchange of intrinsic siloxane bonds. This enables scalable transformation of industrial suction cups to reconfigurable grippers that reconfigure shapes at elevated temperatures while preserving high gripping performance via thermosetting properties at ambient temperatures. We demonstrate an all‐silicone, hierarchically structured suction gripper combining a reconfigurable load‐bearing body with a compliant sealing interface towards sustainable, task‐reconfigurable gripping, ensuring infrastructure compatibility while delivering rapid suction actuation (50 ms) following thermal reconfiguration (e.g., ∼30 min at 140°C), efficient load capacity (27 kPa), and zero‐preload attachment across diverse environments.

title: Oxygen‐Stacking Reconstruction of Spent LiCoO2 for Fast Li‐Ion Kinetics and High‐Voltage Stability
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Recycling spent LiCoO 2 battery cathodes is essential for securing the sustainable supply of lithium and cobalt, yet current recycling methods mainly produce metal salts, precursors, or conventionally regenerated cathodes, making the recovery of high‐value LiCoO 2 with enhanced electrochemical performance remain challenging. To address this challenge, we systematically investigate and compare conventionally regenerated O3‐type LiCoO 2 (O3‐R‐LCO) and O2‐type LiCoO 2 produced through a hydrometallurgy‐assisted ion‐exchange upcycling strategy (O2‐UP‐LCO). The upgraded O2‐UP‐LCO preserves the local CoO 6 framework while exhibiting enlarged Li‐layer spacing and a more open interlayer structure compared with O3‐R‐LCO. Multiscale characterizations further reveal that the distinct oxygen stacking in O2‐UP‐LCO enables fast Li + transport and stable interfacial reaction kinetics, despite reversible phase transitions during cycling. Benefiting from these structural and kinetic advantages, O2‐UP‐LCO delivers 201 mAh g −1 even at 20C in coin cells and achieves an energy density of 486 Wh kg −1 at 1C in a 2 Ah‐level pouch cell. In contrast, O3‐R‐LCO suffers from restricted Li + diffusion and increased interfacial impedance at high voltage, accompanied by aggravated particle cracking after cycling. Overall, this work provides a polymorph‐upgrading strategy for efficient recovery of spent LiCoO 2 material.

title: Ultrastable Chromium Pyrazolate Polyhedra With Amorphization‐Enhanced Microporosity for Corrosive Guest Capture
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The chemical stability of porous coordination solids is commonly rationalized using hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) considerations, which have largely excluded chromium(III)‐pyrazolate architectures owing to their incompatibility and the kinetic inertness of Cr(III). Here, we report the first porous chromium(III) pyrazolate metal–organic polyhedron. The material exhibits extraordinary chemical robustness, remaining chemically intact over a pH window spanning 13.7 units (pH d 3 electronic configuration of Cr(III) maximizes crystal‐field stabilization energy, leading to unusually strong Cr–N (pyrazolate) bonding that overrides HSAB‐based expectations. Such robustness enables efficient and recyclable adsorption of highly corrosive guests, including water vapor, SO 2 , and NH 3 . Notably, the amorphous MOP achieves the highest SO 2 uptake reported among metal–organic polyhedra, exceeding the previous benchmark by 74%, together with outstanding SO 2 /CO 2 selectivity that is corroborated by dynamic breakthrough experiments.

title: Self‐Calibrating Fluorescence‐Exclusion Microfluidic Platform for 3D Topographic Profiling of Living Cell Monolayers
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Cell monolayers are active living matter whose three‐dimensional (3D) architecture and mechanical remodeling regulate tissue function, yet fast and continuous topographic monitoring remains difficult. Here, we present fluorescence exclusion microscopy for monolayers (FLEXOM), a microfluidic platform combining multilayer micropillar arrays with negative‐staining optics to convert wide‐field images into self‐calibrated 3D height maps. Geometry‐anchored cavities allow in‐frame self‐calibration at confluence, correcting global intensity variations shared by sample and reference regions. FLEXOM enables longitudinal 3D profiling from isolated cells to confluent sheets with sub‐second temporal resolution, sub‐micrometer temporal height precision, and multiday biocompatibility and operational stability. FLEXOM reveals two distinct anisotropic signatures. First, monolayers show distinct cell type‐dependent vertical thickness profiles despite comparable lateral footprints. Two vertical descriptors, mean height and within‐cell height standard deviation, distinguish cell types more accurately than nine two‐dimensional (2D) lateral descriptors. Second, under acute osmotic shock, diverse confluent cell monolayers exhibit geometrically anisotropic vertical–lateral remodeling. Under hypotonic stimulation, projected area changes lag behind height changes. Consistent with this lag, cyclic hypotonic–isotonic switching at 3‐min intervals produces predominantly vertical remodeling with limited cycle‐dependent lateral changes. Our work provides a high‐resolution 3D profiling tool and a framework for axis‐resolved analysis of topographic responses in active living matter.

title: Task‐Oriented Co‐Design of Optoelectronic Synaptic Devices: From Physical Mechanisms to System Integration
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Optoelectronic synaptic devices integrate optical sensing, state storage, and conductance modulation, offering high bandwidth, ultrafast response, and low energy consumption. These capabilities enable the development of energy‐efficient, scalable intelligent vision systems with rich synaptic plasticity, making optoelectronic synaptic devices one of the most promising approaches for overcoming the limitations of conventional von Neumann computing architectures. However, existing studies often evaluate device performance and synaptic functions under disparate structures and operating conditions, obscuring the relationships among physical mechanisms, device design, and task requirements, and limiting the establishment of generalizable design principles. This Review presents a task‐oriented framework that connects biological functions and application requirements with physical mechanisms, multilevel hardware design, and system integration. We first summarize biological synaptic and retinal functions and define key evaluation metrics and task requirements. We then discuss major operating mechanisms and strategies for coordinated optimization across materials, interfaces, device structures, and arrays. Representative applications are further reviewed, together with key challenges, including device stability, array uniformity, large‐scale integration, peripheral‐circuit overhead, and standardized benchmarking. By shifting the focus from isolated performance optimization toward cross‐level co‐design, this Review provides design guidelines for reproducible, scalable, and energy‐efficient optoelectronic neuromorphic hardware.

title: Single‐Device Bidirectional Photonic Synapses: From Polarity Switching to Adaptive Neuromorphic Computing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single‐device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses within the same physical element, provide a compact platform for adaptive photonic computing. However, the diverse architectures, regulation strategies, and physical mechanisms reported for BPS have hindered systematic understanding and quantitative comparison. Here, we establish a unified Structure–Regulation–Mechanism–Function (S–R–M–F) framework to organize single‐device BPS from device architecture and polarity regulation to physical mechanisms, synaptic functions, quantitative benchmarks and neuromorphic applications. We further distinguish physical photoresponse polarity from its functional interpretation in synaptic computing and highlight key considerations including energy consumption, reproducibility, variability, and system‐level scaling. Finally, we identify the transition from empirically observed PPC–NPC switching toward predictive, deterministic, programmable and reproducible operation as a key direction for future BPS development, with physics‐informed modeling and closed‐loop control offering promising routes toward adaptive photonic neuromorphic hardware.
