Live attenuated vaccination induces stronger T-cell responses, while the absence of detectable neutralising activity against the challenge virus suggests that cellular immunity, rather than neutralising antibodies, may contribute to protection. These findings demonstrate that seasonal live attenuated influenza vaccination can provide cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus, potentially through cellular immune responses in the respiratory tract.

title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neural decoding is a widely-used machine learning technique for investigating how behavior, perception and cognition are represented in neural activity. However without careful application data leakage can occur, where information from the test set contaminates the training set, leading to biased estimates of decoding performance and potentially invalidating biological conclusions. Here we show that leakage can be introduced in neural decoding studies by common supervised and unsupervised preprocessing steps, including dimensionality reduction. We reveal that in some cases leakage can paradoxically decrease decoding performance relative to unbiased estimates, and we provide theoretical analyses explaining how this occurs. We also show that, for autocorrelated neural time series, randomized k-fold cross-validation can dramatically overstate decoding performance. Based on these findings, we provide detailed recommendations for avoiding data leakage in neural decoding.

title: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Physical exercise promotes bone health. However, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. Here, we identified the hepatokine AGP2 as an osteoanabolic mediator of exercise. Exercise increases circulating AGP2 levels in mice and humans. Hepatocyte-specific Agp2 knockout substantially attenuates exercise-induced bone formation, whereas hepatic AGP2 overexpression prevents bone loss in ovariectomized mice. Mechanistically, exercise-induced lactate promotes hepatic Agp2 expression through histone H3K14 lactylation. Secreted AGP2 directly binds the Wnt co-receptor LRP5, activates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, promotes osteoblast differentiation, and suppresses osteoclast activity. Recombinant AGP2 administration also alleviates bone loss in mouse models of osteoporosis. Thus, these findings delineate a critical role of liver-bone crosstalk in mediating the beneficial effects of exercise on bone metabolism, highlighting AGP2 as a key mediator in exercise-induced bone anabolism and suggesting AGP2 as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of metabolic bone disorders.

title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Symbiotic bacteria in the human intestinal microbiota provide many pivotal functions to human health and occupy distinct biogeographic niches within the gut. Yet the molecular basis underlying niche-specific colonization remains poorly defined. To address this, we conducted a time-resolved dual RNA-seq experiment to simultaneously monitor the transcriptional co-adaptations of human commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron and human gut epithelial cells in a hypoxic, mucus-producing, epithelial co-culture system. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of mucus-associated versus supernatant Bacteroides populations unveiled small RNAs (sRNAs) that are differentially regulated between spatially segregated subpopulations. Among these, we identified IroR as a key sRNA that facilitates B. thetaiotaomicron adaptation to iron limitation and host glycan availability, partly by modulating expression of capsule-associated surface states. This work provides new insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of gut colonization and underscores a previously underappreciated role for bacterial sRNAs in shaping mutualistic interactions between the human microbiota and the gut epithelium.

title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring‐opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen‐containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen‐containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired‐electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs + , Sr 2+ and UO 2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO 2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO2 2+ uptake of 336 mg g −1 and a Cs + permeation flux of 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 , while exhibiting suppressed Sr 2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /UO 2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

title: Single-Molecule DNA Sequencing with Nanopores
abstract: Abstract DNA sequencing is indispensable in healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding of biology. DNA sequencing with nanopores uses a unique principle where individual DNA strands are threaded through a ring-like nanopore, which acts as a read head to electronically detect the bases. Due to the simple principle, nanopores enable sequencing at previously unachieved speeds and read lengths as well as direct sensing of epigenetically modified bases. The electrical nature also allows highly portable devices to be used in the clinic or the field. This review places DNA nanopore sequencing within the context of other DNA sequencing technologies and explains its functional principle and the essential components of commercial nanopore sequencing platforms. The advantages of nanopore sequencing are demonstrated with relevant case studies, and nanopore sequencing is compared to other technologies in terms of sequencing parameters such as read length, throughput, cost per base, and accuracy. A brief outlook discusses how the current shortcomings of nanopore sequencing can be addressed with future advances.

title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
abstract:
Abstract
                  Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing.

title: Spatial Confinement Enables In Situ Growth of the Nano-Sn@Sn3(PO4)2 Anode for Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nanoarchitecturing improves capacity utilization and mitigates mechanical stress of Sn anodes for elevated energy density sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet substantial surface energy induces nanoparticle aggregation. Traditional heterotopic coatings cannot sustain long-term mechanical confinement upon repeated volume variation of Sn. Herein, we propose a dealloying-induced phase transformation and spatial confinement strategy to in situ construct a robust Sn3(PO4)2 coating on Sn nanoparticles. Sn3(PO4)2 provides spatial confinement for the homogeneously dispersed Sn nanoparticles, while the nano-Sn (∼20 nm) within the Sn3(PO4)2 framework effectively alleviates mechanical stress and suppresses volume expansion. Consequently, Sn@Sn3(PO4)2 exhibits attractive structural integrity and electrochemical performance, with a reversible capacity of 772 mAh g–1, 83% capacity retention after 3600 cycles, and 583 mAh g–1 at 5 A g–1. Moreover, the Sn@Sn3(PO4)2||Na3V2(PO4)3 full cell delivers a favorable cycling stability and rate performance. This in situ reconstruction strategy guides electrode surface engineering and facilitates the application of Sn-based anodes in future SIBs.

title: Cathode-Generated Hydrogen Peroxide Contributes to Degradation of the Membrane Across Its Full Thickness in PEM Water Electrolyzers
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Proton-exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzers must operate for 80,000 h, and membrane degradation limits this lifetime. Because electroosmotic drag carries degradation products toward the cathode, the fluoride emission rate, the standard diagnostic, underrepresents anode-side and bulk degradation. It also misses larger fluorocarbon fragments (LC-MS); after correction for compression, about 80% of the excess measured thinning (SEM) over fluoride-derived thinning at 1 A cm−2 is chemical loss. Depth profiles at both membrane faces in time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry, with transport analysis, indicate anisotropic degradation across the full PEM thickness, consistent with cathode-generated hydrogen peroxide diffusing toward the anode, most strongly at 0.5–1.0 A cm−2. The estimated peroxide production rate is six times the molar rate of membrane loss. To reach 80,000 h, our results point to two design targets: oxygen crossover an order of magnitude below today's 1% benchmark, and peroxide-decomposition catalysts distributed throughout the membrane bulk.

title: Localized High-Concentration Electrolyte with Nonfluorinated Diluent for Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Localized high-concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) have been extensively investigated to improve rechargeable battery performance, yet most rely on costly fluorinated diluents. Herein, we develop a 1M LHCE using toluene as nonfluorinated and low-cost diluent for wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The 1M LHCE features a compressed solvation structure and preserved ion-transport pathways, enabling the antimonene alloy anode to deliver stable capacities of 555.2 mAh g–1 over 600 cycles at 25 °C and 573.2 and 512.3 mAh g–1 at 50 and –20 °C, respectively. Na3V2(PO4)3//antimonene full cells further demonstrate stable operation under 50 and –20 °C. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the 1M LHCE forms an adaptive solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that dynamically regulates composition and thickness, which becomes thicker and more organic-rich after sodiation but thinner and more inorganic-rich after desodiation. Such “breathable” SEI effectively accommodates large volume changes and ensures efficient Na+ transport. This work provides a rational electrolyte design strategy for wide-temperature SIBs.

title: Ultrafast cellulose nanocrystal production from diverse lignocellulosic biomass
abstract: Producing cellulose nanocrystals conventionally involves hazardous chemicals, complex purification and high energy consumption. A recyclable hydrolytic quasi-solvent strategy now enables rapid production of cellulose nanocrystals from cellulose and untreated biomass with lower environmental impacts and costs.

title: Unlocking Intrinsic Narrowband Organic Ultralong Afterglow Through Efficient Two‐Photon Ionization
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic ultralong afterglow (OUA) materials are exclusively constrained by their reliance on host–guest exciplexes, which inherently suffer from spectral broadening and limited color tunability. Here we demonstrate an effective strategy to achieve narrowband OUA by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two‐photon ionization (TPI). Through engineering multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) guests, we achieve full‐color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours, which are comparable to commercial inorganic afterglow materials. The rigid planar molecular architecture of MR‐TADF not only promotes TPI but also reinforces host–guest interactions, thus fostering efficient charge separation to boost OUA properties. The intrinsic OUA can also be achieved based on fluorophore and metal–organic complex guests with planar molecular skeletons. The resultant materials enable promising applications in spectrally pure emergency afterglow lighting and sophisticated afterglow organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). The afterglow OLEDs exhibit a maximum luminance of 26481 cd/m 2 , an external quantum efficiency of 8.7%, and record‐breaking ultralong electroluminescence afterglow lasting over 15 minutes. Our findings establish a valuable design principle for modulating charge migration and exciton transitions towards developing next‐generation OUA materials.

title: Superspreading droplets for scalable and green perovskite photovoltaics
abstract: Scaling up the manufacturing of perovskite solar cells requires rapid, zero-waste film deposition. The authors design a universal ink that accelerates production 30-fold, achieving high efficiencies.

title: Adapting minds to live with climate change
abstract: Climate adaptation psychology is fragmented across psychology’s subfields and neighbouring social sciences. This Perspective consolidates the scattered research into a four-layer framework (exposures, mediators, responses and outcomes) and closes with clinical implications and a research agenda.

title: Built‐in Electric Field Modulating Interfacial Charge Dynamics in V 2 AlC‐Derived Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterostructures for Broadband Microwave Absorption
abstract: ABSTRACT The tailored design of magnetic‐dielectric heterostructures offers considerable potential for high‐performance electromagnetic wave absorption, yet achieving efficient interfacial charge separation remains challenging. Herein, we constructed VC/FeCoNi/Al 2 O 3 heterostructures with built‐in electric fields (BIEFs) via the topological structural transformation of V 2 AlC in Lewis acidic molten salts. This transformation involves the redox‐potential‐driven substitution by Fe/Co/Ni cations, leading to in situ alloying within the VC interlayers to balance the electromagnetic parameters. Theoretical calculations reveal that the work‐function difference drives directional interfacial charge redistribution, as evidenced by experimental observations of charge transfer and surface‐potential differences. This charge redistribution reconstructs the local electronic states, leading to interfacial orbital hybridization and establishing BIEFs at the heterointerfaces. Atomic vacancies and lattice distortions generated during etching, coupled with the BIEFs, enhance interfacial and defect‐induced polarization. Consequently, the optimized composite achieves a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.72 GHz (at 1.7 mm) and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB (at 2.8 mm). This BIEF‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy offers a viable route for designing high‐performance broadband microwave absorbers.

title: Anion‐Anchoring, Anti‐Swelling Polymer Interphase Enables Durable Lithium Metal Anodes in Localized High‐Concentration Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) can improve the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries by promoting anion‐rich solvation structures that favor the formation of inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). However, their favorable interfacial chemistry is not self‐sustaining because the native SEI is heterogeneous and prone to repeated rupture during Li plating/stripping, thus progressively depleting active Li and electrolyte. Polymeric artificial SEIs have emerged as a complementary strategy for interfacial stabilization, but their effectiveness in LHCEs is limited by an inherent conflict: the polar functional groups that coordinate ions also coordinate solvents, causing polymer swelling, dissolution, and disruption of anion‐rich solvation structures. Here, we develop an anion‐anchoring and anti‐swelling artificial SEI (AS–SEI) by integrating imidazolium cations with long aliphatic side chains. Imidazolium cations enable anion anchoring to sustain the LHCE‐favored anion‐rich environment at the interface, while long aliphatic chains provide anti‐swelling behavior that protects anchoring sites from competitive solvation. Consequently, AS‐SEI exhibits a high Young's modulus (5.0–10.5 GPa) and a high Li + transference number (0.94), while promoting the formation of LiF/Li 2 O‐rich SEIs. Li||Cu cells achieve 480 cycles with 99.5% average Coulombic efficiency, while Li||NCM811 cells deliver ∼900 cycles with 80% capacity retention (a nearly threefold improvement), with the strategy remaining effective across ether‐, ester‐, and sulfone‐based LHCEs.

title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)‐mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium‐doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice‐induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20‐fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate ( para ‐nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N‐terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD‐NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This pan‐ PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro‐inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle‐mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

title: Revealing Oxidation‐State‐Dependent Selectivity in Urea Electrosynthesis Over Stabilized Co/CoO x Surfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic upgrading of CO 2 and nitrogen wastes offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, yet its selectivity is limited by competing parallel reactions and operando catalyst reconstruction. Here, using cobalt‐based model catalysts, we demonstrate that product partitioning among competing pathways can be selectively directed by metallic and oxidized cobalt phases. By introducing oxophilic Cr 3+ to retard cathodic over‐reduction of cobalt oxides, we stabilize a non‐equilibrium Co/CoO x surface under working conditions. The optimized Co@CoO x ‐Cr 1 catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 40.1 ± 1.1% and a yield rate of 102.27 ± 3.31 mmol h −1 g cat −1 under pressurized CO 2 at −0.3 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support a proposed oxidation‐state‐dependent relay mechanism in which metallic Co favors CO 2 ‐to‐*CO conversion, stabilized CoO x motifs may promote *NH 2 formation, and their interface is inferred to facilitate *CO─*NH 2 coupling for urea formation. This work identifies the controlled stabilization of coexisting phases with distinct oxidation states as a strategy for steering selectivity in multi‐reactant electrocatalysis.

title: Overriding Polarity Mismatch in Radical Difunctionalization of 1,3‐Dienes
abstract: ABSTRACT The difunctionalization of conjugated dienes poses a significant challenge in controlling regio‐ and stereoselectivity due to the presence of two conjugated double bonds. Conventional radical addition reactions adhere to the polarity‐matching principle, wherein nucleophilic alkyl radicals preferentially attack the electrophilic C4 position of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes. Consequently, the polarity‐mismatched C1‐selective addition has remained unexplored. Herein, we report a three‐component 1,4‐dicarbofunctionalization of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes with α ‐aminoalkyl radicals and alkyl bromides via dual nickel/photoredox catalysis. This protocol overcomes the inherent polarity‐mismatching effect, achieving unprecedented C1‐selective addition with complete 1,4‐regioselectivity and excellent E ‐stereoselectivity. The reaction provides efficient access to structurally diverse β ‐amino acid derivatives, featuring broad substrate compatibility and promising utility in the derivatization of complex molecules. Combined mechanistic investigations and DFT calculations reveal that both radical addition and C–C reductive elimination govern the regio‐ and stereoselectivity. Notably, a significant hyperconjugative interaction between the forming C–C bond and the carbonyl group of the 1,3‐diene in the transition state plays a pivotal role in directing the radical addition to the polarity‐mismatched C1 position.

title: A research agenda for integrating artificial intelligence in mitigation scenario workflows
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into mitigation scenarios development could reduce the current bottlenecks. This Perspective proposes a research agenda to address these challenges at each phase, highlighting the importance of both agentic architecture and expert oversight.

title: Rattlesnake-Inspired Near-Infrared Sensing Based on Photothermal-Induced Asymmetric Interfacial Ion Rearrangement
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conventional near-infrared (NIR) light sensing materials, reliant on inorganic or organic semiconductors, are often limited by their photoelectric conversion efficiency, cooling volume, and recyclability. Inspired by the pit organ of rattlesnakes, this work presents an NIR sensing strategy based on photo-thermal-electric conversion. An NIR sensing unit is constructed based on Au@ITO-graphite asymmetric electrodes and ionogel, effectively coupling interfacial photothermal and thermoelectric conversion. NIR light energy is rapidly converted into heat due to the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs). This thermal stimulus induces asynchronous ion adsorption and desorption at asymmetric electrode–electrolyte interfaces, generating a measurable open-circuit voltage even under nearly zero temperature gradient. The NIR sensing unit, with an electrode spacing of 0.1 mm, exhibits a sensitivity approximately 70 times higher than that of symmetric electrodes. Moreover, the NIR sensing unit can be disassembled and reused, and the Au@ITO electrodes exhibit at least 5 times of reusability and stability. This mechanism allows us to construct a sensing array for spatial NIR mapping and a biomimetic system that replicates the complete “perception‑to‑orientation” behavior sequence. This work provides a material-agnostic strategy for application in ultrathin, environmentally friendly, and self-powered NIR sensing systems.

title: Tomato NLR R1L mediates SlSPL3 degradation to trigger a growth-to-defense switch against Phytophthora infestans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Intracellular nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) receptors activate effector-triggered immunity (ETI), a key branch of plant immunity conferring robust resistance. The downstream signaling mechanisms of ETI receptors remain unclear. We characterize tomato NLR protein R1L that specifically recognizes the Phytophthora infestans effector AVR1. R1L is predominantly cytoplasmic and partially relocalizes into the nucleus upon infection. With helper SlNRC1, R1L and AVR1 trigger a hypersensitive response (HR). R1L positively regulates tomato immunity against P. infestans. Yeast two-hybrid screening identified SlSPL3, a positive regulator of growth and development, as a direct R1L interactor. SlSPL3 binds the GTAC-box motif in the SlLTP3 promoter and activates this negative immune regulator. R1L counteracts SlSPL3-mediated immune suppression by promoting the ubiquitin-mediated degradation of SlSPL3. Thus, the AVR1-R1L-SlSPL3-SlLTP3 module mediates a growth-immunity trade-off. In uninfected plants, SlSPL3 promotes growth and suppresses immunity via SlLTP3. Upon infection, R1L-mediated SlSPL3 degradation activates immunity and represses growth. This study elucidates a pathogen perception-transcriptional reprogramming-immunity axis, offering insights into plant defense and growth-immunity balance.

title: SMYD1 trimethylates myosin K129 to restrain cardiomyocyte hypercontractility
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mutations in the force-generating motor protein myosin are common etiologic drivers of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), a prevalent inherited cardiac disease. However, whether deregulation of myosin post-translational modifications also contributes to HCM remains unknown. Here we show that SMYD1 selectively catalyzes trimethylation of cardiac β-myosin heavy chain at lysine 129 (MyHC-K129me3), and that loss of this activity promotes cardiomyocyte hypercontractility and is linked to HCM pathogenesis. A biochemical-proteomic coupled strategy identifies MyHC-K129 as the principal physiological substrate of SMYD1 in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs). The SMYD1-MyHC co-crystal structure reveals extensive interactions underlie K129 substrate specificity and shows that the HCM-associated SMYD1F272L mutation disrupts S-adenosyl-L-methionine binding, thereby compromising catalytic activity. K129me3 loss alters the myosin motor domain intrinsic mechanical behavior, decreasing maximal ATP turnover rate and motility. Finally, eliminating K129 methylation enhances contractility and force generation in iPSC-CM monolayers and engineered cardiac tissues. Collectively, our results uncover a pivotal role for the SMYD1-MyHC-K129me3 axis in restraining cardiac contractility, providing insight into the pathogenic mechanism of an HCM-associated SMYD1 mutation.

title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The photon avalanche effect exhibits a large optical nonlinear response, which is crucial for advancement in super-resolution imaging and optical sensing. However, photon avalanche systems with nonlinearity exceeding 100 remain confined to a single band in the near-infrared region, where standard detectors have low sensitivity. Here, we show that a cascade amplified photon avalanche strategy via lattice reconstruction to address these limitations. Introducing lutetium substitution into the host lattice enhances interionic energy exchange and cross-relaxation, activating multiple visible emission channels of holmium and erbium ions with amplified nonlinearities. A nonlinearity order of up to 560 is achieved in ~216 nm nanoparticles, while 43 nm nanoparticles retain a nonlinearity of 183 and enable super-resolution microscopy with 28 nm lateral resolution. We further demonstrate multi-color super-resolution microscopy and sub-cellular bioimaging. Benefiting from high detection efficiency and flexible wavelength selection, cascade amplified photon avalanche nanoprobes are promising for ultrasensitive sensing and super-resolution lithography beyond optical imaging.

title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The high-yield synthesis of nanoscale graphene oxide is increasingly critical, yet widespread scalable implementation of top-down methods remains hindered by low efficiency. Here, we report a highly efficient, scaled-up approach coupling photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage to fragment micron-sized graphene oxide into nanoscale flakes. Irradiation induces nanoscale holes on the graphene oxide basal plane, causing rapid fragmentation upon hydrogen peroxide treatment. This yields nanoscale graphene oxide (20 to 60 nanometers) featuring an sp2-hybridized carbon core and carboxylic acid-rich edges. The material exhibits exceptional stability against thermal ripening, prolonged solar irradiation, and chemical reduction. Achieving an 85 ± 5 % conversion yield, the practical scalability of this process is demonstrated using a pilot-scale device with a projected annual capacity of 0.52 tons of powder. This work provides a route for the pilot-scale production of high-performance nanoscale graphene oxide materials.

title: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transcutaneous electrical stimulation can elicit hand movements by activating peripheral nerves and muscles. Here, we present a wearable system integrating programmable constant-current stimulation, a flexible 32-electrode forearm array with full-array active–return routing, and real-time path and parameter updating. Human-derived skin–electrode load tests showed a mean current-delivery accuracy of 94.0%, while four-hour reassessment showed 93.5% within-participant action-category agreement. Using reconfigurable active–return routing and an anatomy-informed two-level traversal strategy, we established current-path-to-action maps spanning 12 wrist and hand action categories, with spatial patterns broadly consistent with superficial forearm flexor and extensor compartments. Data-glove and inertial measurements quantified parameter-dependent finger-joint responses and action-specific wrist rotations. The mapped actions were sequentially combined for feedback-guided, stimulation-assisted task-level hand operation, supporting wearable functional electrical stimulation for task-oriented hand assistance and rehabilitation research.

title: Quantitative prediction model of FB-113-driven self-assembly nanopesticides
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nanopesticides offer new opportunities to improve pesticide efficacy and utilization efficiency; however, they are often complex to produce and exhibit low cargo loading, except for those formed through molecular self-assembly. Currently, the formation of these self-assembly nanopesticides remains difficult to predict, heavily relying on serendipitous observation and trial-and-error screening. Here, we report that the widely used and environmentally benign biopesticide synergist fluorescent brightener FB-113 drives the self-assembly of various pesticides into nanoparticles with ultrahigh loadings exceeding 80%. We developed an interpretable Quantitative Pesticide Structure-Assembly Prediction model (QPSAP), which reveals hydrophobicity, halogenation, polarity, and topological structure of pesticide molecules as key descriptors associated with FB-113-mediated self-assembly propensity. QPSAP was applied to large-scale virtual screening of a pesticide library to identify novel candidates for FB-113-mediated self-assembly, demonstrating complete concordance between predictions and experimental outcomes in a prospectively tested validation subset. The resulting nanopesticides enhance foliar wetting, adhesion, photostability, and transcuticular penetration, thereby increasing insecticidal and acaricidal efficacy against multiple pests while exhibiting improved crop compatibility and a reduced acute toxicity profile under the tested conditions. This work advances self-assembly nanopesticides from empirical formulation toward predictive, computationally screenable design, representing a significant advancement in safe and efficient pesticide nanoformulations.

title: Scalable 3D hybrid integrated photonic computing chiplets
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The exponential surge in artificial intelligence computing power demand is driving a transition from electrons to photons across the infrastructure. Although integrated photonics has revolutionized communications and computing, its scaling for large-scale information processing is constrained by monolithic scalability, modulation efficiency, and multi-chip integration. Here, we present HyPec, a hybrid photonic extensible chiplet architecture that synergizes thin-film lithium niobate modulation chiplets with femtosecond laser-written three-dimensional functional chiplets. Through function disaggregation, HyPec partitions high-performance active modulation from the 3D photonic routing network. This chiplet architecture facilitates seamless multi-chip connectivity across diverse material platforms to achieve aggregate performance beyond monolithic limits, thereby allowing the system to scale through the addition of functional chiplets. To validate the advantages of this architecture, we experimentally built a co-packaged photonic computing chiplet system that implements a scalable graph solver and further identifies critical protein residues in structural biology networks. This work establishes a scalable hardware path for integrated photonic computing, with broader implications for high-density optical interconnects and photonic quantum information systems.

title: Directional atomic-ordering gradients enable fatigue-resistant superelasticity in carbon tube aerogels
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Elastic inorganic aerogels are highly attractive for weight-sensitive applications in extreme environments, yet integrating high strength, large-strain recoverability and fatigue resistance within a single architecture remains a longstanding challenge. Here we show that directional atomic-ordering gradients in carbon tube aerogels provide a structural route to overcoming this trade-off. Guided by finite-element analysis, we create atomic-ordering gradient junctions through stepwise-modulated chemical vapor deposition, producing a radial increase in carbon ordering across load-bearing tube walls and inter-tube junctions. Multiscale characterization and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the directional gradient enables the outer crystalline region to function as a sliding-enabled stress-relief layer, thereby promoting stress delocalization, suppressing bond rupture and reducing irreversible energy dissipation before network densification becomes dominant. As a result, the directional-gradient aerogel sustains reversible compression up to 95% strain, reaches a maximum stress of 8.0 MPa, and retains ~87% of its initial maximum stress after 10,000 cycles at 90% strain with only ~6% permanent deformation. These findings show that controlling atomic ordering at carbon tube junctions offers an effective way to improve the mechanical robustness and fatigue resistance of highly compressible porous solids.

title: Low-pressure operation of all-solid-state batteries enabled by an organic electrode
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All-solid-state batteries offer enhanced safety and high energy density. However, their practical application is challenged by the need for high external pressures, often tens of MPa, to maintain intimate solid–solid contact and preserve ion/electron percolation pathways during cycling. In this work, we demonstrate that low-modulus, low-hardness, creep-compliant, low-strain organic active materials that readily deform in response to external pressures and microstructural changes enable stable cell operation under low stack pressures. Using bis-tetraaminobenzoquinone (TAQ) as a model compound, we show its low modulus (8.4–15.3 GPa), low hardness (0.33–0.76 GPa), and moderate creep compliance (m = 0.038–0.073), quantified by nanoindentation of both pristine and lithiated TAQ, enable adaptive deformability under low stack pressures. TAQ-based solid-state cells achieve stable cycling and promising rate performance at external pressures as low as 1 MPa, retaining 80.3% capacity after 100 cycles at 0.5C. Operando and post-mortem electron microscopy reveal that TAQ electrodes maintain high structural integrity at pressures as low as 0.2 MPa. These findings establish a materials design strategy centered on mechanically adaptive materials to enable solid-state battery operation under practically relevant pressure conditions.

title: Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reversible light control of supramolecular interactions underpins fundamental processes in nature, inspiring artificial molecular devices and adaptive materials. Existing approaches rely on light-modulated interconversion between ground-state species characterized by distinct binding properties. Here, we introduce twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) as an excited-state specific lever to modulate dye–surface adhesion. Using rhodamine B base (Rhb) as the photoactive species, we combine femtosecond spectroscopy with theoretical calculations to provide a direct observation of TICT formation and its thermal equilibrium with the locally excited state. We show that the associated dihedral twisting and charge redistribution weaken Rhb-graphene binding, enabling light-induced dye desorption in water. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate that the out-of-plane TICT conformations induce steric hindrance against the graphene basal plane, significantly reducing the binding affinity and lowering the thermodynamic barrier of the dye-surface desorption. This synergy between experiment and theory establishes excited-state conformational dynamics as a general strategy to control supramolecular interactions in host-guest systems in physiological conditions, with implications for sensing, delivery, and materials science.

title: A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies
abstract: Potent immune responses against diverse HIV strains have ignited the field, but major hurdles remain.

title: Vision sensors that remember the scene and report change
abstract: An optoelectronic pixel stores slowly varying intensity of a scene as a persistent baseline and superimposes rapid changes as transient currents, reducing redundant visual data while preserving spatial context.

title: Stereoelectronic effects in glycan conformation
abstract: This Tutorial Review discusses the stereoelectronic effects that determine glycan conformation. Chemical strategies to tune these effects and control glycan conformations are discussed to inspire new glycan designs.

title: Energy Storage Properties of Natural Clinoptilolite-Based Anodes for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Improved Capacity and Stability via Magnesiothermic Reduction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, we investigate the morphology, chemical composition, and electrochemical performance of natural clinoptilolite subjected to thermal and chemical treatment. Magnesiothermic reduction of this natural zeolite resulted in an increase in the Si/O ratio and the formation of a new crystalline silicon phase. SEM observations showed that the original particle morphology was largely preserved, whereas EDS and XRD confirmed changes in the elemental and phase composition, respectively. The suggested partial reduction of SiO2 was additionally confirmed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), which revealed a substantial decrease in the surface aluminum content and densification of Si species on the modified surface. Electrochemical studies showed that the clinoptilolite-based materials can be used effectively as negative electrodes in lithium-ion batteries. Cyclic voltammetry indicated stable electrochemical properties, with a predominantly capacitive contribution at higher scan rates and a greater contribution from diffusion-controlled processes at lower scan rates. In turn, galvanostatic tests confirmed the high specific capacity, reaching 668 mAh/g for the material after magnesiothermic reduction, with a capacity retention of ∼94% after 1000 cycles. The results indicate the potential use of the tested materials as negative electrodes with high specific capacity and long-term cyclic stability.

title: Self-Propelled Magnesium-Based Janus Micromotors Enabling Enhanced Drug Delivery into Cartilage for Osteoarthritis Therapy
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage damage. Intra-articular injection is the preferred therapeutic route for OA, yet drugs are rapidly cleared from the synovial fluid, and they poorly penetrate the dense, avascular cartilage. Herein, a self-propelled Janus micromotor is developed for enhanced intra-articular drug delivery into cartilage for OA treatment. In this system, the magnesium (Mg) particle acts as the power source, reacting with synovial fluid to generate hydrogen gas for propulsion, while the poly(allylamine hydrochloride) (PAH)-modified poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) layer enables charge-assisted targeting toward negatively charged cartilage for drug penetration. In vitro co-culture studies show that the micromotors rapidly overcome the viscous synovial fluid barrier, deliver drugs to the cartilage surface, and facilitate deep penetration before clearance. Cell experiments demonstrate that micromotors attenuate IL-1β-induced chondrocyte injury and promote GAG and Col II synthesis. Furthermore, in an OA rat model, micromotors loaded with both the anti-inflammatory drug triacetyl andrographolide (A100) and the cartilage-repair drug kartogenin (KGN) inhibit inflammatory factor expression while upregulating Col II, thereby disrupting the vicious cycle of inflammation and cartilage degeneration and efficiently promoting cartilage repair. This well-designed A100/KGN@PAH-PLGA-Mg micromotor offers a promising strategy for improved OA therapy.

title: Complex [Ru(bpy)3]2+-Templated Hybrid Metal Halides with Improved Luminescence for Advanced Optoelectronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Zero-dimensional (0D) organic–inorganic hybrid metal halides (HMHs) have attracted intense interest for their rich selectivity of composition and exceptional luminescence properties. However, the exploration of functional A-site cations is very limited, and their roles are not well understood. Herein, we introduce the intrinsically emissive complex [Ru(bpy)3]2+ (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) as an A-site building block to construct a family of 0D HMHs with the general formula [Ru(bpy)3]MCl6 ([M], M = Sn, Te). [M] not only preserves the orange-red metal-to-ligand charge transfer emission of [Ru(bpy)3]2+ but also exhibit a nearly 10-fold enhancement in photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) compared to that of unhybridized [Ru(bpy)3]Cl2. More interestingly, through alloying with multiple M4+ cations (Sn4+, Te4+, Zr4+, Hf4+, W4+), high-entropy [SnTeZrHfW] crystals are successfully synthesized with improved thermal stability and antithermal quenching behavior. The representative [Sn] analog demonstrates broadband emission spanning from 550 to 800 nm with a high PLQY of 54.1%, promising for efficient red LEDs and near-infrared imaging. Moreover, its strong X-ray radioluminescence performance affords a flexible scintillation screen with a spatial resolution of 17.6 lp mm–1 and low detection limit of 1.99 μGy s–1. This work provides a paradigm for designing high-entropy 0D HMHs with functional cationic chromophores, advancing their applications in solid-state lighting and radiation imaging.

title: Directional codes for quantum LDPC error correction on square and hexagonal grid architectures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Utility-scale quantum computing requires quantum error correction to protect quantum information against noise. Superconducting hardware is a promising platform for fault-tolerant computation, but its typically two-dimensional nearest-neighbour connectivity restricts the variety of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes that can be implemented efficiently. Here we introduce directional codes, a family of qLDPC codes compatible with square-grid and, in some cases, hexagonal-grid architectures. The key idea is to use the iSWAP gate to measure long range stabilisers using only local interactions, without requiring additional connectivity. We evaluate directional codes using a superconducting-inspired circuit-level Pauli noise model and compare them to the rotated toric code and bivariate bicycle codes. The best directional code family considered matches the logical error rate of the rotated toric code at physical error rate p = 10−3 but requires only a quarter to a third of the number of physical qubits to encode a given number of logical qubits.

title: A neuroimmune dichotomy for T cell immunity in the mesenteric iymph node in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Peripheral nerves innervate lymphoid organs, yet how they decode immune signals and direct adaptive immunity remains unknown. Here we show, using three-dimensional tissue imaging, in vivo calcium recordings, single-cell transcriptomics, and chemogenetics in mice, that the mesenteric lymph node (mLN) harbours functionally antagonistic neural circuits that govern T cell fate. Vagal sensory neurons selectively detect IL-1β and TNF-α and release calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which suppresses Foxp3⁺ regulatory T (Treg) cells and expands cytotoxic CD8⁺ effector T (Teff) cells. Conversely, sympathetic neurons sense IL-6 and release norepinephrine (NE), promoting Treg accumulation while restraining effector responses. During Citrobacter rodentium infection, the sympathetic–NE–Treg axis is protective, whereas the vagal–CGRP axis drives immunopathology. Treg-specific deletion of the CGRP receptor or the β₂-adrenergic receptor confirms that these opposing signals converge on Treg cells to calibrate mucosal host defence. These findings establish the mLN as an autonomic rheostat for intestinal immunity.

title: Chip-scale narrow-linewidth optical parametric oscillators
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Continuous-wave-pumped optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) provide an exciting avenue to generate coherent radiation at wavelength regions that are difficult to reach by traditional semiconductor optical amplifiers. However, attaining ultra-narrow linewidth operation in OPOs requires pump lasers with exceptional purity to begin with. Here, we demonstrate an integrated Kerr nonlinear OPO featuring an integrated external cavity based on ultralow-loss silicon nitride that results in a continuous-wave signal with a 15-fold intrinsic linewidth reduction compared to the pump, down to 10 Hz. Our numerical analysis indicates that the intrinsic linewidth can be reduced below the Schawlow-Townes limit of a single-cavity OPO depending on the feedback length and strength of the external cavity. Utilizing an integrated erbium-doped waveguide amplifier, we further demonstrate sub-Hz intrinsic linewidth coherent oscillation. These results establish an effective pathway towards chip-scale ultra-coherent light sources with high power and broad wavelength tunability, opening new opportunities for high-precision optical sensing and detection.

title: Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Lithium holds therapeutic promise for Alzheimer’s disease (AD), yet its clinical application is hindered by a narrow therapeutic range and nephrotoxicity. We rationally design a lithium coordination compound, BuLiPro, chelated with endogenous butyrate and proline. Single-crystal diffraction and mass-spectrometry confirm its crystal structure and solution-state coordination, while spectroscopic assays verify an identity distinct from free lithium. Compared with lithium carbonate, BuLiPro achieves improved plasma exposure, slower clearance, and 61.6%-higher brain lithium accumulation at 48 h in rats. It yields lower renal cytotoxicity and in vivo kidney injury, and inhibits glycogen synthase kinase-3β over three-fold more potently. In female AD model mice, BuLiPro attenuates tau and amyloid-β pathologies to a greater extent and rescues cognition. This coordination-based strategy enhances lithium’s central bioavailability and reduces systemic toxicity, offering a framework for the development of next-generation lithium therapeutics.

title: An interaction module for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: ATP synthase and its dimerization are essential for cristae formation and mitochondrial biogenesis. In plants, the absence of canonical j and k subunits raises the question of how ATP synthase assembly and dimerization are supported in this lineage. We identify MTF5, a fast-turnover, seed plant-specific protein critical for embryogenesis and mitochondrial biogenesis. Loss of MTF5 causes embryo arrest and altered mitochondrial morphology. A conditional complementation line partially rescues the embryo-lethal phenotype but shows growth defects and mitochondrial morphology changes. MTF5 interacts with another fast-turnover protein, MTF5P, and co-migrates with ATP synthase dimerization-associated subunits, supporting a role in ATP synthase assembly and maintenance. Structural predictions reveal a helical architecture comprising a long central α-helix flanked by shorter helices, but do not establish direct correspondence with canonical j and k subunits. Our findings uncover an interaction module for ATP synthase assembly and maintenance that is essential for seed plant growth and development.

title: Atomic-resolution insights into interactions of rifampicin and rifamycin derivatives with orphan CYP143 of M. tuberculosis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Analysis of drug-resistant strains of M. tuberculosis identified a Gly334Ala mutation in the orphan CYP143 gene, located within the ESX-5 secretion cluster. Guided by this clinical association, we tested the frontline antitubercular agent rifampicin as a CYP143 ligand. Atomic-resolution structures reveal a closed binding mode of rifampicin above the heme, which we also observed for other natural and synthetic rifamycins. The high quality of crystallographic data for both the wild type and mutant structures allowed us to track ligand-induced changes from the active site to the meander, the binding site for the redox partner. Consistent with this, the structure of a CYP143–ligand–redox partner complex confirms that these conformational changes are directly coupled to ligand binding. The structure of CYP143 with a selective inhibitor provides a template for rational drug design. Together, these results advance the understanding of rifampicin resistance/tolerance and the role of the orphan CYPome of M. tuberculosis.

title: Toward a Visible‐Range Helicity Filter: Panchromatic Magnetic Circular Dichroism via 4f‐Orbital‐Based Charge Transfer in a Cerium(IV) Complex
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)‐based light‐helicity filters provide a material‐based approach to controlling the helicity of light. However, helicity control across the entire visible spectrum using a single molecular species has not yet been demonstrated. Herein, we report a tetravalent cerium (Ce(IV)) complex exhibiting panchromatic MCD properties originating from 4f‐orbital‐based ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions. A Ce(IV) complex containing four electron‐donating anionic diethyldithiocarbamate ligands was synthesized. This complex exhibits panchromatic light absorption with both positive (520–780 nm) and negative (380–520 nm) MCD signals. Relativistic time‐dependent density functional theory (TD‐DFT) calculations reveal that this panchromatic light absorption originates from multiple LMCT transitions. The strong spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) associated with the Ce(IV) 4f orbitals facilitates the mixing of singlet and triplet LMCT excited states, enabling panchromatic light absorption. The 4f‐orbital‐based transition properties also contribute to effective MCD signals governed by the Faraday B ‐term. These findings highlight the potential of panchromatic MCD in a Ce(IV) complex as a promising approach toward the development of visible‐range light‐helicity filters.

title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N ‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
abstract: ABSTRACT N‐ Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH‐pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal‐editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N‐ alkyl pyrazoles through selective two‐carbon deletion. The N‐ substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine‐mediated Zincke‐type ring opening, acid‐promoted cyclization, and retro‐Mannich extrusion of a two‐carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C 5 N pyridine framework into a C 3 N 2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N‐ alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N‐ alkylation into a programmable precursor‐design strategy.

title: Molecular Crystal Phase Transformation via Nonclassical Pathways: Surfactant‐Based Kinetic Control of Metastable Amorphous Intermediates
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular crystals serve as essential components in a wide range of functional products, yet their performance is often compromised by unpredictable phase transformations, particularly in aqueous environments. Although nonclassical, multistage pathways are frequently proposed for such transitions, the specific role of transient intermediates remains poorly understood. Here, we employ in situ atomic force microscopy and high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy to elucidate a nonclassical transformation pathway in the model molecular crystal piroxicam that proceeds via metastable intermediates. These intermediates serve as amorphous precursors that undergo densification prior to crystallization, facilitating a rapid transition from the anhydrate to a less soluble hydrate phase. The onset and kinetics of this transformation are tunable through the use of cationic surfactants with varying alkyl‐chain lengths. Longer‐chain surfactants cooperatively adsorb onto both dissolving crystal facets and nanodroplets in solution, creating a dense interfacial barrier that delays precursor formation and subsequent crystallization. This work presents a strategy to manipulate phase transformation pathways in molecular crystals by targeting the metastable intermediates via tailored additive‐interface interactions, enabling the predictive design of advanced materials with controlled phase behavior and enhanced performance reliability.

title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation With Expanded Substrate Compatibility
abstract: ABSTRACT The Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is an established transformation in organic synthesis for the preparation of chiral vicinal diols. However, conventional biphasic solution‐based conditions (typically water/ t‐ BuOH) require long reaction times (up to ∼48 h) and large amounts of solvent. Moreover, they often exhibit limited substrate scope due to low solubility of the substrates and functional‐group incompatibility. Herein, we report the first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation, which affords the desired diols with excellent enantioselectivity, comparable to that of conventional methods. Notably, most substrates are fully converted within 30 min without the need for large quantities of solvent. Moreover, the mechanochemical conditions enable efficient reactions of substrates that are challenging to convert under solution‐based conditions, including poorly soluble, base‐sensitive, and catalyst‐coordinating compounds. The practical utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by the efficient dihydroxylation of an intermediate of a natural product and a gram‐scale synthesis.

title: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al2O3/FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO4/FeO4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

title: Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hotspot-based reference frames are foundational to plate reconstructions yet increasing evidence indicates that individual Pacific hotspots have migrated over time. How the overall motion of Pacific hotspots relates to the evolution of the underlying Pacific basal mantle structure (BMS), the inferred source of Pacific mantle plumes, remains elusive. Here we combine plate reference frame analysis with global mantle flow simulations to quantify the average motion of Pacific hotspots and compare it with the predicted motion of the Pacific BMS. Comparisons between Pacific fixed-hotspot reference frames and other absolute reference frames suggest an average southward migration of Pacific hotspots of ~5–10° from 80 Ma. Mantle flow models driven by plate reconstructions independently predict comparable southward average migration of Pacific plumes and the underlying Pacific BMS. In the models, the coupled BMS-plume migration is driven by greater subduction flux along the northern Pacific than along the southern Pacific between ~80-45 Ma, which generated persistent southward lower-mantle flow. Our results indicate that the average drift of Pacific hotspots is linked to the motion of the Pacific BMS, highlighting dynamic coupling between surface hotspot motion and basal mantle evolution.

title: Restoring global forest canopy structure complexity for potential local warming mitigation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Forests are natural coolers of Earth’s land surface temperatures. However, the local biophysical cooling provided by forest is often constrained by trade-off between expanding forest areas and competing land uses, which has challenged both policymakers and scientists for decades. Restoring forest canopy structural complexity has long been viewed as a promising nature-based strategy to alleviate this constrain, yet its effectiveness and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood at the global scale. Using satellite-derived land surface temperature and LiDAR-based measurements of canopy structures, we show that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances local land surface cooling across most global forests (90.0%). The cooling potential of vertical canopy complexity consistently exceeds that of horizontal crown cover density, which has been long overlooked. By aligning canopy structure complexity of managed forests with that of nearby intact forests, we estimate a potential reduction of 0.25 ± 0.001 °C in local land surface temperature globally. Our findings provide insights into strengthening the climate regulation of existing forests through the ecological restoration of forest canopy structure complexity and suggest a space-efficient management strategy that complements, rather than substitutes for, forest conservation and afforestation.

title: Selective Gas‐Phase Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Methanol Conversion Over Gallium Oxynitride With Molecular Oxygen as the Sole Oxidant
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective oxidation of methane to methanol using molecular oxygen remains challenging because methane activation is often accompanied by deep oxidation of the desired methanol product. Here we report a metal‐decorated, partially oxidized GaON/GaN photocatalyst for gas‐phase methane‐to‐methanol conversion using molecular oxygen as the oxidant. The optimized Ag/GaON/GaN catalyst delivers a methane oxidation rate of 2.6 mmol g − 1 h − 1 with ∼85% CH 4 ‐to‐CH 3 OH selectivity under O 2 . When untreated room air is used as the oxidant in a closed‐loop recirculating system, the catalyst maintains an activity of 1.0–1.3 mmol g − 1 h − 1 in a 50 h test, with comparable methanol selectivity. Complementary mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a mechanism in which partial surface oxidation promotes O 2 activation, while residual surface –NH species may moderate the resulting reactive intermediates through local H‐transfer processes, thereby suppressing methanol overoxidation. These results highlight partially oxidized oxynitride surfaces as a promising platform for selective methane upgrading under gas‐phase photocatalytic conditions.

title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO 4 Electrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Directly repair is recognized as a promising route for recycling spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP), but it is challenged by uneven Li supplementation and high energy input. Herein, we propose a photocatalytic strategy for PVDF degradation coupled with targeted Li replenishment toward low‐energy repair of spent LFP materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in‐situ characterizations, TiO 2 can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation. The photogenerated holes promote the formation of •OH radicals, which abstract hydrogen atoms from the methylene units in PVDF, triggering the scission of polymer backbones and thus enabling the effective degradation of PVDF. Meanwhile, the photogenerated electrons accumulated on TiO 2 create a strong reductive microenvironment conducive to the reduction of Fe 3+ to Fe 2+ , which reduces the Li + migration barrier and facilitates lithium replenishment. The TiO 2 catalyst can incorporate into the material lattice as a favorable dopant to optimize the performances of as‐repaired LFP material. Specially, the repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% TiO 2 delivers a high discharge capacity of 140.6 mAh g −1 at 1 C with 99.8% capacity retention ratio after 100 cycles. Even at a high rate of 5 C, it maintains 98.3% capacity retention ratio over 1500 cycles.

title: Rational Regulation of Ligand Conformation Toward Topology Reconfiguration for Sieving Butane Isomers
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving one‐step purification of n ‐C 4 H 10 and iso ‐C 4 H 10 from their isomeric mixtures with high efficiency and high purity is highly desirable yet extremely challenging, as it critically necessitates adsorbents that integrate size‐exclusive sieving functionality, high n ‐C 4 H 10 adsorption capacity, and fast adsorption kinetics. Herein, we synthesize a novel cage‐like anion‐pillared MOF adsorbent (SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu) through ligand‐conformation‐directed topology reconfiguration. Compared with the pillar‐layer prototype SIFSIX‐TEPE‐Cu, SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu exhibits a distinctive “confined window–expanded cavity” synergistic pore structure, with pore apertures strategically situated between the kinetic diameters of n ‐C 4 H 10 and iso ‐C 4 H 10 , thus enabling size‐exclusive molecular sieving. Furthermore, the large cages and 3D pore architecture confer both a high n ‐C 4 H 10 adsorption capacity (46.6 cm 3 /g) and a rapid adsorption rate (2.3 × 10 −12 m 2 s −1 ). Both kinetic analyses and DFT simulations provide mechanistic insights into the preferential adsorption and diffusion of n ‐C 4 H 10 . Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrate that SIFSIX‐TEPH‐Cu enables one‐step purification of both n ‐C 4 H 10 and iso ‐C 4 H 10 from their binary mixture under various conditions, such as high temperatures, high gas flow rates, and high humidities. After one separation cycle, 23.8 L kg −1 high‐purity iso ‐C 4 H 10 (>99.99%) and 27.8 L kg −1 n ‐C 4 H 10 (>99.0%) can be obtained, respectively.

title: Hofmeister Engineering Enables High‐Voltage Aqueous All‐Organic Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous all‐organic batteries (AOBs) offer a safe and sustainable alternative for electrochemical energy storage, yet their energy density is constrained by the limited availability of organic redox couples with high‐working voltages. Here we develop a versatile redox couple by pairing a 3,4,9,10‐perylenetetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) anode with a quaternary‐ammonium bromine cathode, enabling an initial discharge voltage of up to 2.0 V through reversible two‐electron bromine conversion (Br − /Br 0 /Br + ). This battery chemistry is compatible with diverse charge carriers, including Li + , Na + , K + , NH 4 + , Ca 2+ , and Mg 2+ . We further reveal that electrolyte ions exert distinct effects on electrode reactions: Cations primarily regulate reaction kinetics, whereas anions govern both reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect. Kosmotropic anions suppress polybromide dissolution and improve reversibility, but retard electrode kinetics, while chaotropic anions facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of active‐material retention. Guided by this mechanistic insight, a hybrid kosmotropic/chaotropic electrolyte balances these competing effects. The optimized one‐electron configuration retains 83.1% of its capacity after 12 000 cycles, while the two‐electron configuration delivers an energy density of approximately 107 Wh kg −1 based on the combined electrode active‐material mass. High areal capacities exceeding 4 mAh cm −2 further demonstrate its practical potential. This work establishes electrolyte solvation engineering as an effective strategy for high‐energy AOBs.

title: Single‐Vesicle Membrane Order‐Resolved Super‐Resolution Imaging Reveals Cholesterol Enrichment and Its Functional Role in Extracellular Vesicle Uptake
abstract: ABSTRACT Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are heterogeneous in membrane composition, yet conventional lipid analysis cannot resolve individual vesicles. Here we develop membrane order‐resolved, spectrally encoded super‐resolution imaging to simultaneously quantify membrane order and size at the single‐EV level. Combining Nile Red single‐molecule spectroscopy with localization microscopy achieves ∼30 nm resolution and reveals pronounced vesicle‐to‐vesicle heterogeneity. Using defined liposomes, cholesterol enrichment, and pharmacological inhibition, we establish membrane order as a sensitive surrogate for relative cholesterol content in individual EVs. Application to EVs from breast, gastric, and oral cell lines reveals cell‐type‐ and tissue‐dependent differences. Most cancer‐cell‐derived EVs show higher membrane order and higher inferred cholesterol than non‐tumor counterparts, although MDA‐MB‐231 EVs are an exception. Functional assays demonstrate that increasing EV membrane cholesterol enhances cellular uptake and shifts internalization from clathrin‐mediated to non‐clathrin‐mediated pathways. These findings identify cholesterol enrichment as a frequent feature of cancer‐cell‐derived EVs and link membrane composition to uptake efficiency and pathway selection. This work provides a single‐EV analytical platform and new insight into how membrane lipid heterogeneity regulates EV‐mediated intercellular communication.

title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Northern Hemisphere snow cover retreat poses substantial climate risks, but large uncertainties in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) hinder accurate projections of future evolution. We develop a monthly emergent constraint based on historical warming trends, which strongly correlate with ablation-season (May–October) snow cover loss. This constraint reduces inter-model variance by 17.0–58.4% under different emission scenarios and rectifies raw CMIP6 snow-loss biases. Constrained projections reveal that under the higher-emission scenario (SSP5-8.5), winter snow cover retreats in arid regions from the 2030 s, and Arctic summers become snow-free by the 2040 s. By mid-century, mid-latitude spring and autumn snow cover disappears, with arid and semi-arid regions approaching year-round snow-free conditions and humid regions losing 1–4 months of seasonal snow cover. Under the most sustainable scenario (SSP1-2.6) snow disappearance is delayed by 7.1–34 years relative to SSP5-8.5 across vulnerable regions and months. Overall, our constraint narrows projection uncertainty by 0.95–11.91 years, delaying projected disappearance by 0.01–2.65 years in transitional months while advancing it by 0.51–4.15 years in midsummer, providing refined month-specific baselines for climate risk assessments.

title: Computer vision links electroplated lithium morphology to lithium metal battery performance
abstract: Morphology is critical to materials research, yet its analysis often relies on subjective, qualitative observations that are difficult to quantify. Using lithium metal as a model, this study combines large-area automated microscopy with computer vision to establish quantitative descriptors of metal deposits. These measurements enable objective comparisons of lithium growth in different electrolytes and a combined criterion for rapid electrolyte screening. More broadly, this framework offers a transferable route toward quantitative, reproducible morphology analysis across materials science.
