title: Subambient Synthesis of Freestanding Monolayer Cubic ZrO2 Crystals with High Dielectric Permittivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) polymorphic materials offer access to unconventional crystal structures that trigger exotic properties and functionalities beyond equilibrium phases. However, extending this opportunity to metal oxides remains highly challenging because both thickness reduction and phase transformation involve large energy barriers in such strongly bonded ionic structures. Here we report an atomic-freezing conversion strategy that kinetically stabilizes freestanding 2D metastable oxide crystals under subambient conditions. Single-crystalline cubic ZrO2 of monolayer thickness is produced and stabilized below room temperature, although this phase is typically stable only at temperatures above 2000 °C in bulk. Structural analysis reveals that the layered ZrNCl precursor contains a Zr atomic framework that matches the (111) planes of cubic ZrO2. During conversion, suppressed atomic motion under low temperatures and 2D confinement preserves the nonequilibrium cubic structure. The resulting 2D cubic ZrO2 exhibits a high dielectric permittivity of ∼23.5 and enables MoS2 field-effect transistors with an on/off ratio of ∼108 and a subthreshold slope as low as 63.5 mV dec–1. This approach also applies to cubic HfO2 and tetragonal Bi2O3, providing a general kinetic route to bypass thermodynamic phase constraints and expanding access to metastable oxides in the 2D limit.

title: Mechanism of Zwitterionic Photochromism in Aza‐Diarylethenes Revealed by Direct Observation of a Closed‐Ring Intermediate
abstract: ABSTRACT Aza‐diarylethenes represent a unique class of photochromic molecules with reaction pathways inaccessible to conventional diarylethenes. Some aza‐diarylethenes form zwitterionic closed‐ring photoproducts, but direct experimental evidence for the elementary processes remains lacking. Here, we investigate the photochromic mechanism of a benzofuran‐fused aza‐diarylethene ( BF‐ADE ) using steady‐state spectroscopy, transient absorption spectroscopy, time‐resolved infrared spectroscopy, oxygen‐quenching experiments, single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction, and density functional theory calculations. These complementary studies demonstrate that photoirradiation ultimately affords the zwitterionic closed‐ring isomer BF‐ADE(c‐ Z ) , whereas thermal bleaching proceeds via the neutral closed‐ring isomer BF‐ADE(c) . Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy revealed a 1.6 ps process, and time‐resolved infrared spectroscopy provided direct evidence for the formation of the conventional closed‐ring intermediate BF‐ADE(c) within the first few picoseconds after photoexcitation. Oxygen‐quenching experiments and DFT calculations further showed that BF‐ADE(c‐ Z ) is generated predominantly from BF‐ADE(c) on the ground‐state potential energy surface rather than through a triplet‐mediated pathway. These results provide the first experimental validation of the proposed mechanism of zwitterionic photochromism in aza‐diarylethenes.

title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen‐containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice‐derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface‐confined spillover, its atomic‐scale dynamics in asymmetric multi‐site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross‐site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure–activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi‐atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self‐optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space–time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

title: Sensitive, Flexible Circularly Polarized Light Detection Driven by Circular Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Lead‐Free Double Perovskite Ferroelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT Circular bulk photovoltaic effect (CBPV) of ferroelectric materials can be utilized as a distinctive methodology to detect circularly polarized light (CPL), especially in the system of organic–inorganic hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics. However, currently reported CBPV predominantly focuses on lead‐containing hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics and the resultant CPL detectors are generally based on bulk crystals, hindering further applications of those materials. Here, sensitive, flexible CPL detection is successfully realized by using lead‐free double perovskite ferroelectrics, (C 6 H 5 CH 2 NH 3 ) 2 CsAgBiBr 7 (BCAB). Along with the spontaneous polarization, BCAB presents intriguing CBPV, which drives photovoltaic current highly dependent on the helicity of CPL. Consequently, CPL detectors using BCAB crystals deliver robust anisotropy factor up to 0.68 and high detectivity of 8.5 × 10 12 Jones at zero bias. More notably, BCAB single‐crystalline thin films can be obtained by mechanical exfoliation from its bulk crystals, allowing for flexible self‐powered CPL detection with a high anisotropy factor of 0.63 at specific bending angle. The value of 0.63 reaches the highest value among the reported flexible perovskite CPL detectors. As a proof‐of‐concept, our work offers a novel path to realize sensitive, flexible CPL detection and would be helpful to design lead‐free hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics for other advanced chiroptical devices.

title: Enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Radical Coupling Through Photoinduced Electron Donor–Acceptor Activation
abstract: ABSTRACT The enantioselective construction of C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bonds via radical pathways remains a formidable challenge, particularly when two transient alkyl radicals must be selectively coupled within a chiral catalytic environment. Here we report a photoinduced enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) radical coupling for the synthesis of α‐fluoroalkylated secondary alcohols, enabled by dual electron donor–acceptor (EDA) activation and chiral nickel catalysis. Central to this approach are two EDA activation events: one directly generates a primary alkyl radical from a carboxylic acid‐derived redox ester, whereas the other generates an alkoxy radical that undergoes intramolecular 1,2‐hydrogen atom transfer to form a secondary α‐oxy alkyl radical. Stereocontrolled interception of these radicals by a chiral nickel complex enables enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) bond formation. The reaction exhibits broad substrate scope and functional‐group tolerance, including the late‐stage functionalization of complex bioactive molecules. Mechanistic studies further support the proposed asymmetric radical coupling pathway.

title: Terminal Ligand Engineering of Clover‐Shaped Windows in Ligand‐Driven Local Pore‐Space‐Partitioned MOFs for Stepwise Enhancement of Propylene/Ethylene Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) and propylene (C 3 H 6 ) are core chemical feedstocks, and high‐purity products are critical for downstream polymer production. However, existing adsorbents generally suffer from poor compatibility between pores and target gas molecules. Herein, a ligand‐driven pore space partition strategy was proposed, whereby a cage‐like metal‒organic framework (JLU‐MOF113) was constructed through the self‐assembly of a benzothiadiazole‐functionalized ligand and trinuclear iron cluster. In the framework, the oriented thiadiazole rings on the ligands enable local pore space partition, forming clover‐shaped ultramicroporous windows. Taking JLU‐MOF113 as the parent framework, 1,2,4‐triazole (trz) and tetrazole (taz) were successfully introduced to replace coordinated H 2 O based on terminal ligand engineering. While further blocking the pore windows, the pore environment was optimized, resulting in the preparation of isostructural JLU‐MOF114/115. Through such stepwise regulation, the microenvironment of local pores in MOFs was successfully tailored, enabling a stepwise enhancement in separation selectivity for C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures. Among them, JLU‐MOF115 exhibits excellent selectivity that surpasses many known MOFs and can separate 73.8 L/kg −1 of C 2 H 4 with a purity of 99.95% from equimolar C 3 H 6 /C 2 H 4 mixtures. This work enriches MOFs with locally partitioned pore characteristics and provides a novel design strategy for the improvement of gas separation performance in MOFs.

title: Identification of Potent Target VDAC1 for Hepatocellular Carcinoma Therapy with the Natural Chloroxanthone–Xanthone Heterodimer Molecule Inducing Ferroptosis
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major cause of cancer‐related mortality, underscoring the need for actionable targets and effective small‐molecule therapeutics. Voltage‐dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), a key regulator of mitochondrial homeostasis, remains incompletely explored as a therapeutic target in HCC. From the endophytic fungus Penicillium sp. RM, we isolated two pairs of enantiomeric heterodimers ( 1 and 2 ) and their monomers ( 3 and 4 ). Penirmxanthone A ( 1 ) is the first reported chloroxanthone‐xanthone heterodimer, whereas penirmxanthone B ( 2 ) features a previously undescribed chloroxanthone‐gentisin scaffold. In vitro, (+)‐ 1 suppressed aggressive phenotypes of HCC cells and induced ferroptosis. Chemical proteomic, biophysical, and genetic analyses identified VDAC1 as a direct and functionally required target of (+)‐ 1 . Mechanistically, (+)‐ 1 engages VDAC1 through K239 and N241, destabilizes the V‐Set and Transmembrane Domain Containing 2 Like (VSTM2L)‐VDAC1‐Hexokinase 2 (HK2) complex, promotes VDAC1 oligomerization, and impairs mitochondrial membrane potential and energy metabolism, culminating in ferroptosis. VDAC1 knockout attenuated these effects, whereas VDAC1 re‐expression restored them. In vivo, VBIT‐4 diminished (+)‐ 1 ‐induced antitumor and ferroptosis‐related effects. Collectively, these findings identify (+)‐ 1 , to our knowledge, as the first natural product that directly targets VDAC1 to promote its oligomerization and induce ferroptosis, highlighting VDAC1 oligomerization as a potential therapeutic target in HCC.

title: Long‐Lived Fluorinated Foldamer Channels Conduct Protons Through a Plausible Confined Carbonyl–Water Relay
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial proton channels that combine high conductivity with strict exclusion of water and competing ions remain challenging. Herein, we report a series of fluorinated aromatic amide foldamers ( 1 ‐ 6 ) that intramolecularly fold into transmembrane channels with angstrom‐scale pores. The lead compound, channel 1 , features an intrinsic pore diameter of approximately 2.0 Å and mediates rapid H + transport across lipid bilayers, with an EC 50 value of 40 nM (∼6.0 x 10 −7 mol% relative to lipid), a single‐channel conductance of 196.2 pS, and long‐lived open states lasting up to 170 s. Notably, 1 displays high H + selectivity over Cl − , Na +, and K + (selectivity ratios of 192.0, 132.6, and 41.3, respectively) with no measurable enhancement of water permeability. Combined molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, DFT calculations, and hydrogen‐deuterium exchange experiments indicate a predominantly dehydrated pore and support a novel confined hybrid proton‐relay mechanism, in which pyridone carbonyl O‐atoms cooperate with one or a few (protonated) water species, distinct from conventional water‐wire conduction. Beyond its transport function, 1 induces apoptosis and exhibits potent anticancer activity, with IC 50 values of 2.7–5.4 µM against four cancer cell lines.

title: Stress‐Modulated Ionic Transport Limits Composite Cathode Kinetics in Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) require thick composite cathodes, yet these architectures exhibit heterogeneous reaction distributions that limit their performance. Here, we show that chemo‐mechanical transport switching governs the spatiotemporal lithiation behavior of such electrodes. By combining operando depth‐resolved diffraction with microstructure‐resolved and multi‐scale simulations, we link utilization gradients to the dominant transport pathway and demonstrate that the reversal of reaction fronts between charge and discharge arises from dynamically evolving transport limitations. This switching originates from the coupled reconfiguration of electronic and ionic transport networks during cycling. Particle breathing and interfacial delamination disrupt electronic percolation, whereas the contact‐mechanics model indicates that stress‐field interactions within the solid electrolyte (SE) can limit ionic transport. The model predicts that this suppression depends on the activation volume and elastic properties of the electrolyte and can exceed an order of magnitude as interparticle spacing decreases at high active‐material loadings. Our findings establish a direct link between chemo‐mechanical evolution and transport control in solid‐state cathodes, and highlight the need for SEs with low pressure sensitivity and sufficient mechanical compliance to enable high‐energy ASSB architectures.

title: Photothermal Upcycling of Waste Polyolefins to Ethylene and Propylene Over Waste Plastic‐Derived Carbon Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficient valorization of polyolefin wastes is challenged by the inertness of C─C bonds and the poor selectivity for olefins, which severely limits the conversion efficiency under mild conditions. Herein, a “treating waste with waste” strategy is proposed by using polypropylene waste derived carbon nanospheres (PP‐C) as the photothermal catalyst for polyethylene (PE) upgrading under focused Xenon light irradiation. Comprehensive characterizations identify that sp 2 ‐C domains with abundant edge defects of PP‐C serve as the catalytic active sites, which enable outstanding photothermal conversion and facilitate photogenerated charge separation. Theoretical calculations reveal that zigzag edges of sp 2 ‐structured graphene suppress the recombination of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby the localized electrons at the edge sites effectively weakens C─C bonds on the absorbed reactant and improves the photothermal catalytic efficiency. A remarkable olefin yield of ~60% with approximately 100% PE conversion is achieved within 10 min using PP‐C catalyst under sunlight condition, demonstrating great potential for practical applications. This work not only establishes a sustainable route for plastic valorization but also actively advances an innovative concept for the focused‐sunlight‐drives upgrading of polyolefins.

title: Sulfur Substitution of Oxygen‐Induced Multiferroic Phase Transition in Chiral Supramolecular Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiferroics exhibiting multiple ferroic orders have gained tremendous attention for decades owing to their intriguing properties and potential applications in future multifunctional devices. However, despite their unique advantages, such as inherent chirality—in contrast to traditional inorganic multiferroics, the design of molecular multiferroics with ferroelectricity and ferroelasticity remains a great challenge. Herein, through oxygen–sulfur (O/S) heavier congener substitution, we successfully designed the first chiral supramolecular ferroelectric–ferroelastic multiferroics [( R / S )‐1‐(2‐fluorophenyl)ethylamounium)(1‐thia‐15‐crown‐5)]BF 4 . We found that O/S substitution on parent chiral supramolecular compounds with no phase transition results in a 222F2‐type ferroelectric/ferroelastic multiferroic phase transition at 350 K, which can be attributed to the fact that the lower electronegativity of S than O weakens intermolecular interactions in the supramolecular system to reduce the energy barrier for molecular motions. Moreover, the O/S substitution induces remarkable chiral amplification, with the dissymmetry factor of the second‐harmonic generation circular dichroism (SHG‐CD) response one order of magnitude larger than that of the parent counterpart. Notably, such an SHG‐CD response can be switched from a high to a low state during the multiferroic phase transition. Our work opens up a new avenue for constructing multiferroic phase transitions in molecular systems and sheds light on the further exploration of chiral supramolecular multiferroics.

title: Efficient Chirality Transfer Enables Amplified Circularly Polarized Luminescence in Chiral Metal Halides Hybrid Structures
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral organic‐inorganic hybrid metal halides have aroused considerable interest for chiroptical applications. However, developing effective structural design strategies and elucidating the underlying chirality transfer mechanisms remain challenging. Herein, utilizing a structure‐directing strategy, two pairs of enantiomeric hybrid manganese chlorides including one‐dimensional (1D) structures [ R ‐/ S ‐(C 6 H 11 NO 2 ) 3 Mn]·[MnCl 4 ] (denoted as P ‐/ M ‐PCA‐2Mn) and R ‐/ S ‐(C 6 H 11 NO 2 )MnCl 2 (denoted as P ‐/ M ‐PCA‐Mn) were synthesized based on the chiral ligands ( R / S )‐(‐/+)‐piperidine‐3‐carboxylic acid (( R / S )‐(‐/+)‐C 6 H 12 ClNO 2 ). This approach also demonstrates generality and can be extended to systems incorporating different ligands. Magnetic susceptibility measurements revealed that antiferromagnetic spin arrangement may contribute to the 7‐fold emission efficiency enhancement in P ‐PCA‐Mn. Furthermore, the luminescent dissymmetry factor | g lum | value increased from 1.3 × 10 −3 in P ‐PCA‐2Mn to 4.2 × 10 −2 in P ‐PCA‐Mn, which is associated with stronger intramolecular hydrogen‐bonding interactions, more pronounced structural distortion, and an enhanced magnetic transition dipole moment, collectively suggesting their potential contributions to the improved circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) performance. Through integration with liquid crystals, stepwise CPL amplification was achieved, elevating | g lum | to the 10 −1 order of magnitude, which exhibits the enantioselectivity of asymmetric photopolymerization. This work confirms the effectiveness of a structure‐directing strategy in boosting both luminescence efficiency and chirality transfer in chiral hybrid metal halides, and presents a novel and efficient platform for regulating CPL properties.

title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Ring Cleavage of Naphthols Enabling Structural Diversification
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural modification of aromatic frameworks by breaking core C─C bonds is challenging due to their inherent stability. Herein, we introduce an electrochemical dearomative ring‐cleavage method that converts readily available β ‐naphthols into synthetically versatile, stereodefined ring‐opened esters with broad functional‐group tolerance. Further ring reconstructions provided various carbocycles and heterocycles, highlighting the synthetic versatility of this strategy for the skeletal modification of aromatic frameworks. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate isolation, cyclic voltammetry, and electrode surface analysis, support a stepwise multielectron oxidation process. In this approach, controlled anodic oxidation, cathodically generated nucleophiles, and proton‐coupled electron transfer collectively govern chemo‐ and stereoretentive C─C bond cleavage.

title: A Programmable α‐Aminonitrile Platform for Tunable and Stimulus‐Responsive Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) Delivery
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite increasing evidence that endogenous cyanide participates in cellular signaling, its biological functions remain poorly understood because programmable chemical control over hydrogen cyanide (HCN) delivery has been unavailable. Here we establish a general chemical framework that enables controlled HCN delivery by exploiting the retro ‐Strecker reactiveity of α‐aminonitriles under physiologically compatible conditions. We uncover a predictable structure–reactivity relationship that allows HCN release kinetics to be rationally programmed over more than three orders of magnitude, with half‐lives ranging from 2.9 to 9165 min, primarily through nitrogen‐centered electronic effects with additional steric and conformational modulation. This unified framework further supports multiple modes of molecular control, enabling esterase‐responsive intracellular HCN delivery, ROS‐responsive activation that protects against ischemia–reperfusion injury in both OGD/R cells and MCAO mice, and bioorthogonally triggered HCN generation that suppresses LPS‐induced TNF‐α production in macrophages. Together, these studies establish α‐aminonitriles as an enabling platform that converts cyanide from an experimentally intractable toxic molecule into a chemically programmable signaling entity, providing a molecular foundation for systematic investigation of cyanide biology and its therapeutic potential.

title: Partial Solvation Promotes Chlorate Formation on Sea Salt Crystal Surfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Partial solvation creates interfacial environments that are neither dry solids nor bulk solutions, yet how this intermediate state controls chemical reactivity remains poorly understood. Here, we show that partial solvation at relative humidities far below deliquescence activates unexpected redox chemistry at ionic salt surfaces. Using surface‐sensitive X‐ray spectroscopy, we observe chlorate formation on Arctic sea‐salt crystals and an independent natural salt system following exposure to water vapor, whereas chlorate is absent under dry conditions. Chlorate formation is associated with partially solvated, MgCl 2 ‐enriched surface domains. First‐principles molecular dynamics simulations reveal strong interfacial electric fields and undercoordinated hydroxide environments, providing physicochemical conditions compatible with charge separation and radical‐mediated oxidation. Our results identify partial solvation as a previously overlooked regime for activating chemical transformations at ionic surfaces and establish partially solvated salt surfaces as distinct reactive environments bridging solid‐state and aqueous‐phase chemistry.

title: Dipole‐Polarized Tri‐Pore COF Delivers Electrons to an O 2 ‐Enriched Pore for H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Although covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ordered and tunable, the structural homogeneity of conventional COFs leaves charge delivery and O 2 activation spatially and functionally uncoupled, limiting both H 2 O 2 selectivity and yield. Here, we report a three‐component, tri‐pore COF by integrating para‐phenylenediamine into a binary fluorenone‐pyrene framework. The asymmetric tri‐pore architecture selectively channels O 2 into one pore before reduction, while the built‐in dipole polarization field‌ directs electrons to the O 2 ‐occupied pore. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy shows excited‐state carrier lifetime is doubled, thereby enabling exclusive electron delivery to that O 2 ‐preconcentrated pore. Molecular dynamics simulations and in situ infrared spectroscopy further reveal favorable O 2 adsorption behavior and an *OOH‐mediated pathway. The COF exhibits a photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production rate of 6.04 mmol g − 1 h − 1 in pure water under O 2 , surpassing its two single‐pore counterparts by respective factors of 18.9 and 6.4. An 18.9‐fold increase in the reaction rate, far exceeding the 3.0‐fold enhancement in the electric field, is not another routine charge‐separation effect but a pore‐specific charge‐delivery effect: electrons are shuttled to the pore where O 2 has already been adsorbed, and *OOH is formed predominantly at that O 2 ‐enriched pore. For next‐generation COF photocatalysts, delivering O 2 mass transport to the catalytic pore should be prioritized over simply enhancing the electric field.

title: Vibrational Strong Coupling of Hydrogen‐Bonding Solvent Modes Modulates Proton Transfer in Wieland–Miescher Ketone Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Vibrational strong coupling (VSC) is emerging as an efficient tool for influencing chemical reactions within an optical cavity. Here, we report the enhancement of ground‐state proton transfer in a multistep Robinson annulation reaction by directly coupling the cavity mode to a selective solvent vibrational mode that is absent in the reactants. Being a hydrogen‐bond‐donating solvent, methanol facilitates proton transfer via a hydrogen‐bonding network, and this proton transfer is further enhanced under VSC. An increase in the product formation upon coupling to the solvent O─H and reactant C═O stretch suggests a unique role of the cavity‐coupling of specific vibrational modes involved in the rate‐determining step (RDS) of the reaction. In this context, the intrinsic intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) lifetime of the two modes acts as a key factor in determining the reaction outcome under VSC. Moreover, we find that VSC involving these modes also impacts stereoselectivity, leading to an increased enantiomeric excess (ee). This demonstration of enhanced yield and enantioselectivity under VSC highlights the pivotal role of solvent‐mode coupling in facilitating ground‐state proton transfer through hydrogen‐bonding networks, paving the way for mode‐selective control in complex multistep reactions.

title: A Phosphinidene‐Bridged P 6 Platform for Phosphorus Framework Editing, Fragment Transfer, and Derivatization
abstract: ABSTRACT White phosphorus (P 4 ) is an indispensable feedstock for organophosphorus synthesis, yet strategies for the controlled manipulation of P 4 ‐derived polyphosphorus frameworks remain rare. Here, we report a phosphinidene‐mediated strategy that converts P 4 into a phosphinidene‐bridged hexaphosphane, which functions as a versatile P 6 platform rather than merely an isolable P 4 ‐derived framework. This scaffold undergoes controlled P─P bond reorganization, P 4 release, phosphinidene transfer, heteroelement insertion, and selective derivatization, providing access to phosphorus species spanning P 1 to P 8 . Mechanistic studies with water, cyclic(alkyl)(amino) carbenes (CAACs), and N‐heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) reveal dynamic phosphorus‐fragment transfer and carbene‐mediated framework reorganization through phosphinidene‐containing intermediates. Extension to aluminum(I) chemistry affords structurally diverse Al─P clusters that can be converted into value‐added phosphorus products including PH 3 and PMe 3 . These results establish phosphinidene‐functionalized polyphosphorus frameworks as promising synthetic platforms for the controlled molecular manipulation of elemental phosphorus.

title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO 4 : From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid growth of LiFePO 4 (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ H f ), migration barriers ( E a ), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy ( λ ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Synergy Enables Neon/Helium Separation in an Anion‐Pillared Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Separating neon (Ne) from helium (He) remains challenging because both gases are chemically inert and weakly interacting, while classical size‐sieving principles predict faster transport for the smaller He atom. Here we address this challenge with the anion‐pillared metal–organic framework (MOF) Ni(4‐DPDS) 2 CrO 4 , whose confined pores combine narrow apertures with electrostatically heterogeneous cavities. This environment provides multiple weak contacts that favor Ne adsorption while producing an inverse diffusional response relative to the expected size trend. At 77 K and 100 kPa, the framework adsorbs 50.63 cm 3 g −1 of Ne but only 0.40 cm 3 g −1 of He in static adsorption, with a kinetic Ne/He selectivity of 113.58. Fixed‐bed experiments afford He with a purity above 99.999%, followed by temperature‐driven recovery of Ne with a purity above 99.7%. The results show that coordinating adsorption thermodynamics with molecular transport offers a route to separating weakly interacting gases beyond equilibrium affinity or classical size sieving alone.

title: d 5 ‐Probed Interlocked Charge‐Structural Disorder Enables Deep Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ Redox Chemistry in Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based layered oxide cathodes are attractive for next‐generation rechargeable batteries, owing to their abundant resources and rich redox chemistry, but achieving reversible deep Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ redox remains challenging. Herein, we developed an interlocked charge‐structural disorder protocol in P2‐derived Na 0.67 Fe 0.1 Mn 0.9 O 2 to regulate Mn redox and stabilize discharge voltage. A disordered cation framework is engineered through electronic configuration and atomic rearrangement, where Fe 3+ (d 5 , half‐filled) breaks charge periodicity, and rapid quenching prevents structural reordering to eliminate Fe/Mn order. Electron energy‐loss spectroscopy (EELS) reveals suppressed Mn 4+ /Mn 3+ charge ordering, which enables extended Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ redox as confirmed by soft x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (sXAS). The optimized cathode quenched at 700°C nearly doubles the Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ redox contribution within the Mg‐compatible window (1.8–1.6 V vs. Mg 2+ /Mg) from 15.2% to 29.4%, and it delivers 291.3 Wh kg −1 energy density (based on the mass of active cathode) with capacity retention increased from 62.4% to 87.5% over 50 cycles. Mechanistically, the interlocked disorder lowers the migration barrier by flattening the electrostatic‐potential landscape and enhances the thermodynamic driving force for Mn 3+ /Mn 2+ by destabilizing Jahn–Teller correlations. This work establishes charge‐state disorder as a versatile design principle for layered oxide cathodes, enabling deep, reversible transition‐metal redox for advanced energy storage.

title: Enantioselective Enyne Cyclization to Thermodynamically Favored Endocyclic Alkenes via a Rhodium‐Migration Relay
abstract: ABSTRACT Transition‐metal‐catalyzed addition/cyclizations of electrophile‐tethered alkynes constitute one of the most powerful and broadly applicable strategies for the step‐economical construction of cyclic alkenes. However, these reactions overwhelmingly furnish exocyclic products because the catalytic cycle typically terminates upon kinetically favored ring closure, even though the corresponding endocyclic alkenes are thermodynamically more stable. Herein, we report a catalytic enantioselective arylative cyclization of 1,n‐enynes that directly delivers thermodynamically favored endocyclic alkenes bearing an exocyclic stereogenic carbon center in high yields with excellent chemo‐ and enantioselectivities. Deuterium‐labeling experiments and control studies support a pathway in which the catalytic sequence, rather than terminating after the initial arylative ring closure, continues through a formally circuitous relay of sequential 1,2‐, 1,3‐, and 1,4‐rhodium migrations. This migration relay ultimately transposes the C═C bond to the thermodynamically favored endocyclic position, stereospecifically transfers chirality to the exocyclic stereogenic carbon center, and returns rhodium to its initial carbon attachment site. This work not only establishes a distinct mode of catalytic cyclization but also elucidates the previously unknown mechanism underlying this unusual reactivity.

title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
abstract: ABSTRACT Band‐filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid‐band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π‐conjugated electron‐donating molecules are covalently linked to form one‐dimensional pore channels. The introduction of a well‐defined amount of electron‐accepting molecules without disrupting the framework structure enabled the first successful demonstration of the deliberate band‐filling control while elucidating the charge state through various spectroscopic measurements. Enhanced electronic itinerancy facilitated by host–guest charge transfer was evidenced by spectroscopic, transport, and magnetic measurements in support of theoretical calculations. The present study opens a new avenue for exploring more advanced electronic organic solids based on band‐filling engineering.

title: Conformational Locking in Covalent Organic Frameworks Promotes Coupled H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Organic Valorization
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a compelling platform for coupling photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) production with organic valorization. However, the practical efficiency remains limited by rapid electron‐hole recombination. Inspired by the conformational rigidity and planar geometry imposed by peptide bonds, we develop a conformational locking strategy that introduces a fused‐ring linker, which restricts backbone rotation and thereby enhances framework planarity and conjugation, affording a series of COFs (TFPPy‐DATMBP, TFPPy‐DABP, and TFPPy‐DAPy) with progressively improved planarity and conjugation. The conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy achieves an impressive H 2 O 2 production rate of 119.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , with an apparent quantum yield up to 29.14% at 410 nm, while delivering a yield of >98% toward the high‐value imine product. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy extends the lifetime of the long‐lived charge‐separated state by approximately 10‐fold to 102.87 ps, compared with 10.34 ps for TFPPy‐DATMBP. This work establishes TFPPy‐DAPy as an efficient photocatalyst for fine chemical co‐production, and provides a generalizable molecular‐level design strategy for developing advanced catalysts across diverse photocatalytic applications.

title: Temporal Fidelity Reveals Transient Dissolution Chemistry at Dynamic Electrocatalyst Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic electrocatalyst dissolution consists of short‐lived, potential‐dependent interfacial events tied to surface redox, reconstruction, and catalysis. Accurate interpretation of these processes requires preserving the temporal link between metal release and electrochemical state, but this link is often lost in electrochemical inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (EC‐ICP‐MS) due to transport‐induced signal convolution. Here we reduce this distortion by using thin‐layer hydrodynamic confinement to improve near‐electrode convective removal. Paired‐pulse dissolution experiments show that two consecutive 2 s dissolution inputs separated by 50 ms remain distinguishable. Cu‐pulse residence‐time‐distribution measurements and computational fluid dynamics further identify electrode‐region convective coverage and near‐electrode flow velocity as key determinants of signal broadening. Applying this temporal fidelity to representative noble‐metal, carbide, nitride, hydroxide, oxide, and single‐atom interfaces under fast cyclic voltammetry reveals distinct dynamic dissolution fingerprints. This approach further resolves weak reoxidation‐associated Ir dissolution from reduced IrO x and oxygen‐reduction‐associated suppression of spontaneous Cu release from Cu–N–C. These results highlight the importance of temporal fidelity for assigning transient dissolution chemistry at dynamic electrocatalyst interfaces.

title: Highly Adaptable Electrochemical Lithium Extraction From Brine via Heterojunction Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical lithium extraction from salt‐lake brines has received extensive attention due to its low energy consumption, environmental friendliness, and high efficiency. However, conventional electrode materials suffer from sluggish desolvation kinetics and competing cations intercalation (Na + ) in the diverse brine environment across the world. Herein, a heterojunction engineering strategy was proposed to solve the above challenges. A lithium titanium oxides (LTO) heterojunction was rationally designed and constructed on the surface of LiFePO 4 (named LFP‐SEF), which could expedite the desolvation process of Li + via the induced built‐in electric field and suppress competing cation intercalation via size sieving. Consequently, the LFP‐SEF‐based device consistently delivers outstanding lithium extraction performance in a series of brines (Na/Li ≈ 1–150) around the world. Even in the brine from southern Tibet (Dangxiongcuo Salt Lake) with a high Na/Li mass ratio of 150, LFP‐SEF also exhibits 83.72% capacity retention after 50 cycles with high separation factor (Na/Li ≈ 989.80; Mg/Li ≈1856.50). The exceptional performance is preserved as the device size increases from lab‐scale to production‐scale (1.5 m 2 ), demonstrating its excellent industrialization prospects. The concept of heterojunction engineering proposed in this work opens a promising route to industrial‐scale lithium extraction in complex brine environment.

title: Magnetic Switching of Exciton Lifetime in CrSBr
abstract: ABSTRACT Exciton dynamics in layered magnetic semiconductors provide a sensitive probe of the interplay between spin order and light–matter interaction. Here, we study thin CrSBr layers using time‐resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy in an external magnetic field, revealing a step‐like reduction in the exciton lifetime from 11 to 7 ps during the magnetization flip from the antiferromagnetic to the ferromagnetic phase. The reduction of the exciton lifetime in the ferromagnetic phase persists below the Néel temperature, as evidenced by its strong magnetic‐field dependence that disappears in the paramagnetic phase. Ab initio calculations reveal a one‐dimensional nature of free excitons, accompanied by a pronounced change in the oscillator strength across the magnetic phase transition, predicting a shorter radiative lifetime of free excitons in the antiferromagnetic phase of CrSBr, contradicting the experimental observations. This discrepancy is explained by strong localization of excitons at low temperature. We show both experimentally and theoretically that the observed magnetic switching of the exciton lifetime is attributed to a larger exciton localization volume leading to a larger oscillator strength in the ferromagnetic phase. The results show that disorder‐induced localization effects play a key role in exciton dynamics in CrSBr.

title: Data‐Driven Conformational Mismatch Design Enables Extreme‐Temperature Energy Storage in Copolyimides
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐temperature capacitive energy storage requires polymer dielectrics to combine a wide optical bandgap ( E g ) with a high glass‐transition temperature ( T g ), properties that are often difficult to optimize simultaneously through conventional backbone design. Here, we introduce conformational mismatch into semi‐alicyclic polyimide copolymers and identify promising monomer combinations through a multistage workflow integrating machine‐learning prediction of T g , density‐functional‐theory calculations of electronic structure, and molecular‐dynamics analysis of chain conformations. Incorporating a methyl‐substituted diamine yields Co‐PI‐tC, in which local conformational mismatch modifies molecular fluctuations and chain packing while suppressing thermally activated charge transport. Conformational entropy estimates derived from atomic fluctuations quantitatively capture these changes and complement conventional structural and electronic descriptors. The resulting Co‐PI‐tC film combines a T g of 271.52°C with E g of 4.28 eV, delivers a discharged energy density of 8.6 J cm −3 at 200°C with 90% efficiency and retains 6.7 J cm −3 at 250°C, setting a high‐temperature energy‐storage record among reported copolymer dielectrics. These results establish conformational mismatch as an effective molecular‐design strategy for reconciling thermal stability and electrical insulation in high‐temperature polymer dielectrics.

title: An Electrically Gated Solid‐State Thermal Transistor for Energy‐Efficient Thermal Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Vapor‐compression heating and cooling systems dominate modern thermal management, yet their efficiency and scalability remain constrained by mechanical complexity and refrigerant‐based operation. Solid‐state approaches offer an attractive alternative, with recent demonstrations showing the potential for highly efficient, compact thermal control. Here we demonstrate an electrically gated solid‐state thermal transistor based on bulk single‐crystal barium titanate, achieving a switching ratio of 1.6, among the highest reported for bulk ferroelectrics. We further introduce switching efficiency as a figure of merit, reaching ∼8.52 cm 3 J −1 , more than two orders of magnitude higher than that of the highest‐performing reported thermal switch, PbZrO 3 . Unlike previous thermal switches that operate between two discrete states, this device provides continuously tunable thermal‐conductivity states, enabling transistor‐like modulation and amplification of heat flow. In situ x‐ray diffraction combined with first‐principles calculations shows that switching originates from anisotropic phonon transport between ferroelectric domains. Integrated into a proof‐of‐concept thermal‐management system, the device shifts the baseline temperature of a miniature human analog by ∼0.6°C at a cycle‐averaged power input of 33 µW cm −2 , approximately ninefold lower than a vapor‐compression heat pump performing the same task. These results establish ferroelectric thermal transistors as a programmable, energy‐efficient platform for solid‐state thermal management.

title: Resolving topological obstructions to vectorial structured field control
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The use of structured matter, such as optical retarders, for vectorial control is a well-established and widely used technique in modern optics, and has driven continued advances in the manipulation of complex, spatially varying vectorial fields. However, achieving arbitrary field conversion typically requires the use of cascaded elements, as intrinsic physical and fabrication constraints fundamentally limit individual devices to a restricted subset of transformations. This results in an overall continuous transformation potentially failing to be continuous at the level of the parameters of the cascade, leading to detrimental engineering consequences such as the introduction of complex, discontinuous aberrations that disrupt important topological properties of the underlying light and matter fields. In this work, we establish a mathematical framework for analyzing the topological difficulties that emerge in the decomposition of an overall transformation into individual layers, and for determining the minimal depth required to overcome them. The strategy introduced provides a general pathway for optimizing designs for vectorial field control and matter field generation, with particular importance for the manipulation of topological phases in optical polarization fields, such as Stokes skyrmions, where continuity is of vital importance.

title: Characterizing ocean flows with the scattering transform
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a useful statistical descriptor of these flows, it cannot always distinguish between different types of motion. We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics. Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

title: Misremembered social networks are predictions of the future in disguise
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mistakes in how the brain processes social network information in the present can predict the network’s future state.

title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual–auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory–visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

title: Breakdown of the classical rupture theory and earthquake propagation in the “forbidden” super-Rayleigh range
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Earthquakes propagating faster than the shear wave-speed are commonly thought to undergo a supershear transition upon which they discontinuously jump from the sub-Rayleigh regime to the supershear one. The super-Rayleigh regime, i.e., the range of propagation speeds between the Rayleigh and shear wave-speeds, is regarded as “forbidden” by the two-dimensional classical rupture theory. Here, we revisit the assumptions underlying the classical theory and develop a rupture theory that takes into account the dependence of the fault strength (frictional resistance) on the slip rate. The theory quantitatively agrees with numerical simulations nearly up to the Rayleigh wave-speed. Yet, very close to the latter, numerical rupture solutions change their character due to frictional rate nonlinearity, involving rate-strengthening friction, and rupture continuously propagates through the “forbidden” super-Rayleigh range into the supershear regime, without a sharp supershear transition. These results demonstrate that frictional rate dependence, generically observed in experiments, can have profound implications for fast earthquake propagation.

title: TREX1 and TREX2 3′ → 5′ DNA exonucleases enhance the fidelity of translesion synthesis by DNA polymerase θ
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A multiplicity of translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases (Pols) promote replication through DNA lesions in an error-free or error-prone manner. Among these Pols, Polθ operates in an error-prone manner. However, Polθ conducts TLS in human cells in a much more error-free manner than implicated from the high error-proneness of the purified Pol. To resolve this incongruity, here we show that the TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonucleases are integral components of TLS mediated by Polθ. In TREX1- or TREX2-deficient cells, Polθ-dependent TLS becomes nonoperational and chromosomal instability rises similar to that in Polθ-deficient cells. Consequently, similar to that in Polθ
                    −/−
                    mice,
                    
                      trex2
                      −/−
                    
                    mice exhibit increased susceptibility to ultraviolet-induced skin cancers. Furthermore, our findings that in the absence of TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonuclease activities, Polθ-mediated TLS manifests high mutagenicity, and an increase in the diversity of misincorporated nucleotides demarcate a crucial role of these exonucleases in the removal of Polθ misinsertions and, thereby, in enhancing Polθ TLS fidelity and the consequent genome stability.

title: Multimodal robotic matter enabled by unified magnetic control primitives
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Robotic matter seeks to achieve collective functionality through interactions among modular units governed by global control signals. A persistent challenge is identifying control frameworks that are simultaneously scalable and deterministic. Here, we introduce a unified magnetic control paradigm that enables multimodal robotic matter using a minimal set of global-field primitives. We show that combinations of rotating and pulsed uniform fields, together with controlled field gradients, are sufficient to generate diverse behaviors—including multimodal locomotion, deterministic bottom-up assembly, and rapid, reversible shape morphing in origami-inspired modular robots. Each module incorporates permanent magnets with prescribed chirality and magnetic moment, encoding mechanical and magnetic asymmetries that map global field inputs to predictable forces, torques, and deformation pathways. Using a programmable three-dimensional Helmholtz coil system, we demonstrate four locomotion modes (rolling, steering, sliding, and walking), hierarchical assembly of three-dimensional robotic architectures, and millisecond-timescale transitions among discrete stable states, with applications to origami state machines and global shape change for navigation through confined spaces. By unifying locomotion, assembly, and reconfiguration within a single control framework, this work establishes a generalizable approach to magnetic robotic matter in which multifunctional collective behaviors emerge from a minimal set of control primitives.

title: The Yersinia pestis effector YopM binds the human pyrin death domain to inhibit inflammasome activation and effector-triggered immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Bacteria in the genus
                    Yersinia
                    use type III secretion to inject several effectors into phagocytes to disrupt signaling. Two effectors disrupt host signaling by inactivation of RhoA, triggering pyrin inflammasome assembly in infected phagocytes and protective immunity. A third protein, YopM, counteracts effector-triggered immunity by binding to and inactivating pyrin. Prior evidence suggested that gain of function codon changes in the pyrin gene
                    MEFV
                    that cause Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and provide resistance to
                    Yersinia pestis
                    were selected to evade YopM binding. YopM was shown to bind an N-terminal region of human pyrin, which includes the eponymous pyrin domain (PYD), however, the interaction mechanism was undefined. Using bacterial two-hybrid assay, protein biochemistry, and X-ray crystallography, we determined that YopM binds to the PYD, which has few validated FMF amino acid variants. We show that YopM binds PYD R42, a “Site 2” amino acid important for positive and negative regulation of pyrin and that binding to the R42W variant is reduced. YopM amino acid change variants defective for PYD binding failed to inhibit the pyrin inflammasome in human monocytes infected with
                    Yersinia
                    . In addition, PYD binding was dispensable for YopM to inhibit the inflammasome in murine macrophages, suggesting this effector uses a distinct mechanism to target mouse pyrin. These results define that
                    Y. pestis
                    YopM binds to human PYD to promote pathogenesis, and because Site 2 variants that evade YopM binding have low gain of function inflammasome activity, these data may explain why most validated FMF codon changes are in other domains of pyrin.

title: A sweeping twist defect as a topological flagellum that enhances colloid translation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nematic liquid crystals can dramatically reconfigure under dynamic forcing, providing exciting opportunities in active matter. Here, we study a disk colloid with hybrid planar and homeotropic anchoring rotated by an external magnetic field which generates a dynamic companion topological defect. The disk moves faster when the defect sweeps across the disk’s face. We identify the defect as a nonsingular twist wall, characterize the twist energy landscape, and identify that the sweeping motion is driven by a topological instability. As the defect sweeps, it reverses the handedness of twist and lowers the free energy in the fluid in the gap above the disk. Landau–de Gennes modeling shows that the sweeping wall behaves as a propagating director texture: the director field is nearly stationary in the wall frame, while nematogens rotate locally as the wall passes. The nematogens’ rotation generates a viscous stress on the surface of the disk that hastens its propulsion. Thus, the defect acts as a flagellum that powers colloid swimming, providing an example of a dissipative topological structure whose dynamics can be harnessed to perform useful work.

title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Helicobacter pylori
                    infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

title: Tuning microswimmer motility by liposome encapsulation: A membrane clutch enables controlled swimming and cargo transport
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. Nevertheless, the underlying motility mechanisms from a hydrodynamic perspective are often unresolved, and reliable velocity control remains challenging. In the present study, we use our previously introduced biohybrid system termed the chlamylipo, in which the motile alga
                    Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
                    is encapsulated within a giant liposome, as a model system to investigate how liposome encapsulation regulates microswimmer motility under controlled perturbations. From a fluid mechanical perspective, we establish a deformation-velocity expression that incorporates liposome radius, beating frequency, and membrane protrusion. We further show that motility can be reversibly switched by incorporating light-responsive lipids, with the liposome acting as a “clutch” that modulates membrane protrusion. To demonstrate its transport function, we further show cargo loading, carrying, and triggered release. These results show that liposome encapsulation can convert a motile microorganism into a controllable carrier, with the membrane acting as a clutch that regulates swimming and, therefore, cargo transport.

title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high-
                    Z
                    interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

title: Mechanical instability generates monodisperse colloidosomes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Formation and rupture of vesicles are fundamental processes underlying diverse phenomena in biology, materials science, and biomedical applications. Vesicles form when the area of a growing disk-like membrane reaches the instability point at which the energy barrier to the disk-to-vesicle transition vanishes. Observing such topological transitions in lipid bilayers is a challenge because of their nanoscale dimensions and rapid dynamics. We study a scaled-up model of membranes assembled from rod-shaped colloidal particles. The unique features of colloidal membranes enable the real-time visualization of spontaneous vesicle closure driven by an instability arising from competition between edge and bending energies that is universal to all membrane-based materials. A continuum theory with independently measured material parameters quantitatively predicts the instability point for vesicle formation and intermediate membrane conformations during the disk-to-vesicle transition. The instability generates monodisperse, selectively permeable colloidosomes whose size is controlled by gravity and membrane elasticity, providing a scalable and programmable platform for diverse applications.

title: Design of ionic self-assembled monolayers suppressing proton release to mitigate proton-based degradation of perovskite solar cells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) serve as effective hole-transport layers (HTLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), facilitating energy-level alignment and defect passivation at perovskite interfaces. However, their integration is limited by weak anchoring to transparent conducting oxides (TCOs), resulting in desorption during deposition and the release of acidic protons, which react with components of the perovskite leading to degradation [T. Li et al., Nature 648, 84–90 (2025) and C. Fei et al., Science 391, eadz7969 (2026)]. To strengthen anchoring between the SAM and TCO while simultaneously mitigating proton-induced degradation of the perovskite, we have prepared ionic SAMs featuring a phosphonate anchoring group and a perovskite-compatible cation. The benchmark SAMs, [2-(3,6-dimethoxy-9

                    as the HTL in lead-based PSCs results in devices with a PCE of 26.53%, outperforming the PCE of 24.97% for the Me-4PACz-based device. After heating at 85°C for over 1,000 h, the [FA]
                    +
                    [Me-4PACz]
                    −
                    -based device retained ca. 88% of its initial efficiency. This study establishes the broad utility of ionic SAMs as versatile compounds to concurrently increase device efficiency and long-term stability.

title: Age-associated B cells drive lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in Faslpr mice through the p38α−CXCL10 signaling axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Defective Fas cell surface death receptor (FAS) signaling leads to lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder, yet the mechanisms involved remain unclear. Using genetic mouse models homozygous for the lymphoproliferation spontaneous mutation (
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    ), we showed that age-associated B cells (ABCs) were critical drivers of lymphadenopathy and autoimmunity. Single-cell transcriptomics of lymph node immune cells in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice revealed a marked expansion of ABCs. Depletion of these ABCs in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice significantly restrained lymph node enlargement and alleviated autoimmune manifestations, whereas adoptive transfer of ABCs from
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice to wild-type mice exacerbated disease pathology. Mechanistically, p38α signaling emerged as a critical regulator of ABC differentiation and function, and conditional deletion of p38α in CD11c
                    +
                    cells profoundly suppressed ABC expansion and ameliorated autoimmune manifestations in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice. Furthermore, we identified CXCL10 as an important downstream effector of p38α signaling in ABCs that drives autoimmune disorder. Neutralization of CXCL10 significantly attenuated disease severity in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice. Although clinical relevance analyses of autoimmune patient cohorts revealed a parallel expansion of ABCs in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and primary Sjögren’s syndrome, ABCs with higher p38α content were specifically enriched in SLE patients. Together, these findings identify p38α-driven ABCs as an important regulator of lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice and suggest that targeting the p38α−CXCL10 axis in ABCs may be a therapeutic strategy for treating this autoimmune disease.

title: A deep-learning-boosted framework for quantum sensing with nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a versatile quantum sensing platform for high sensitivity measurements of magnetic fields, temperature, and strain with nanoscale spatial resolution. A common bottleneck is the analysis of optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra, where target quantities are encoded in resonance features. Conventional nonlinear fitting is often computationally expensive, sensitive to initialization, and prone to failure at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Here we introduce a robust, efficient machine learning (ML) framework for real-time ODMR analysis based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). The model performs direct parameter inference without initial guesses or iterative optimization, and is naturally parallelizable on graphics processing units (GPU) for high-throughput processing. We validate the approach on both synthetic and experimental datasets, showing improved throughput, accuracy, and robustness than standard nonlinear fitting, with the largest gains in the low-SNR regime. We further validate our methods in two representative sensing applications: diagnosing intracellular temperature changes using nanodiamond probes and widefield magnetic imaging of superconducting vortices in a high-temperature superconductor. This deep-learning inference framework enables fast and reliable extraction of physical parameters from complex ODMR data and provides a scalable route to real-time quantum sensing and imaging.

title: A nanoscale gap junction–perinexus nanodomain governs balance of ephaptic and gap-junctional activation in excitable cell pairs
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Electrical communication between excitable cells depends on gap junction (GJ) currents and field-mediated ephaptic interactions, but their relative contributions have been difficult to quantify, limiting insight into arrhythmia and other disorders of bioelectric signaling. Building on the nanoscale, sodium channel-rich perinexus at the cardiac intercalated disc, we developed a “Single-on-Paired” (SoP) preparation, recording whole-cell sodium current from one adult ventricular myocyte that remains coupled by an intercalated disc to an intact partner. This revealed a composite two-cell sodium current with two rising-phase slopes and an activation jump between closely spaced voltage steps, an “Intercalated Disc Signature” (IDS) absent from isolated single myocytes and providing a direct readout of intercellular activation. Rapid sodium channel activation cannot be resolved under voltage clamp at physiological extracellular sodium ([Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    ), so SoP recordings used reduced [Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    of 25 to 35 mM. Within this nonphysiologic range, graded GJ inhibition, perinexal widening with an Scn1b-derived competitive adhesion peptide, and [Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    modulation showed that GJ inhibition abolished the IDS at 25 mM, whereas a modest 10 mM rise to 35 mM restored it despite persistent GJ inhibition. GJ coupling and a perinexus-centered ephaptic mechanism are thus separable contributors to intercellular activation whose relative engagement is set by extracellular sodium. A two-cell computational model constrained by these data reproduces the IDS and predicts that at physiological 145 mM [Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    with reduced GJ conductance, perinexus-centered ephaptic mechanisms suffice for intercellular activation. Clamping cleft potential, but not cleft sodium, disrupts this behavior in silico, identifying cleft potential as the proximal ephaptic signal.

title: Pinning of Van Hove singularities and correlated insulators in M-valley twisted transition metal dichalcogenides
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We investigate the role of long-range Coulomb interactions in M-valley moirés using the self-consistent Hartree–Fock approximation. This platform was recently proposed [D. Călugăru et al.,
                    Nature
                    643
                    , 376–381 (2025) and C. Lei
                    et al., Phys. Rev. Lett.
                    135
                    , 196402 (2025)] as a new class of experimentally realizable moiré materials using twisted transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) homobilayers with the 1T structure. While these seminal studies considered the noninteracting theory without an electric displacement field, this work shows that both electron–electron interactions at finite doping and an interlayer bias strongly modify the moiré bands. For small twists (
                    
                      
                        ≲
                      
                    
                    5°) the density of states versus filling and interlayer bias displays qualitatively different behavior for twisting near aligned (0°) and antialigned (60°) stacking with tunable Van Hove singularities (VHSs). Moreover, interactions pin the VHS to the Fermi energy over a finite range of doping both at zero and finite bias depending on the stacking type, an effect known to enhance both superconductivity and strongly correlated states. At half-filling, we obtain the phase diagram as a function of interaction strength, interlayer bias, and twist angle. We find a competition driven by band mixing between an isotropic ferromagnet and an antiferromagnet that are nearly degenerate over a wide range of experimentally accessible parameters. Our work demonstrates that correlated states in M-valley twisted TMD homobilayers can be strongly tuned in situ both by applying an electric displacement field and by electron doping.

title: Compound heterozygosity for I692del and V726A variants in MEFV leads to severe autoinflammation and elevated interleukin-18 (CHIVE-18)
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We describe a severe
                    MEFV
                    -associated autoinflammatory disease, distinct from familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), and designate it CHIVE-18 syndrome (Compound Heterozygosity for I692del and V726A
                    MEFV
                    variants and Elevated IL-18). We present the clinical features and inflammatory signatures of 44 CHIVE-18 patients and 9 other patients with two
                    MEFV
                    variants including I692del. Clinical findings in CHIVE-18 patients often include transfusion-dependent anemia, arthritis, organomegaly, inflammatory bowel disease, failure to thrive, and less frequently cytokine storm, Amyloid A (AA) amyloidosis, and neutrophilic dermatoses. Serum total and free IL-18 levels in CHIVE-18 patients were markedly elevated compared to those of healthy controls, classical FMF patients, and compound heterozygotes for I692del and a pathogenic
                    MEFV
                    variant other than V726A and were comparable to the previously described levels of patients with pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome. Cultured U937 cells expressing the V726A/I692del double mutant exhibited significantly increased release of IL-1β, IL-18, and lactate dehydrogenase compared to the other FMF-associated mutants. Patients’ myeloid cells showed enhanced STAT1 phosphorylation after stimulation with IFNγ. Despite having undetectable serum IL-1β, a previously reported CHIVE-18 patient with autoimmune hepatitis had in situ staining of a liver biopsy that showed high expression of IL-1β, TNFα, and IL-18, which localized to CD68+ tissue macrophages. CHIVE-18 patients usually require an IL-1 inhibitor and sometimes combination therapy with another biologic to control disease activity. In summary, CHIVE-18 is a distinct, severe disease that expands the spectrum of
                    MEFV
                    -associated autoinflammatory disorders and highlights genotype/phenotype complexity in compound heterozygous disorders.

title: Strategic coexistence theory for evolutionary games
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Evolutionary game theory and ecological coexistence theory both seek to predict the outcome of competition between biological entities, be they strategies or species, but the two fields have relied on largely separate approaches. Replicator equations provide a foundation for predicting the outcome of strategic competition, but comparing how different mechanisms alter competition across games remains challenging. Inspired by modern coexistence theory from community ecology, we develop Strategic Coexistence Theory (SCT), which translates payoff-based invasion conditions at monomorphic boundary conditions into strategic niche differences and fitness differences between any two competing strategies described by classic replicator dynamics. We show that SCT recovers the classic classification of two-strategy games and also allows us to compare mechanisms for the evolution of cooperation within a shared niche-fitness difference space. In stochastic games, environmental stochasticity increases both boundary invasion growth rates, whereas in multiplayer public-goods games, nonlinear benefits can either stabilize or destabilize competition. These applications also show that the number or stability of internal equilibria generally cannot be predicted from invasion growth rates at monomorphic boundaries, illustrating a key limitation of characterizing competitive systems using boundary invasion rates alone. Together, these results show that SCT provides a coexistence-theoretic perspective for characterizing how different mechanisms alter strategy competition across games.
